requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens every general start with the notification type question, and the prototype wins on the question itself; the INS front door hosts it because it is the only all-types dashboard (c-007, c-147). The templates ruling and the 9 October afternoon ruling block only the INS dashboard's summary information: the INS home's 'Create new' and the type question go ahead on today's INS home.

The older end-to-end traces show the earlier start, where the dashboard's create button posted to /live-animals/notifications and landed on the new notification's origin page with no type question (trace-e2e-p4-001, trace-animals-fit-p5-001).

requirements.statement: The notification type page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the heading 'What are you importing?' set as the radios' fieldset legend (h1), with the caption 'About the consignment' inside the heading.
requirements.why: The target design's copy for the page.

requirements.statement: The notification type question offers radio options in this order, with no hint text and none pre-selected on a new start: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products. Live animals continues to the animals frontend's live-animals start, which creates the GBN-AG draft with the live-animals category and lands on its origin page. Germinal products continues to the start of the germinal products set, the live-animals set's sibling in the animals frontend, which creates its own GBN-AG draft with the germinal products category and lands on that set's origin page; this option may land before the germinal products set itself is built. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products continue to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend, which creates a plants draft in that service's own reference format and lands on plants' own first page.
requirements.why: The target design's options and order, with each type sent to the real service or set that takes it: the real services split journeys by type, each creating its own draft and reference (c-007). The 9 October ruling offers Germinal products second and makes it start the germinal products set, each set passing its category when it creates the draft, and lets the link land ahead of the set. The templates ruling gives plants the same entry from the INS type question.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the question offers four options, Live animals, Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products, with no Germinal products option and no hints, each option already sent to its own service (repo-tests-p14-043, repo-tests-p14-044, repo-tests-p14-046, repo-tests-p14-095), so only the Germinal products option and its place second in the list are added.

requirements.statement: Returning to the notification type question from a notification's first page shows that notification's type already selected, and only that one. requirements.statement: The germinal products set's commodity search offers only germinal-product commodities, so it never offers a live-animal commodity.
requirements.why: Each set holds one category, so a consignment mixing live animals and germinal products is never written, and the germinal set's own pages and search are not blocked on MDM. Taking today's germinal lines out of the live-animals catalogue is not this programme's work: ruling 10 November puts that in the separate commodity-search ticket's hands, which req-1754 records.
requirements.deltaNote: There is no germinal set today and its search does not exist; the 12 germinal lines it offers are the ones the live-animals commodity catalogue holds (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026). Taking those lines out of the live-animals catalogue is the separate commodity-search ticket's work (req-1754).

requirements.statement: The germinal products catalogue holds the 12 specified germinal commodities, with embryos and ova as separate items: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); and '<Animal>, Semen' for Cattle (05111000), Cat, Dog, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rabbit/Rodent and Sheep (05119985): 18 items, sorted by name, codes shown with their leading zero. Each item offers the species listed under that animal (Cattle: Bison bison, Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis, plus Bovidae for semen; Horse: Equus asinus and Equus caballus; Goat: Capra hircus; Pig: Sus scrofa domesticus; Sheep: Ovis aries; Cat: Felis catus; Dog: Canis familiaris; Rabbit/Rodent semen: one row labelled Rabbit/Rodent). There are no poultry, fish or bee germinal products and no Cat or Dog embryos or ova.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a commodity catalogue's names, codes and species are reference-list content, which is MDM's and reaches the service through trade-imports-reference-data, never edited in code and never a reason to block a row (ruling:ian-2026-11-11 points 2 and 3). The germinal catalogue's content therefore leaves the backlog as an MDM concern, exactly as the live-animals catalogue's content already has (req-094 to req-101), and c-282 records the clause that had blocked it. What the data page still decides is which germinal commodities the germinal fields apply to, naming the same twelve entries in all five of its applicability lists, and that is carried by req-121, req-123, req-124 and req-251. Its Cat and Dog embryos and ova are mock data the 9 October ruling does not copy, and the data page gives them no fields (c-230). The page writes the codes without their leading zero and never says how they map to the codes a notification carries, which c-340 settles in favour of the eight-digit codes the catalogue and MDM use.

requirements.statement: Each live-animal species asks 'Number of animals' in a narrow numeric field with no hint; it is required ('Enter the number of animals') and must be a whole number of 1 or more ('Enter a whole number greater than 0'), each error linked to that species' field.
requirements.why: The number of animals is needed for every live-animal species: the data fields page makes it mandatory to proceed, entered by the trader. The page's own conditions cell is empty, so the floor of 1 and the whole-number rule are Design Release 2.1's and the real service's, not the specification's.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-037, -p10-038, -p10-041, -p10-043 and -p10-044 hold the label, the empty description, the required rule and both messages, and repo-tests-p1-075 and -p1-083 prove them end to end.

requirements.statement: 'Number of packages (when required)', hinted 'Such as crates, bags or boxes', is asked for a chosen species only where the data fields page's package-count list names its commodity. That list covers bees; birds of prey (owls, falcons and other); cats; cattle; dogs; embryos or ova of cattle, goats, horses, sheep and pigs; ferrets; game birds (adult and day-old partridge and pheasant, and pheasant and partridge hatching eggs); goats; horses and donkeys; insects and other invertebrates, including the Asian hornet; domestic pigs and pig meat under safeguard measure; poultry (adult and day-old chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys and guinea fowl, and chicken, turkey, goose, duck and guinea fowl hatching eggs); psittaciformes, including parrots, parakeets, macaws and cockatoos; domestic European rabbits and other domestic rabbits; reptiles; rodents; semen of cattle, dogs or cats, horses, goats, pigs, rodents or rabbits and sheep; domestic sheep; and SPF eggs. A species whose commodity is not on that list is asked only for the number of animals.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals data fields page is the specification for which commodity codes each conditional rule covers, and it outranks Design Release 2.1's demo commodity data on that; Design Release 2.1 still gives the field its label and its hint. A reference list is never a reason to block a row (ruling 11 November), so the question's coverage is not held back by the commodity list's content.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the question is shown for the commodity codes the frontend's own applicability rules name, read from its commodity service rather than from the specification's list, and a code they do not cover is asked for the number of animals alone (repo-frontend-p10-039, -p10-040, -p10-060); Design Release 2.1 withholds the question from poultry, rabbits, parrots, reptiles, bees and ornamental fish, and the specification names all of those but ornamental fish. Nothing in the end-to-end suite yet asserts the hint or the field's coverage (repo-tests-p1-089).

requirements.statement: For live animals the number of packages is optional, but when given must be a whole number of 1 or more, otherwise 'Number of packages must be a whole number, like 5'.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-042 takes no required message for the field, and -p10-047 and -p10-047-m1 refuse a non-whole number and anything below one with the same message, which repo-tests-p1-083 proves end to end.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-054 to -p10-059 hold the message, its singular forms, the rule's conditions, the link to the species' identification card and the walk that removes a record and carries on.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', before Number of packages, for every germinal commodity in the catalogue. It is optional: left blank, no error is shown, and the trader enters the figure.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 measures germinal products by weight and asks it on every germinal species block; V4 makes the total gross weight in kilograms an optional numeric field the trader supplies, with the example 24.50, and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only. V4's weight row is the one germinal row with no 'Applicable to' list, so it never says which germinal commodity codes the field is asked for (confluence-6497338582-p5-012); as the germinal set holds only germinal commodities and the other five germinal fields apply to all twelve entries, it is asked on every germinal species block, as Design Release 2.1 does.

requirements.statement: The germinal set stores each species line's 'Total gross weight' answer as that line's gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal, and shows it back in the service; it is not published on GBN-AG, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no gross weight.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks, errors and reviews the answer as 'Total gross weight', and what the real record stores is persistence, so the prototype's internal netWeight key does not decide the quantity. The ruling publishes only what v0.2.0 already carries.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each commodity complement and species line records only whole-number animal and package counts, with no gross weight (repo-backend-p1-039, p1-040, p1-043, p1-044, cited in the backend's own area). The line's quantity stays its number of packages (c-234); only the gross weight is a decimal.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block asks 'Number of packages', with no hint and no '(when required)', after Total gross weight, and the trader enters the count; germinal species are not asked the number of animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products by package, not by head. V4 holds the germinal quantity on each commodity line and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only; its quantity row is the other germinal row with no 'Applicable to' list, so it never says which germinal commodity codes it is asked for, and as the set holds only germinal commodities it is asked on every species block.

requirements.statement: The germinal set's Commodity details page always asks one 'Temperature' radio question, its legend styled at label size (not a heading), with the hint 'How will the products be stored' and the options Ambient, Chilled and Frozen in that order, after all commodity blocks. requirements.statement: A germinal products notification is started by the germinal set's own start (reached from the type question's Germinal products option or from 'Create new' on the germinal set's own notification list at /germinal-products), which creates the draft and skips the notification type question. requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-010-m1 and trace-animals-fit-p12-061 show the Draft strip; trace-animals-fit-p7-059 shows the error summary above the caption.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set the main import reason is one radio choice of five reasons, in this order: Internal market; Transhipment or onward travel; Transit; Re-entry; Temporary admission horses. The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, only one reason is held, no reason is pre-selected on a notification without one, and the list is the same for every live-animal commodity. The germinal-products set's own copy of the page carries its own two-reason list of Internal market and Transit.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service all offer the same five reasons in the same order, as a single-select answer at notification level, and the policy page names which of them the germinals journey offers. The 9 October ruling puts germinal products in a sibling set with its own catalogue, so the reduced list belongs to that set's copy of the page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-065 and repo-frontend-p8-071 show the five reasons in the service's order today, and repo-tests-p1-059 shows none pre-selected. The radio labels come from the shared import-reason-purpose service rather than the page's own copy file (repo-frontend-p8-072), so that is where a label changes. The policy page marks the reason field block 'At least one' while the field itself is a single-select enumeration and no field records a second reason (confluence-6497338582-p3-006): the single-select reading is what both the prototype and the real service build, so one reason is held.

requirements.statement: Each reason carries its hint: Internal market 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'; Transhipment or onward travel 'For animals intended for direct travel to a third country, that will stay only within the same port or airport in Great Britain while moving to another means of transport.'; Transit 'For animals moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'; Re-entry 'For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.'; Temporary admission horses 'For horses authorised for temporary entry.'
requirements.why: The five hints are word for word the same in the target design and the real service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-066 to repo-frontend-p8-070 hold the same five hints today, in the page's own copy file.

requirements.statement: A main import reason is optional to proceed: Save and continue with no reason chosen shows no error and moves on.
requirements.why: The policy page makes the reason mandatory to submit but lets the trader move past the page without it, the target design makes it optional to proceed, and the real service already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-109 shows the reason itself is not a required answer on the page, and repo-tests-p1-071 shows a seeded draft left with no reason. No fit or page test submits the page with nothing chosen (repo-frontend-p8-109, trace-animals-fit-p7-076), so a test should pin it.

requirements.statement: Each reason that needs follow-up questions opens them in a standard GOV.UK conditional reveal directly under its own radio, so the reason and its follow-ups are answered in one submit; Re-entry has no reveal and saves on its own; every reveal is hidden until its reason is chosen. Without JavaScript every reveal shows open and the page still works, because only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved.
requirements.why: The target design asks the follow-ups as reveals on the reason page; the real service moved them there in DR1 parity (inc-067), so it already matches. The policy page names no extra field for Re-entry. The 9 October afternoon ruling requires every page to work fully without JavaScript, which GOV.UK's conditional reveal already gives.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-091 shows no follow-up shown until a reason that needs one is chosen and the Re-entry radio controlling nothing, repo-frontend-p8-090 shows Re-entry saving alone, and repo-frontend-p8-120 shows the page working without JavaScript.

requirements.statement: Choosing Internal market reveals the radio question 'Purpose in the internal market' (medium legend) with eleven options, in this order: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift; Transfer of ownership - Rescue; Breeding; Research; Racing, competition, show or training; Approved premises or body; Companion animal not for resale or rehoming; Production; Slaughter; Fattening; Restocking. The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, no purpose is pre-selected when the reveal first opens, and in the live-animals set all eleven are offered for every commodity. The germinal-products set's own copy of the reveal offers four: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift, Breeding, Research and Production.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service ask the same purpose question with the same eleven options in the same order for live animals, as a single-select answer at notification level, and the policy page names which four the germinals journey offers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-073 and repo-frontend-p8-074 show the legend and the eleven purposes today, and repo-tests-p1-061 shows none pre-selected when the reveal first opens. The purpose labels come from the shared import-reason-purpose service rather than the page's copy file (repo-frontend-p8-086).

requirements.statement: Each of the eleven internal market purposes carries its own hint beneath its label: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift describes any movement aimed at sale or transfer of ownership, including gifts; Transfer of ownership - Rescue rehoming, adoption or fostering; Breeding reproduction and breeding programmes; Research 'Animals for use in scientific or medical research.'; Racing, competition, show or training 'Animals to participate in competitive or training events.'; Approved premises or body 'Animals for exhibition, zoos, collections, or conservation programmes where a licence or approval is needed.'; Companion animal not for resale or rehoming privately owned animals that cannot meet the non-commercial rules; Production 'Animals that are farmed for the production of meat, milk, eggs, wool or any other animal product or by-product.'; Slaughter 'Animals to be slaughtered and processed for meat production shortly after arrival into Great Britain.'; Fattening 'Animals to be fattened for meat production.'; Restocking 'To replenish or enhance populations of species, for example, restocking of game or fish.'

It also rules that list content is MDM's to own, not the prototype's.

It also rules that the duplicate and misspelt ports are MDM's real data.

requirements.statement: The exit date is one text field using the MOJ date picker, labelled 'Exit date' with a 'Choose date' calendar (Monday-first weeks, picking a day fills the field as day/month/year); the open calendar never covers the question below it, surrounding spaces are trimmed before the date is read, no earliest or latest date is set, and a date chosen from the calendar is saved and offered back in the field.

The MoJ date picker is one of the components the 9 October afternoon ruling accepts, the interaction designer confirms it as the picker every other date in both frontends uses, and design question 12 covers only the germinal dates read from a document, so the exit date keeps its calendar.

requirements.statement: Only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved; changing the reason removes the earlier reason's answers that the new one does not ask, so returning to Internal market after switching away offers no purpose and asks for it again.
requirements.why: The target design clears follow-up answers that belong to reasons no longer chosen, and the real service already purges them on save.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-099 shows only the chosen reason's questions checked and saved, and repo-frontend-p8-112 the purge when the reason changes.

requirements.statement: The notification holds one destination country, one port of exit and one exit date answer, each reached through its own form field per reveal, and every reveal that asks for it is prefilled from the saved answer, so a Transit country is still offered under Transhipment.
requirements.why: The target design names a separate field per reveal, but DR1 judged that the per-branch names are a DOM artefact, not extra questions, and that carrying a shared answer between reveals is not a requirement (inc-067); that judgement on the same difference stands. The policy page holds the answers at notification level.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-111 shows the destination country, the port of exit and the exit date each held as one answer whatever reason asked for them, and trace-e2e-p4-117 shows them prefilled in every reveal.

requirements.statement: The reason, internal market purpose, certification purpose and unweaned answers are stored as the service's codes (for example internalMarket, breeding, further-keeping, yes), not as their displayed labels.
requirements.why: Stored values are a persistence contract with the backend and other services that the prototype, which stores labels, cannot express; the ruling lets that constraint override the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-070 shows the reasons answered as internalMarket, transit and temporaryAdmissionHorses, repo-tests-p1-178 the unweaned answer posted as yes or no, and trace-animals-fit-p12-007 the kebab-case certification codes.

requirements.statement: A submitted reason, certification purpose or unweaned value that is not one of the offered options is refused with 'Select a valid option', linking to and focusing the group's first radio, with no option left checked and the other question's valid answer kept; a refused submit writes nothing to the notification.
requirements.why: Server-side validation that refuses tampered values and never saves a refused submit is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (it silently drops or stores them), so it overrides the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-108, repo-frontend-p8-134 and repo-frontend-p8-135 show the refusal, the focus move, no option left checked and the other answer kept; trace-animals-fit-p12-027 and trace-animals-fit-p7-060 give the message's words, and trace-e2e-p4-115-m1 shows nothing written on a refused submit.

requirements.statement: When either page is refused on submit, the browser title is prefixed 'Error: ' and the page is answered with HTTP 400; each inline message carries a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix.
requirements.why: The 'Error: ' title prefix is how GOV.UK tells screen-reader users a validation error has happened; the prototype's title omits it, but accessible validation is a real constraint the prototype does not express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-119 and repo-frontend-p8-142 show the bad-request status on both pages, and trace-animals-fit-p7-059 and trace-animals-fit-p12-029 the 'Error: ' prefix.

requirements.statement: When a saved destination country, port of exit or certification purpose is no longer in the reference list, reopening the page says so ('The saved destination country is no longer available. Select a country from the list.', 'The saved port of exit is no longer available. Select a port from the list.', 'The certification purpose you chose is no longer offered. Select a purpose from the list.') and blanks it in every reveal that asks for it; a saved purpose or exit date is not re-checked this way.
requirements.why: A saved answer going stale against reference data is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real service keeps handling it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-106 and repo-frontend-p8-136 hold the three messages, repo-frontend-p8-112-m1 the blanking in every reveal and repo-frontend-p8-107 that only the country and port answers are re-checked; no fit test exercises any of them (repo-frontend-p8-148).

requirements.statement: If saving either page fails, the page is shown again with the user's entries and the shared recoverable-error message, with HTTP 500.
requirements.why: A failed save is a persistence condition the prototype cannot express; the real service already recovers from it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-119 and repo-frontend-p8-142 show a failed save showing the page again in a recoverable-error state with a server-error status.

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' on the main import reason page makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue', and differs only in where it goes when every answer passes: the notification overview rather than the next journey page. A missing or invalid follow-up answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one, the chosen reason still checked, its reveal open and the entries shown again. When amending, the 'Save and return' (review) action makes the same checks and goes to the review page.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling, which outranks every other source, makes Save and return to overview run exactly the checks Save and continue runs, with an error for each missing or invalid answer and the trader kept on the page, and says no page is an exception; it replaces the earlier soft save recorded in c-211 and its plants counterpart c-313. The germinal-products set's copy of this page is a sibling set in the same frontend with the same two buttons, so it takes the same rule even though the ruling names only live animals and high-risk plants (ruling claim 24).

The 26 October ruling recorded that the button once skipped those checks (ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-001), and no fit or E2E trace in this area exercises it (trace-animals-fit-p7-079).

The target design's template editing of this page is set aside with them.

requirements.statement: The additional details page asks 'What are the animals certified for?' (medium legend) as radios with sixteen options and no hints, in this order: Further keeping; Slaughter; Confined establishment; Germinal products; Registered equine animal; Travelling circus/animal act; Exhibition; Event or activity near borders; Release into the wild; Dispatch centre; Relaying area / purification centre; Ornamental aquaculture establishment; Technical use; Quarantine or similar establishment; Live aquatic animals for human consumption; Other. requirements.blockedBy: Parked as concept work by ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2, and the 13 November design ruling leaves the search-only layout deferred with it. When it is planned it needs design's answer to question 10 (whether the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible will do) and the INS address lookup as a real feature. Transporter management no longer blocks it.

requirements.statement: A saved transporter is recorded with its type Private or Commercial and status New; a commercial one carries its entered authorisation number as its approval number and an address ending in Northern Ireland; its separate details (name, address lines, town, county, postcode, country, email, phone) are kept; and it joins the organisation's transporters.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on what a new transporter's record holds.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-084 and -086 record the private and commercial records with their separate details, repo-frontend-p13-087 records the type, and repo-frontend-p13-088 creates the record in the organisation's address book.

requirements.statement: Both add forms' Back links go to 'Choose a transporter type', and a saved form shows its values again when reopened.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-014 and -015 return each Back link to the type question carrying the trail, and repo-frontend-p13-103 and -104 show every saved value back in the form when it is reopened.

requirements.statement: When adding a transporter was started from the address book, the 'Choose a transporter type' Back link goes to the address book's 'Choose an address type' question.
requirements.why: The add pages are the address book's, reached from its own address type question as well as from the journey.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p15-008 proves the Back link returning to the address book's address type question, and repo-tests-p15-001 that choosing Transporter there opens the type question.

requirements.statement: When adding a transporter was started from the address book, both add forms' cancel button reads 'Cancel and return to address book' and goes to the address book filtered to transporters, storing no transporter.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns a trader who cancels to where they started.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p15-024 and -025 prove the label and the landing, and repo-tests-p2-105 records that the animals journey's forms do not use it, which is right because they cancel to the dashboard (req-440).

requirements.statement: When adding a transporter was started from the address book, saving adds it to the organisation's transporters in the address book, shows the address book's success banner naming it, and goes to the address book filtered to transporters, where it is listed with its type, address and approval number and found by a search on its name, type, address, approval number or country.
requirements.why: A transporter added from the address book should be there straight away, and the address book is the system of record for transporters.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p15-026 and -027 land the trader on the address book filtered to transporters under a success banner naming the record, and repo-tests-p15-029, -031, -039, -040, -042 and -043 prove the listing and the search.

requirements.statement: Transporters a trader adds belong to the organisation, not the user or the session: each saved transporter is its own record in the organisation's address book, it appears on every later notification's transporter list without being pre-chosen there, and another organisation's address book holds none of them.
requirements.why: A real persistence and authorisation constraint the prototype cannot express: its added transporters live only in one session. Nothing merges two transporters that share a name: the type page's warning is the service's only guard against a duplicate (req-416).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-088 creates the record in the organisation's address book, repo-frontend-p12-029 offers only the organisation's transporters, repo-frontend-p13-089 and repo-tests-p7-110 show it on the next notification, trace-animals-fit-p20-061 leaves it unselected there, and repo-tests-p15-030 scopes it to the organisation that saved it.

requirements.statement: Transporters a trader adds are held by the address book service, so they survive a restart and every instance of a frontend offers the same list, and reference data serves no transporters list for any page to read.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling makes the address book the system of record for transporters, so what a trader adds is real persistence rather than the demo-grade capture the animals frontend's in-memory store gave, and the requirement that added transporters stay on the list for later notifications is met for real.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-088 already saves every added transporter as a record in the organisation's address book and repo-tests-p15-052 proves the address book holds it, so the durable store the rulings require is in place; repo-referencedata-p1-091 confirms reference data serves no transporters list.

requirements.statement: If saving on a transporter page fails in a recoverable way, the page is shown again with a recoverable-error message, the trader's entries and search term kept and HTTP status 500, and no success banner follows.
requirements.why: A real persistence and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-055 re-renders the list with the pick and term kept and repo-frontend-p13-102 the add form with its values kept and the just-added name cleared.

requirements.statement: Every transporter form posts a cross-site request token and a concurrency token and sets novalidate, so validation is the server's.
requirements.why: Real persistence and security constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-054 and repo-frontend-p13-057 carry both tokens on every submission and turn the browser's own validation off.

requirements.statement: The transporter pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and classes, with email and phone inputs of type email and tel, their autocomplete attributes and the GOV.UK width utilities, the one exception being the radios-in-a-table list that Design Release 2.1 also uses.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-033 to -035 set the autofill hints, the input widths and the email and tel types, and trace-animals-fit-p18-108 and -p21-051 show govuk-* classes throughout.

requirements.statement: The transporter pages copy the prototype's custom caption, heading, section-heading and input-width classes, its custom address-search widget styling and its plain text inputs for email and phone.
requirements.why: Out of scope: these are the prototype's implementation, not its design; the real service draws the same look from GOV.UK Frontend and keeps the email and tel input types that help users on mobile.

requirements.statement: Every transporter page, in its first, searched, no-match and error states, has no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA rules.
requirements.why: The service must meet WCAG 2.2 AA; today's suites already hold most states to it, but not every one.

requirements.statement: Errors raised on 'Choose a transporter type' stay in the session and show on the transporter list after the trader goes back.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a defect in the prototype, where the list page does not clear stored errors; not a design decision.

requirements.statement: The service has no approved commercial transporter register page: nothing serves /transporters/select or 'Search for an approved commercial transporter', and no test drives it.

requirements.statement: A blank document reference, after surrounding spaces are trimmed, shows 'Enter a document reference' in the error summary and above the field, and the summary link moves focus to the field.
requirements.why: The design and the real page agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-039 and repo-frontend-p17-112 trim and require the reference with the same message today.

requirements.statement: A document reference longer than 58 characters shows 'Document reference must be 58 characters or fewer', and the over-long value stays in the field.
requirements.why: The prototype sets no length limit on the page, but the V4 data fields page specifies a reference of at most 58 characters and a stored reference needs a limit: policy and a real validation constraint the prototype cannot express, so the limit stays.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-040 enforces 58 characters today, from the document-uploads claim contract; the backend allows up to 100 (repo-backend-p4-006), so the frontend limit is the one a trader meets.

requirements.statement: A document reference may contain letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, full stops and forward slashes, so a reference such as 'ITAHC-001', an air waybill's '125-12345675' or a TRACES certificate's 'CHEDA.GB.2026.1234567' is accepted all the way through to the stored record.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 accepts any non-blank reference, and the V4 data fields page sets no format or pattern for it, giving its example as GBHC1234567890. Nothing in the evidence shows a downstream system needs a letters-and-digits rule.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals frontend already accepts those characters (repo-frontend-p17-041), but the backend's document-upload request still refuses any reference that is not letters and digits (repo-backend-p4-007, overruled), so a reference the page accepts can still be turned away by the service. The k6 suite's references (PERFDOC<vu>V<iteration>N<n>, repo-perftests-p1-037-m1) are letters and digits, so they keep passing once the rule is relaxed.

requirements.statement: The second field is a select labelled 'Document type' with no hint, opening on a 'Select one' placeholder with no value; the trader chooses the type on the page and the filename is never used to guess it.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-022 and repo-tests-p5-007 show the select with its placeholder today.

requirements.statement: The Document type select offers thirteen types, in this order: ITAHC (Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate); Other veterinary certificate / veterinary declaration; Self-declaration; Journey log; Import permit / authorisation; CITES permit/certificate; Air waybill; Sea waybill; Rail waybill; Bill of lading; Commercial invoice; Packing list / species list; Other supporting documents.
requirements.why: The V4 data fields page is the specification for which document types a notification may carry, and its list was replaced with one the business supplied on 29 October 2026; it outranks the prototype's demo data on the permitted values (c-348), while how each option reads stays the business's and Design Release 2.1's as c-349 settles. Sam's ruling on data makes V4 the source of truth, so no row rests on the prototype's app/data list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-023, repo-frontend-p17-024 and repo-tests-p5-008 show exactly these thirteen types in this order today. The traces captured before that change show fourteen types in a different order, including Letter of authority (Directive 2008/61/EC), Catch certificate, Laboratory sampling results for aflatoxin (Reg 2019/1793) and Health certificate (trace-animals-fit-p22-017, trace-e2e-p12-016). The document types list is not served by reference-data (repo-referencedata-p1-092).

requirements.statement: The document type is submitted, stored and published by its code (for example ITAHC, VETERINARY_HEALTH_CERTIFICATE), not by the prototype's slugs. The trader never sees the code.
requirements.why: The code is what the backend stores and what the outbound GBN-AG event carries: a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-083 and repo-tests-p5-058 show the type sent and stored by its code today.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Other supporting documents' as the document type asks for no further description.

That ruling sends the calendar on the germinal dates to design (design question 12) because MoJ advises against its picker for dates read from a document, but it names only those germinal dates and says the documents theme stands as distilled, so this existing picker, which enhances a typed text input that works without JavaScript, stays.

requirements.statement: A file may be up to 50MB, counted as 50,000,000 bytes: the size bullet says 50MB, the browser and server checks both allow it, and a larger file shows 'The selected file must be smaller than 50MB'. requirements.statement: Every file is really virus scanned. A file the scan rejects shows a red tag naming the reason, 'Virus found', 'Upload failed' or 'Download failed', and the plain 'Rejected' where the upload service gave a reason the page has no wording for; the row has no View file link, and '<filename> cannot be used. Remove it and try again with a different file.' shows in the error summary, linked to the documents table, on every view until the document is removed, with 'The file' standing in where the filename is not known. Save and continue holds while a rejected document is listed. A status the service cannot recognise shows a grey 'Unknown' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 simulates a scan that always passes, so it has no failure state. A real scan can find a virus or fail: a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real failure handling and its own wording stay.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-064, repo-frontend-p18-042 and repo-tests-p5-037 show the reason-named tags and the per-file error today. requirements.statement: While a document is scanning, the page updates its status without the trader acting: with JavaScript it polls a JSON status endpoint under the page's own address every 3 seconds up to 10 times, re-reading every document's status each time, updates settled rows in place with their View file link, announces the settled state once in a polite live region, and reopens the page from the server once every scan settles; without JavaScript a 'Refresh virus scan status' link re-reads the status and carries the attempt count; after 10 attempts the hint 'Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment.' shows.
requirements.why: A real scan takes time; the trader needs to see it finish. Design Release 2.1 fakes this with a timed call, which the real scan replaces. The polling is the real service's own enhancement, not script written to copy the prototype, and the refresh link means nothing the trader needs is shown only by script, as Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling requires.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p18-017 to repo-frontend-p18-037 and trace-e2e-p12-048 show the polling, the announcements and the no-JavaScript refresh link today. The announcements read 'Document scan complete: the file is safe to use' and, for a rejection, 'Document check failed: the file contains a virus. Remove it and try again.' and its upload and download counterparts (repo-frontend-p18-028 to repo-frontend-p18-032); the trace captured before that wording change reads 'Document scan failed: a virus was found. Remove the file and try again.' (trace-animals-fit-p23-031).

requirements.statement: A document that scanned clean has a 'View file' link (hidden text 'for document N') that downloads the stored file byte for byte through the service, with the file's own content type only when it is an accepted type, otherwise as plain bytes, and with nosniff and the service's other security headers; a pending or rejected file has no link, and another notification's upload is answered 404.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never stores a file, so it cannot show one; storing and serving the real file is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and the trader needs to check what they attached.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-068, repo-frontend-p17-082 and repo-tests-p5-056 offer and serve View file for clean documents today.

requirements.statement: Each row has a 'Remove' button styled as a link, usable while the document is still scanning; it removes the document straight away with no confirmation, warning or undo, deletes its upload, discards anything typed in the form and reloads the page. requirements.statement: Uploading a document is optional: with none of the document details entered, Save and continue and Save and return to overview both leave the page with no error. requirements.statement: The file goes from the browser to the frontend, which sends it through the backend to cdp-uploader for virus scanning and storage in the documents S3 bucket; cdp-uploader reports the result to the backend's scan-result callback, matched by correlation id, and a document becomes COMPLETE only when no file was rejected (fail closed). A failure to reach or use the uploader shows 'The selected file could not be uploaded. Try again.', and a failure to reach it at all shows the service's general recoverable-error banner with the fields the trader posted shown back. In CDP the scan is the real cdp-uploader; on the local stack it is the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan.
requirements.why: This is the real upload handshake behind the page; Design Release 2.1 sends only the filename and cannot express it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-003, repo-backend-p4-018 and repo-backend-p4-063 show the proxied cdp-uploader flow working end to end today, and repo-frontend-p17-051 and repo-frontend-p17-105-m1 give the wording a trader sees when it fails.

requirements.statement: Documents can be added, listed and removed whatever the notification's status, draft, submitted or in amendment; they are deleted with their notification; and only documents that scanned clean are referenced in the events the backend publishes.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-078, repo-backend-p4-079 and repo-backend-p4-080 hold these rules today, over the four notification statuses repo-tests-p5-062 names.

requirements.statement: Where at least one animal on the notification needs a permanent address, the consignment addresses page shows a 'Permanent address' section headed 'Permanent address' with the hint 'A permanent address is where an animal:' and the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address'; no other consignment shows it. Once every such animal has one and a single address covers them all, the section shows that address's name and lines in its inset with a 'Change' link; where several different permanent addresses have been given it shows 'Permanent addresses added for N animals' instead; and while any such animal still owes one it shows no inset at all.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the permanent address among the consignment's addresses for pets, and the real page has to say something sensible when several animals have different addresses.

requirements.statement: Pressing a same-as button submits the consignment addresses page's own form, saves on the notification a copy of the source party's record as the target party, and reloads the page with no success banner, showing the copied address with a 'Change' link and no same-as button. The copy is independent: changing the source party later does not change it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 fills the section in place with no picker; the real service must persist the copy on the notification like any other pick, and the sections have to sit inside its form for the button to submit it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-044 to repo-frontend-p14-047 show the page's own form posting the same-as action, the copy being saved and the target then shown like any other chosen party, and repo-tests-p7-083, -p7-086 and -p7-087 prove the fill and its independence end to end.

requirements.statement: On the consignment addresses page, 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' make exactly the same checks: neither shows an error for a section that is still empty, and each keeps what the trader entered. Completeness shows only in the task status.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real page both let the trader move on with sections still empty, and the owner's 26 October ruling makes 'Save and return to overview' check exactly what 'Save and continue' checks, on every page carrying both buttons in live animals and in high-risk plants, with no page an exception. That ruling names only those two, so the germinal-products copy of this page follows the live-animals page under the sibling-set ruling.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-106 shows the page enforcing no validation, whichever button is pressed, and repo-frontend-p14-013 shows both buttons saving nothing and moving on. ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-001 names upload documents, origin and main reason for import as the pages where the two buttons differ today; this page is not one of them.

requirements.statement: On a new notification's opening run through the journey, 'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page goes on to the contact address for this consignment page, or to check your answers when no later page applies. Opened from its overview task, the page returns to the overview; under check-your-answers change context it returns to check your answers.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 takes the trader on to the next step of the journey, the contact address, rather than to the CPH number, which it reaches only from the page's own CPH section. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 confirms that a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview.

Before it landed the opening run went on to the CPH number page (trace-animals-fit-p14-075).

It is its own waiting-on-design increment, built as design answers or dropped if design drops it.

Before it, Design Release 2.1 narrowed the list as the trader typed and DR1 judged a live filter worth porting, but ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm held filtering as you type until design answered.

requirements.statement: Submitting a party picker's search, or opening it with a search in the address, narrows the list on the server to matching addresses and keeps the text in the box; an empty search shows the whole list again, and a submitted search opens the first page of results.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the existing server-side search must stay as the fallback for traders without JavaScript, and the prototype also filters on the server when given a search.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-040 and -p7-045 show the animals picker searching on the server within its own role and keeping the term through paging, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-015 to -p9-019 show plants passing the term to the address book, opening the first page and restoring the whole list on an empty search.

requirements.statement: Each of the five party pickers, place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination, in both animals sets, and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, shows eight a page of the addresses it found, its whole list or the matches when a search narrows it, with GOV.UK pagination under the results where more than eight were found and none where eight or fewer were. The page links carry the search term, the page, the address held as chosen and the trail the trader arrived on; a submitted search starts again at the first page; a page past the last page serves the last page and one that is not a page number serves the first, each logged once. A picker offers no sorting, no filter beyond its search box, no tabs and no control over the page size.
requirements.why: Eight a page is the figure the INS address book list already uses over the same records, and a trader with many addresses for one role needs the list broken up. Ruling ian-2026-11-23 drops the one-page clause this requirement used to carry, and ruling ian-2026-11-25 keeps that drop, so every picker in both journeys pages at one figure. The contact address pages are not party pickers and page at the same figure in their own rows: req-2312 and req-2313 for the animals sets, req-1965 for plants.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-044 to -p7-046 show the animals pickers at eight a page with pagination from the ninth match, the search term and the chosen address kept across pages, after EUDPA-827 landed on the animals frontend's main (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-027, -p1-029). repo-plantsfrontend-p9-049 to -p9-058 and -p9-089, -p9-090 show the shared plants picker, which its consignor and place of destination pickers use, cutting pages of eight, showing pagination only past one page, carrying the search, the choice and the trail on every link, and logging a page past the last or not a page number once each; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-096 shows no sort, extra filter, tab or page-size control. repo-plantsfrontend-p14-067, -p14-073 and -p14-074 show a plants picker opening on the first eight addresses, paging the rest and dropping the paging once a search narrows the list onto one page.

requirements.statement: Every party picker, the five in both animals sets and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, shows a 'Selected address: <name>' inset between the search box and the results, naming the address the picker holds as chosen, on every page and after a search; the inset shows only while that address is still a live address-book record the picker offers.
requirements.why: The inset exists because the chosen row can be on another page, which paging at eight makes true again. Without it a trader on page two has nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen. Ruling ian-2026-11-23 restores it in both frontends with the words they already had, and ruling ian-2026-11-25 keeps that restoration. The contact address pages restate the chosen address in their own rows: req-2313 for the animals sets, req-1965 for plants.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-042 and -p7-045 show the animals picker naming the chosen address between the Search button and the results heading and keeping it on page two, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-022 and -p9-023 show the same inset in plants, shown only while the held id still resolves to a live record the picker offers. repo-plantsfrontend-p14-078 shows a returning trader seeing 'Selected address: <name>' above the results in plants.

requirements.statement: Every party picker's address table sits inside one fieldset whose legend, visually hidden, reads the results heading, so the radios are announced as one choice; when a selection is refused the form group around the results takes the GOV.UK error state and the fieldset is described by the error message.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-039 to -p9-043 and -p9-091 show the five columns, their names in both languages and the small radio labelled 'Select <name>', and repo-tests-p7-051 and -p2-113 prove the animals rows the same way.

requirements.statement: Every party picker's Address column shows each street line on its own line, with the town or city, county and postcode together on the line below, and leaves out any part the record does not hold; the country sits in its own column.
