requirements.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' on a party picker with no address chosen shows no error, leaves the party as it was — empty, or holding its earlier address as the trader edited it — and moves the trader on as a valid save would, an animals picker to the consignment addresses page and a plants picker to the next page of its journey or to the overview. The save is logged once as committing nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader leave a picker without choosing; completeness is checked by the task status and the review, not by the picker. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' pickers the same lenient blank save, and the owner's 26 October ruling makes plants' 'Save and return to overview' check exactly what its 'Save and continue' checks, so both of its buttons are lenient.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-050 shows an animals picker saved with nothing ticked returning to the consignment addresses page with that party still offering only its add link, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-065, -p9-066, -p7-080, -p7-081 and -p7-099 show plants committing nothing, raising no error, leaving an edited copy untouched and logging the save once. Before it landed both frontends re-rendered the picker with status 400 and 'Select a <party> from the list' (trace-animals-fit-p14-050 to -054).

requirements.statement: Saving a picker with an address that is not in the organisation's book, has been deleted since the page loaded, or is not offered for that picker's role saves nothing and re-renders the picker with status 400, an error summary 'There is a problem' and the picker's own error: 'Select a place of origin from the list', 'Select a consignor from the list', 'Select a consignee from the list', 'Select an importer from the list', 'Select a place of destination from the list' or 'Select a contact address from the list' and their Welsh, shown above the results with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, the summary link going to the first address radio or, with no rows, to the search box. The ticked row is cleared, the search term and its results stay, and the refusal is logged with the address id and the reason.
requirements.why: A real constraint the prototype cannot express: the notification must never hold a party copied from a record the organisation does not have, or does not have for that role.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-028 holds the five animals errors and repo-frontend-p14-095 treats a deleted or wrongly-roled record as never chosen; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-067 to -p9-072 show plants refusing such an id at status 400 with its own message, clearing the tick, keeping the search and logging the reason, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-037 shows the summary link going to the first row or to the search box.

requirements.statement: Outside an amendment, each of the five animals party pickers and the CPH number page end with a single primary 'Save and continue' button, with no 'Save and return to overview' button and no cancel link. While amending, each ends with the amendment's own save and return controls.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled this same difference (rule (b)): only pages the overview links to end with the three return controls, and a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone; the animals pickers are reached from the consignment addresses page. The amendment's endings are req-1624's, in the journey-flow area.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p9-045 and trace-animals-fit-p15-030 show the animals pickers ending with 'Save and continue' alone today, and document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-057 records the CPH number page built the same way under DR1 rule (b). The permanent address page follows the same rule (req-748).

requirements.statement: Choosing an address on an animals picker and pressing 'Save and continue' saves on the notification a copy of that record — the record it came from, its name, telephone number, email address and address — and returns to the consignment addresses page, or to check your answers under change context. The page names each party from that copy, never from the address book, so renaming, moving or deleting the record afterwards leaves the notification, its review, its submitted view and its amendment as they were.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real service both save the chosen address against the party and return to the page; the copy keeps the notification stable when the book changes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-052 shows every party answer stored as a copy taken when it was chosen rather than a live reference, repo-frontend-p14-030 the return to the consignment addresses page, and repo-tests-p7-073, -p7-075, -p7-097 and -p7-100 that a later rename or deletion leaves the draft, the review, the submitted view and the amendment unchanged.

requirements.statement: If saving a picked address fails because the backend is briefly unavailable, the picker re-renders with status 500, the recoverable-error message, the trader's choice still ticked, their search term still in the box and the page of results they were on, and the failure is logged once.
requirements.why: A real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: the trader must not lose their choice when the save fails.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-079 shows the picker shown again at status 500 with the recoverable-error banner and the choice still ticked, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-005-m1 that the page of results is honoured, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-080 that a programming failure is raised instead.

requirements.statement: Each party picker, on both animals sets and in the high-risk plants frontend, offers only the organisation's addresses whose roles include that party's role: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination. Its search looks only within that role, and a party filled from another party's record is not offered that record in its own picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters each picker to its role, so a trader is not offered a GB importer as a place of origin; DR1 found the unfiltered list a live defect on all the pickers, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles because DR1 asked for role-filtered pickers. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm builds the role-filtered pickers and gives plants the same change in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-029 binds each animals party to its address-book role so only records offered for that role can be chosen, and repo-tests-p7-038, -p7-040 and -p7-085 prove the role-filtered list, the role-scoped search and the source record not being offered after a same-as fill; repo-plantsfrontend-p7-007, -p8-023 and -p9-073 show plants' consignor and place of destination pickers asking for their own role. Before it landed all five animals pickers searched one undifferentiated book (trace-animals-fit-p14-045).

requirements.statement: The consignor picker offers addresses saved for the consignor role, including any a trader thinks of as the exporter; there is no separate exporter party and no exporter role. How the address book records those roles is the address book's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's consignor section covers the exporter too. Ruling ian-2026-11-16 decides that no EXPORTER role is added anywhere, because the prototype's consignor-or-exporter vocabulary is its own internal type rather than a domain role, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 leaves the field shape of address roles to the address book service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-116 and -p7-117 show the address book holding six roles — place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer and branch address — with no exporter among them.

requirements.statement: An address saved with several roles appears on the picker of every party whose role it carries.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets one saved address be reused across parties, such as the same company as consignee and importer.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-038 shows a record saved for two roles listed on both roles' pickers.

requirements.statement: The address book holds one or more roles on each address record and lets a frontend list an organisation's live addresses for one or more roles, newest first and a page at a time, excluding deleted records, with the role filter running in the service before the page is cut. The animals frontend and the high-risk plants frontend each ask for their picker's role. The record's field shape for roles is the address book service's own design, not the prototype's.
requirements.why: DR1 found role filtering needs a typed address record, which no frontend can fake, and the address book is one of this programme's repos. Ruling paul-2026-11-05 point 8 keeps pagination on the list even though the prototype has none, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses, and ruling ian-2026-11-25 drops this requirement's earlier 'unpaginated' clause and confirms Paul's point 8 stands in full.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-012 to -p1-018 record the service as it stands on main: a list request filters on searchTerm, countryCodes, roles and searchRoles, lists the caller's live addresses newest first one page at a time with a 1-based page and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, and cuts the page after the role filter has run. repo-tests-p7-116 and -p2-132 show the six roles held against each record, and repo-frontend-p14-029, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-073 and -p9-019 show each frontend asking for its picker's role. Collecting the roles when an address is saved is the address-book and party-address-add-and-edit areas' work. The list API's own parameters, limits and filter order are req-2352 and req-2353 in the address book list area; this row holds the roles on the record, the role-scoped list a picker reads and each frontend asking for its picker's role.

requirements.statement: An address-book record that carries no role yet is offered on every party picker, in the animals frontend and in the high-risk plants frontend, until it is given a role, in the compose stack and in CDP alike.
requirements.why: Records saved before roles existed are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and DR1's judgement rules out filtering them on a guess, which would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-073, -p7-008 and -p7-009 show plants' pickers offering the records that carry their own role together with those carrying no role, and no others. No claim in this working set shows how the animals pickers treat a record with no role: repo-tests-p7-038 proves only that a picker lists the addresses saved for its party's role.

requirements.statement: In stub mode, each canned address-book record carries one or more roles, in the animals frontend's stub and in the high-risk plants frontend's stub book, so the stub-mode pickers filter by role as the real ones do.
requirements.why: The stub mirrors the tests repo's address-book fixture record for record and is what local development and each frontend's own suite run against; without roles it cannot show role filtering.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' stub book now holds roles: nine of its records are offered on the consignor picker and nine hold the destination role, while eighteen are offered on the role-free contact picker (repo-plantsfrontend-p7-009, -p8-042, -p7-073). No claim in this working set shows the animals frontend's own stub records carrying roles, and repo-tests-p2-131 records that the address book's role-driven ordering and filtering is proven only against the real service and skipped against stubs.

requirements.statement: Each party picker lists its addresses newest first, so an address just added through the address book appears at the top.
requirements.why: The prototype lists newly added addresses first, and the address book already serves its list newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-013 records the address book listing the caller's live addresses newest first, one page at a time, and trace-e2e-p9-030 and -p9-031 show the newest record filling the top of page one of the picker.

requirements.statement: When a party picker has no rows to list, because a search matched nothing or because the organisation's book holds no address it offers, it shows 'No addresses match your search.' where the results count would go, renders neither the fieldset nor the table, and still offers 'Save and continue'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not draw an empty result; the real message tells the trader why the list is empty, and nothing in the prototype contradicts it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-054 and -p2-115 show the animals message today, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-021 and -p9-036-m1 the same wording in plants, shown whenever the picker has no rows rather than only after a search.

requirements.statement: Every address-book read a journey makes is made on the server, for the signed-in session's organisation only, and a record belonging to another organisation is never offered or resolved; with no organisation on the session no read is made.
requirements.why: A real authorisation constraint: the address book trusts the organisation the caller names, so the frontend's scoping is what keeps one organisation's addresses from another.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-094 scopes the read to the organisation on the trader's signed-in session so another organisation's record is never returned, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-084 scopes both the addresses offered and the record a save resolves, and trace-e2e-p9-101 shows the calls made server-side.

requirements.statement: A deleted address-book record is never offered on a picker and can never be saved, and a stored answer picked from one shows no ticked row; an address book that cannot be reached is an error, never read as a deletion.
requirements.why: Deleted addresses must not be chosen again, and an outage must not look like a deletion.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-095 treats a deleted record as never chosen, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-071 and -p9-074 keep it off the picker and show no ticked row, and repo-tests-p7-076 and -p7-077 prove the soft delete and the dropped row end to end. repo-plantsfrontend-p7-102 shows plants handling no failure at all when the address book cannot be reached while listing addresses: only a failed save of the notification is handled.

requirements.statement: A journey reads the address book and never writes to it: adding a record goes through the INS frontend, and neither journey serves a create-address page of its own.
requirements.why: The INS frontend is the address book's only writer; how Design Release 2.1's in-journey add page is met belongs to the party-address-add-and-edit area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-096 shows the live-animals addresses/create path answering 404, repo-frontend-p14-075 the hand-off out to the INS address book's add page, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-095-m1 that no plants picker offers a way to add an address the book does not hold.

requirements.statement: Every string on the consignment addresses page and on every party picker, in both frontends, has a Welsh counterpart, still marked as a machine draft awaiting translator sign-off and not to be shown to users before Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: Both real services are bilingual, and DR1 asked for each copy change in both languages; the prototype has no Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-104 shows the animals page's Welsh file carrying the same keys as the English one and marked as an unreviewed machine draft, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-086 and -p8-129 show every word the plants picker shell and the place of destination page show existing in both languages, likewise marked a machine draft (repo-plantsfrontend-p9-085, -p8-045).

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page and every party picker, in both frontends, have no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 A and AA and 2.2 AA, on first render and in their error states, and a stored address name or address line holding markup characters is shown as text rather than rendered as markup.
requirements.why: The real pages pass today and must keep passing as they change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p7-027, -p7-028 and -p8-044 show plants' pickers clean on first render and in their refused state, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-048 that stored markup is shown as text, and trace-animals-fit-p14-020 and -p15-037 clean axe scans of the animals page and picker.

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search is labelled 'Enter a country'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype itself withdrew the place of origin picker's separate country search, so the picker takes the same search as the other four. Before that, Design Release 2.1 searched the place of origin list by country with this label and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm built it.
requirements.deltaNote: Every picker, place of origin included, labels its search 'Search' (repo-tests-p2-114).

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search has the hint 'Enter each country that the consignment will travel through'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype itself withdrew the place of origin picker's separate country search, so the picker takes the same search hint as the other four. Before that, Design Release 2.1 gave this hint and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm built it.
requirements.deltaNote: The place of origin search's hint is 'Name, address or country' (repo-tests-p2-114).

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search box shows the placeholder 'Search for a country'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype itself withdrew the place of origin picker's separate country search, so the picker takes the same search box as the other four. Before that, Design Release 2.1 prompted for a country inside the box and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm built it.
requirements.deltaNote: No picker's search box carries a placeholder (repo-tests-p2-114).

requirements.statement: On both animals sets, the place of origin picker's country search is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select of the countries MDM serves through reference-data, behaving as the real frontend configures it, with a button that submits the chosen country so the server narrows the rows to addresses in that country; submitting with no country shows every row. Without JavaScript the native select and the button do the same.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype itself withdrew the place of origin picker's separate country search, so there is no country search to build. Before that, ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm built the no-JavaScript half with the accessible autocomplete, whose entries come from MDM.
requirements.deltaNote: The place of origin picker has the same free-text server search within its own role as every other picker (repo-tests-p7-040).

requirements.statement: The prototype's fixed demonstration addresses (nine places of origin, nine consignors, six consignees and importers, three places of destination) and its development socket polling are built into the real service.
requirements.why: Out of scope: they are the prototype's seed data; the real pickers list the organisation's own address book.

requirements.statement: The prototype's page paths (/roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination under /design-release-2.1) replace the real service's routes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling sam-2026-10-09 says the prototype never decides URL paths and no increment changes an existing real path to match it; the real service keeps /addresses and its /select routes, in both the live-animals and the germinal-products sets.

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page's Change links drop the visually hidden party name, as the prototype's do.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype's identical 'Change' links are an accessibility gap a sighted user cannot see, not a design choice; the real links keep naming the party for screen-reader users.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an add-address page served inside the live-animals journey at /<role path>/add-address that saves into the address book without the trader leaving the animals service.
requirements.why: Where the add page is served and which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the single-app prototype cannot express, so the INS frontend stays the address book's only writer, reached through the journey handshake; the animals frontend serves no /<role>/add-address page and its address-book service stays read-only (c-106).
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Add a new address' sends the trader to the INS address book's add page (repo-frontend-p15-057), whose page sits in the INS layout (trace-e2e-p9-055-m1); the journey's own create page was retired and answers 404 (trace-e2e-p9-080).

requirements.statement: Every party picker (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination) and the consignment contact page has an 'Add a new address' control to the INS address book's add page, carrying journey-type 'gbn-ag', the notification reference, the role's fulfilment id and a fresh handshake token, which the INS add page keeps as hidden fields and sends back unchanged; the pickers show no add control while the frontend runs in stub mode.
requirements.why: The handshake is how the INS address book knows which notification and role to return the new address to; it stays because the INS frontend remains the address book's only writer (c-106). DR1 asked for a route to add an address from every address-selection page (inc-053), and it now exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: the picker offers 'Add a new address' beside its heading and sends the four parameters to the INS add page (repo-frontend-p15-056, repo-frontend-p15-057), the contact page offers its own 'add a new branch address' link (repo-tests-p7-013), all five pickers are proven to open the page (repo-tests-p7-002), the handshake comes back unchanged (trace-e2e-p9-070-m1) and stub mode offers neither the add control nor the View links (repo-frontend-p15-036).

requirements.statement: The journey's address-return route accepts a return only when its fulfilment id names a role and its handshake token matches the single-use token the picker issued for that role, a missing, reused or mismatched token included, and looks the returned address id up in the signed-in organisation's own address book.
requirements.why: Stops a forged or replayed return from writing another organisation's address, or any address, into a notification.
requirements.deltaNote: The return route is built and carries the fulfilment id and token back unchanged, with a fresh token on every render of the picker (trace-e2e-p9-016, trace-e2e-p9-070, trace-e2e-p9-070-m1); what no source in this area shows is a missing, expired, reused or mismatched token being refused (trace-e2e-p9-078), so the refusals are what is left to prove.

requirements.statement: When a return cannot be completed, the trader goes back to the role's picker: an address that is not found or is deleted shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.', and an address book that cannot be reached, or a save that fails, shows 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: A failed return must leave the trader somewhere they can carry on, with a reason they can act on.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: the picker opens with the not-found message (repo-frontend-p15-059) or the unreachable message, marked as a recoverable error (repo-frontend-p15-060).

requirements.statement: A trader with no INS session who follows 'Add a new address' signs in through Defra ID first and then lands on the INS add page with the handshake intact.
requirements.why: The INS frontend owns its own session and stays the address book's only writer (c-106); crossing to it must not lose which notification and role the address is for.
requirements.deltaNote: Seen today end to end (trace-e2e-p9-052).

requirements.statement: The add-address page reached from the journey is headed 'Add address and contact details', with the browser title 'Add address and contact details - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading says the page collects contact details as well as the address.
requirements.deltaNote: The tests repo proves the heading and the browser title on the page reached from the journey (repo-tests-p7-024, repo-tests-p7-023); the e2e traces still show the earlier 'Add address details' page because they were captured before it was rebuilt (trace-e2e-p9-055, c-396).

requirements.statement: The add-address page shows the caption 'Add new address' above its heading.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 captions the page.
requirements.deltaNote: The caption is proven on the page reached from the journey (repo-tests-p7-024); the traces predate it (trace-e2e-p9-055, c-396).

requirements.statement: The add-address page shows the notification's status block, a 'Draft' tag and the notification reference, as the other journey pages do.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the trader oriented in their notification while they add an address.
requirements.deltaNote: The page reached from the journey shows the 'Draft' tag and the reference (repo-tests-p7-025); the traces still show it in the INS layout with no notification status (trace-e2e-p9-055-m1, c-396).

requirements.statement: The add-address page has a Back link to the picker of the role the address is being added for.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the trader a way back to the page they came from.
requirements.deltaNote: The page offers a Back link and it lands on the picker it was reached from (repo-tests-p7-003, repo-tests-p7-022); the traces show no back link (trace-e2e-p9-055, c-396).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's first section heading is 'Address'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The page groups its fields under 'Address' and 'Contact details' (repo-tests-p7-026); the traces still show 'Enter address details' (trace-e2e-p9-057, c-396).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's second section heading is 'Contact details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven as the page's second section heading (repo-tests-p7-026); the traces still show 'Enter contact details' (trace-e2e-p9-057, c-396).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's name field is labelled 'Name or organisation'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The page's first field is labelled 'Name or organisation' (repo-tests-p7-015); the traces still show 'Name or organisation name' (trace-e2e-p9-058, c-396).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's address fields are labelled 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code' and 'Country' (a select), and address line 2 may be left blank.
requirements.why: These labels are the ones the design gives.
requirements.deltaNote: The page already carries these labels, with address line 2 marked optional (repo-tests-p7-015, trace-e2e-p9-059, trace-e2e-p9-060, trace-e2e-p9-061, trace-e2e-p9-063).

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an add-address page with no County field.
requirements.why: Set aside by the ruling of 14 October 2026, which keeps 'County (optional)' on the address book's add-details step, the very step the journey's add-address page is: the V4 Address Block gives every address block the same fields, County included, and an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view page and the edit form all carry would lose that data on a round trip (c-395). What the page asks for instead is the requirement beside this one.
requirements.deltaNote: The page offers 'County (optional)' today (trace-e2e-p9-062, repo-tests-p7-015) and keeps it.

requirements.statement: On the place of origin and consignor add-address pages the Country select's first option reads 'Select one'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the first option reads 'Select a country' on every route into the page (repo-tests-p7-030, repo-tests-p7-029, trace-e2e-p9-064).

requirements.statement: The manual-entry Country select on the add-address page is a plain select rather than the accessible autocomplete, and offers the countries reference-data serves from MDM, never a list typed or edited in code; the page's tests take country names and counts from the captured reference-data fixture rather than a hand-typed list.
requirements.why: No country or port list waits on MDM integration: countries already come from real MDM through trade-imports-reference-data (the stub locally and in CDP dev, real MDM in CDP test), and who owns list content is still DR1's MDM judgement (ruling 2026-10-09, c-107). A field the prototype shows as a plain select stays one, and the INS address book's country autocomplete is a follow-on ticket recorded in deferred.md (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: The select is a plain select and already offers every country reference-data serves, alphabetically with United Kingdom in its alphabetical place (repo-tests-p7-030, repo-tests-p7-037). The design's 42-entry list is not built: where the served content differs from the design, that is MDM's content to change and never a list edited in code (c-107). The traces still show the earlier 32-entry stub list with United Kingdom pulled to the front (trace-e2e-p9-064, c-396).

requirements.statement: Under 'Contact details' the add-address page asks for 'Email address' then 'Phone number', with the phone hint 'For international numbers include the country code'.
requirements.why: These fields and their order already match Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: The page asks for Email address then Phone number with the same hint (repo-tests-p7-015, trace-e2e-p9-065, trace-e2e-p9-066).

requirements.statement: Place of origin and consignor addresses are entered by hand for any country, with every field shown at once; consignee, importer and place of destination addresses are UK addresses, whose Country select holds only 'United Kingdom', preselected, and whose saved country is always United Kingdom, both on the manual entry built now and on the search pages once address search is built.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 splits the roles: origin-side parties can be anywhere, destination-side parties are in Great Britain. The address book refuses a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom and leaves the other roles unrestricted, so the select matches a rule the service already enforces.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the consignee route opens the same full country select, merely defaulted to United Kingdom with 'Select a country' listed first (repo-tests-p7-029), so the list is not narrowed to the United Kingdom for any destination-side role.

requirements.statement: Every add-address page that searches (the consignee, importer and place of destination pages reached from the journey, and the address book's 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' add-details step) starts with a UK address search: a text field labelled 'Search for an address', placeholder 'Start typing...', browser autocomplete turned off, and the service's own joined search button whose accessible name is 'Search', which submits the search to the server on the button or Enter so it works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finds UK addresses by search rather than typing them in; design has since decided the search does not filter as the trader types, so the term is typed and then submitted, and the joined search button is the one design snagging already built for the service's other search boxes.
requirements.deltaNote: No address search exists today: neither the add page nor the party edit form offers one, and the only search in the journey is over the organisation's own address book (repo-frontend-p15-149).
requirements.blockedBy: Parked by ruling:sam-2026-11-09 points 2 and 3: address search is concept work and is not needed for the deadline. It also waits on the INS backend's address lookup becoming a real feature, today only the EUDPA-390 spike gated to dev and local and not wired in; the address search area is re-distilled once it lands.

requirements.statement: Submitting the address search lists matching UK addresses under 'Address search results', each a choice showing the organisation name and the full one-line address; Northern Ireland addresses are not offered.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search results, in the version that works without JavaScript (ruling 2026-10-09 pm); results that appear as the trader types are a separate, design-blocked requirement. Northern Ireland searching waits with the address book's own Northern Ireland rows, which wait on the same lookup.
requirements.blockedBy: Parked by ruling:sam-2026-11-09 points 2 and 3: address search is concept work and is not needed for the deadline. It also waits on the INS backend's address lookup becoming a real feature, today only the EUDPA-390 spike gated to dev and local and not wired in; the address search area is re-distilled once it lands.

requirements.statement: The address search announces its result count to screen readers through a polite live region, such as '1 result available'.
requirements.why: Screen reader users must hear that results have appeared; a custom announcement is JavaScript-only behaviour beyond the component's own options, so it waits on design as well as the lookup (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.blockedBy: Parked by ruling:sam-2026-11-09 points 2 and 3: address search is concept work, not needed for the deadline. When it is planned, design answers design question 10 (ruling 2026-10-09 pm): whether address search keeps a search-only layout that hides the address fields, or uses the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible; that is one waiting-on-design increment. It is also blocked until the INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature, and the address search area is re-distilled once it lands.

requirements.statement: Picking a search result fills name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode with country United Kingdom, all still editable; email address and phone number stay empty for the trader to complete; any earlier error messages stay until the next submit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's pick behaviour, in the version that works without JavaScript: the pick is submitted and the page comes back filled. Hiding the search box on a pick is part of the design-blocked search-only layout (req-653).

requirements.statement: Picking a search result never drops part of the address the lookup returned: a locality (such as Kirkby in 'Depot road, Kirkby, Liverpool') is kept in the filled form.
requirements.why: The prototype loses the locality because its form has no field for it; a saved address missing part of itself is a real data constraint the prototype cannot express.

requirements.why: A trader whose address the search does not find must still be able to add it; the button exists only because the search-only layout hides the fields, so it waits on design question 10 as well as the lookup (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reveals the form only once there is an address to complete; the search-only layout is design question 10's increment, because design is asked whether the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible will do instead (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).

requirements.statement: Submitting a search page with either save button before picking or entering anything shows the six field errors in order ('Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address', 'Enter a phone number'), with no country error and no error of the search's own, and reveals the fields so each error summary link reaches a visible field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's messages for the search-only layout; the prototype's summary links point at hidden fields, which the GOV.UK error summary pattern does not allow, and the owner's 26 October decision makes both save buttons check alike with no page an exception. With the fields always visible the manual-entry messages (req-660 to req-667) already apply, so this waits on design question 10 as well as the lookup.

requirements.statement: The add-address page reached from a party picker asks 'What else should this address be used for?' as a checkbox fieldset; the page reached from the consignment contact page asks no such question, because a branch address plays only its own role.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets one new address be saved for more roles than the one it was added from, and the address book refuses roles from more than one group, so the branch route has no other role to offer.
requirements.deltaNote: The question is built on the page reached from a party picker (repo-tests-p7-027, repo-tests-p7-031) and the contact route asks no roles question (repo-tests-p7-014).

requirements.statement: The roles question's hint reads 'This address is being added as a <Role> address. Select any other roles or addresses this address should be used for.', naming the role's own label (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer or Place of destination) and using 'an' before Importer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; it tells the trader the role they came from is already implied.
requirements.deltaNote: The consignee route shows exactly this hint with the role named (repo-tests-p7-031).

requirements.statement: The roles checkboxes offer only the other roles in the same group as the role the page was reached for, each labelled with the role name alone and no hint: place of origin offers 'Consignor'; consignor offers 'Place of origin'; consignee offers 'Importer' and 'Place of destination'; importer offers 'Consignee' and 'Place of destination'; place of destination offers 'Consignee' and 'Importer'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never lets an origin-side address be marked for a destination-side role, or the other way round, and the address book refuses an address whose roles come from more than one group, each of the six roles sitting in exactly one group.
requirements.deltaNote: The consignor route offers 'Place of origin' alone (repo-tests-p7-027) and the consignee route offers exactly 'Importer' and 'Place of destination' (repo-tests-p7-032).

requirements.statement: No roles checkbox is preselected, ticking none raises no error, a value not offered for the role is discarded, and the ticks are kept when the page is shown again with errors; the address still holds at least one role, because the role the page was reached for is always saved.
requirements.why: The role the trader came from is implied, the extra roles are optional, and the address book requires an address to hold at least one role.
requirements.deltaNote: Both options open unticked (repo-tests-p7-032) and a refused save keeps the tick already made (repo-tests-p7-035).

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved in the address book holding the role it was added for plus every role ticked, and nothing else: the record stores roles only, with at least one, and no address type.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the address for more than the role it was added from, and the ruling of 5 November 2026 settles what the record holds: roles only, renamed from uses, at least one, with the address type derived by the INS front door from those roles rather than stored.
requirements.deltaNote: A save holds exactly the picker's role (repo-tests-p7-005), the branch route's BRANCH_ADDRESS role (repo-tests-p7-017), and both CONSIGNEE and IMPORTER when Importer is ticked (repo-tests-p7-033); the earlier record shape with no role field is what the traces show (trace-e2e-p8-012).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank name shows 'Enter a name or organisation name', linked to the name field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add page shows 'Enter a name or organisation' (repo-tests-p7-036) and the journey's own edit page shows 'Enter a name' (repo-frontend-p15-110).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank address line 1 shows 'Enter address line 1'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven as the add page's first listed error (repo-tests-p7-034) and used on the edit page too (repo-frontend-p15-111).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank town or city shows 'Enter a town or city'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven on the add page (repo-tests-p7-034) and used on the edit page (repo-frontend-p15-113).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank postcode shows 'Enter a postcode or Zip code'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven on the add page (repo-tests-p7-034). The journey's own edit page still shows 'Enter a postcode' (repo-frontend-p15-115), which req-687 keeps as the address book's own message.

requirements.statement: On the add-address page no country chosen shows 'Select a country'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book's own message, which the journey copies, is 'Enter a country' (repo-frontend-p15-116, repo-frontend-p15-119), and no source shows the add page's country error being driven.

requirements.statement: On the add-address page email address is required, and a blank one shows 'Enter an email address'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven on the add page (repo-tests-p7-034) and used on the edit page (repo-frontend-p15-118).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page phone number is required, and a blank one shows 'Enter a phone number'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven as the add page's last listed error (repo-tests-p7-034). The journey's own edit page still shows 'Enter a telephone number' (repo-frontend-p15-117), which req-687 keeps as the address book's own message.

requirements.statement: A failed submit of the add-address page shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing every error in field order, each repeated inline with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix and the field in its GOV.UK error style, and keeps everything the trader entered and every role they ticked.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern, which Design Release 2.1 and today's address forms share; the owner's 26 October decision adds that what a trader typed is never dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: The add page lists its errors in field order, gives each field the 'Error:' description and keeps what was typed and ticked while storing nothing (repo-tests-p7-034, repo-tests-p7-035, repo-tests-p7-036); the journey's own forms use the same pattern (trace-e2e-p8-054).

requirements.statement: The add-address page applies the address book's length and format checks alongside the required-field checks: name and address lines 255 characters or fewer, town or city and county 100, postcode 12, phone 20, email 254 and in a valid format, each with its own message (such as 'Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer' and 'Enter an email address in the correct format').
requirements.why: The address book stores and validates these limits; a real validation constraint the prototype cannot express overrides its required-only checks.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book's rules already carry these caps and messages, and the journey copies them (repo-frontend-p15-108, repo-frontend-p15-115, repo-frontend-p15-118, repo-frontend-p15-119; repo-tests-p7-063, trace-e2e-p8-049, trace-e2e-p8-050).

requirements.statement: A refused add-address submit answers HTTP 400 and prefixes the browser title with 'Error: '.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern tells assistive technology the page holds errors; today's address forms already do it.
requirements.deltaNote: The journey's address forms answer 400 with an 'Error: ' title (repo-frontend-p15-130, trace-e2e-p8-047-m1, trace-animals-fit-p15-062).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's fields carry browser autocomplete hints: organization for the name, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2 for town or city, postal-code, email and tel.
requirements.why: GOV.UK and WCAG 1.3.5 ask personal-data inputs to identify their purpose; the prototype leaves them out.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every field but the name carries its hint: the name field has none, while address line 1, address line 2, town or city, postcode, email and phone carry theirs (repo-tests-p7-028). The journey's edit page already sets organization on the name (repo-frontend-p15-105).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's primary button reads 'Save and select'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The page reached from a party picker offers 'Save and select' (repo-tests-p7-003); the traces still show 'Save and continue' (trace-e2e-p9-067, c-396), which the contact route still uses (c-399).

requirements.statement: 'Save and select' saves the new address to the address book, puts a copy of it on the notification for the role it was added for, and returns the trader to the Consignment addresses page, where the role shows the address with a 'Change' link; after a consignee is saved this way, the unset importer and place of destination rows offer the 'Same as consignee' shortcut that page already carries.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finishes the role in one step.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven: Save and select lands on the Consignment addresses page with the role filled and a Change link (repo-tests-p7-004), reached from the Overview task 'Consignment addresses' (repo-tests-p7-011, repo-tests-p7-006). The same-as shortcut rows are req-577 and req-578 and are already on the page (repo-frontend-p15-091). The traces still show the older return to the picker with the address merely preselected (trace-e2e-p9-071, trace-e2e-p9-073, c-396).

requirements.statement: A secondary 'Save and return to address page' button saves the new address to the address book without selecting it, and returns the trader to the role's picker, where the new address is listed first and nothing is selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader add an address and still choose among the book. Its checks are the primary save's, because the owner's 26 October decision makes the save buttons behave consistently.
requirements.deltaNote: The button is on the page and lands on the picker with the banner and nothing selected, the new address listed first (repo-tests-p7-003, repo-tests-p7-007, repo-tests-p7-008). The picker it lands on shows eight addresses a page and restates the chosen address above the results (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-022, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-025); the traces still show only 'Cancel and return to address page' (trace-e2e-p9-067, c-396).

requirements.statement: After either save, the page the trader lands on shows a GOV.UK notification banner titled 'Success' reading '<Name> address added to your address book', which stays on screen until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1, like DR1, confirms the address went into the address book; a message that leaves on a timer fails WCAG 2.2.1, so the banner stays and the INS frontend's script that hides it is removed (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: The banner is shown on the Consignment addresses page, on the picker and on the contact page, is still there ten seconds later and goes on reload (repo-tests-p7-004, repo-tests-p7-016, repo-tests-p7-020, repo-tests-p7-021, repo-frontend-p15-058).

requirements.statement: The add-address page offers a 'Cancel and return to hub' link to the notification's hub, which saves nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy and destination.
requirements.deltaNote: The link is on the page and lands on the Overview saving nothing, leaving the role with only its add link (repo-tests-p7-003, repo-tests-p7-009, repo-tests-p7-010); the traces still show a 'Cancel and return to address page' button (trace-e2e-p9-075, c-396).

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved into the signed-in organisation's address book with its email and phone, and is then listed in the address book and in every role picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that a journey-added address joins the shared book.
requirements.deltaNote: A newly added address is listed in the picker and above the branch addresses already in the book (repo-tests-p7-008, repo-tests-p7-018), created through the organisation-scoped address book API (trace-e2e-p8-011).

requirements.statement: The add-address page is built from GOV.UK Frontend components (input, select, checkboxes, hint, error summary, notification banner, buttons, back link, width classes); the address search is the one component outside the toolbox, because GOV.UK Frontend has none.
requirements.why: The prototype's app-* field and heading classes are its own implementation, not a difference a trader sees.
requirements.deltaNote: The page uses only GOV.UK Frontend components (trace-e2e-p9-068).

requirements.statement: The add-address round trip (both saves and cancel) is proven end to end from every role picker and from the consignment contact page.
requirements.why: Each picker issues its own fulfilment id, so a return that works from one proves nothing about the rest.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add control is proven to open the page from all five pickers (repo-tests-p7-002), but each of the two saves and the cancel is proven once only (repo-tests-p7-004, repo-tests-p7-007, repo-tests-p7-009), the traces drove the round trip from the consignor picker alone (trace-e2e-p9-077), and the hand-off is skipped in stub mode so no fit spec covers it (repo-tests-p7-001, repo-frontend-p15-146).

requirements.statement: A picked or added address is copied onto the notification, not linked: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record later leaves the draft's copy as it was, with no error, and the picker then neither preselects nor offers a deleted record.
requirements.why: A notification must hold the address it was made with; Design Release 2.1 also stores a copy on the section.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today: a chosen address is copied rather than referenced (repo-frontend-p15-063), a deleted or role-less record counts as no selection (repo-frontend-p15-055), and the copy survives renaming and deletion of the record (trace-e2e-p8-001, trace-e2e-p8-006, repo-tests-p7-061).

requirements.statement: On the review page each consignment party and the contact address read back as the name followed by the address lines and country (GB shown as 'United Kingdom'), each on its own line, without the telephone number or email address, under a card titled 'Consignment addresses'. The plants frontend's check-answers place of destination, consignor and contact cards read back the same way, in the same increment: the name, then one line per address line, then the country, with no telephone number and no email address row.
requirements.why: The trader checks the copy the notification holds before submitting, and the owner's 17 November decision gives the addresses the same wording on check your answers, the overview task list and the addresses page. Plants has the same party cards, so it takes the same change at the same time (ruling 2026-10-09 pm), which withdraws plants' own d-013 addition of telephone and email to the contact card (c-293). The address-book record still carries both.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review shows each copied address as a block, name in bold then each non-empty field on its own line, telephone and email included (trace-e2e-p8-004, trace-e2e-p8-018), and the review already carries a 'Consignment addresses' card and a separate 'Contact address' card (repo-tests-p7-067, repo-tests-p7-068). Plants' party cards today carry Name, Address, Telephone number and Email address rows with the address joined by commas, and lose telephone and email and read line by line in the same increment (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-045); the plants repo claims that show today's cards sit in the party-cards area's working set, not this one. The overview-and-review area writes the same card title, so the cross-area pass merges the two.

requirements.statement: Each role and the consignment contact has its own page for editing the copy the notification holds, at the role's own edit path, reached from the hub's and review page's 'Edit details' links; in the high-risk plants frontend the same page serves each party plants holds.
requirements.why: The address book accepts records that break the notification's address rules, so a notification needs a way to correct its own copy without touching the book: a real validation and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today in both frontends: six edit pages in live animals (repo-frontend-p15-096, repo-frontend-p15-003) and three in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-052), reached from the 'Edit details' link (repo-tests-p7-055, repo-tests-p7-056). Design Release 2.1 shows no such page; it is kept because rule-breaking copies need it (req-694).

requirements.statement: The party edit page is headed 'Edit address details', captioned with the party's own title ('Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination' or 'Contact address for consignment'), titled 'Edit address details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', below the notification's journey strip.
requirements.why: The merged consignor-and-exporter party is the single Consignor, as the design's own section heading reads and the service's role vocabulary already holds, so the caption names the party once.
requirements.deltaNote: The heading, the title and the strip are built (repo-frontend-p15-098, repo-frontend-p15-098-m1, trace-e2e-p8-032-m1, trace-e2e-p8-090), and the consignor's caption reads 'Consignor or exporter' today, which names a party the service does not model and no role vocabulary holds (ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-029, ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-035). Plants already captions the same page with the party's own title (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-053), so plants needs no change here.

requirements.statement: The party edit page explains 'Changes apply to this notification only. Your address book is not changed.'
requirements.why: The trader must know the edit does not reach the book.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-099, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-054, repo-tests-p7-057).

requirements.statement: The party edit page asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code' (width 10), 'Country' (a plain select, 'Select a country' then the address book's country list), 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code') and 'Email address', in that order; only address line 2 and county are optional.
requirements.why: The page sets every field the address book record carries, so a corrected copy loses nothing. Its Country stays a plain select in this programme: the animals party address country's autocomplete is a follow-on ticket recorded in deferred.md (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: Built today with these nine fields in this order in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-100, repo-frontend-p15-101, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-056, repo-tests-p7-059, trace-e2e-p8-035 to trace-e2e-p8-044).

requirements.statement: The party edit page's buttons are 'Save changes' and a secondary 'Cancel', with no save-and-return-to-overview control.
requirements.why: The page is an aside from a picker or from the review, not a step of the journey.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-120, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-070, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-072, trace-e2e-p8-045).

requirements.statement: The party edit page opens pre-filled with every field of the notification's copy, the country select set to its code; before any address is picked for that party it sends the trader to the party's picker and saves nothing.
requirements.why: There is nothing to edit until a copy exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-121, repo-frontend-p15-131, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-078, repo-tests-p7-058, trace-e2e-p8-034).

requirements.statement: The party edit page applies the address book's rules and messages: 'Enter a name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode', 'Enter a country' for a blank country, 'Enter a telephone number', 'Enter an email address', plus the length caps and the email-format check, with address line 2 and county never required.
requirements.why: The copy must meet the same rules the address book sets, so a corrected copy is valid.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p15-110 to repo-frontend-p15-119, repo-tests-p7-063, trace-e2e-p8-048, trace-e2e-p8-051), and plants copies the same rules and sentences from the address book (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-092, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-093).

requirements.statement: A refused edit answers 400, re-renders 'Edit address details' with the error summary and an error on each field, keeps what was typed (the country select resets to 'Select a country' for an unlisted value) and saves nothing; browser validation is off.
requirements.why: A refused edit must leave the notification's copy as it was, and the owner's 26 October decision is that a save with a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered kept.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-130, repo-frontend-p15-133, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-084-m1, repo-tests-p7-064, trace-e2e-p8-047, trace-e2e-p8-053).

requirements.statement: A valid edit replaces only this notification's copy of the party: the address book record and any other notification holding a copy of it are unchanged, the party's picker opens with no address preselected, and no banner is shown.
requirements.why: The copy belongs to the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-122 to repo-frontend-p15-124, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-082, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-083, repo-tests-p7-061, repo-tests-p7-062, repo-tests-p7-071, trace-e2e-p8-028).

requirements.statement: Save, Cancel and Back on the party edit page return to where the edit was started, named by its return marker from a closed list (the addresses hub, the review page or the contact picker in live animals; check-your-answers or one of the three pickers in plants), falling back to the party's own picker and keeping the trail; Cancel discards what was typed.
requirements.why: The trader comes back to the page they left.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-126, repo-frontend-p15-127, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-088, repo-tests-p7-065, repo-tests-p7-066, trace-e2e-p8-057, trace-e2e-p8-058).

requirements.statement: If saving an edit fails with a recoverable backend error, the party edit page re-renders with status 500 and the recoverable-error message, and the held copy is unchanged.
requirements.why: A failed save must not lose or corrupt the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-132, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-090).

requirements.statement: The party edit page has Welsh copy for every piece of wording it shows, the character-limit sentences included, marked as a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator.
requirements.why: Today's Welsh copy, which needs Welsh Language Standards sign-off before it ships to users.
requirements.deltaNote: Present in both frontends and marked as a machine draft (repo-frontend-p15-142, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-127, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-128).

requirements.statement: The party edit page is built only from GOV.UK Frontend components and has no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.2 AA.
requirements.why: Accessibility.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-140, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-124, trace-animals-fit-p15-067).

requirements.statement: A copy is checked against the notification's address rules: the address book accepts a record the rules refuse (such as a country name rather than a listed code), the picker lets the trader pick it, and its edit form then opens with no country selected.
requirements.why: The address book only checks a country is present, so the notification must catch a copy that breaks its rules.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p15-109, repo-tests-p7-063-m1, trace-e2e-p8-013, trace-e2e-p8-022), and plants can check a held copy the same way (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-126).

requirements.statement: On the review page an answered party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules is named in a 'There is a problem' error summary ('Correct the address details for the <role>', 'Correct the contact address details for this consignment'), linked to that party's edit page with return=notification-view and repeated inside the party's row; a stored answer that has become invalid is named on its card; these entries come before the unfinished-card entries, and either stops Continue.
requirements.why: The trader must see which copy to correct and get straight to it. The single-app prototype holds no copy that can break a rule, so it cannot express these errors (c-139).
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today end to end (trace-e2e-p8-015, trace-e2e-p8-016, trace-e2e-p8-017, trace-e2e-p8-019), and plants links its own check-answers refusal straight to the party's edit page (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-118).

requirements.statement: While a copy breaks the rules, Continue on the review page is refused (400, same error summary) and a direct declaration submit is refused and sent back to the review page.
requirements.why: A notification with an invalid party address must not be submitted, and the review page is where submission is refused.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-020, trace-e2e-p8-020-m1, trace-e2e-p8-021).

requirements.statement: Correcting the copy on its edit page and saving returns to the review page with the error gone, after which the trader can continue to the Declaration and submit to 'Import notification submitted'.
requirements.why: Correction must unblock submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-023, trace-e2e-p8-024).

requirements.statement: Once a notification is submitted its copied addresses are frozen: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record changes neither the submitted view, whose status tag reads 'Submitted' and which offers no Change or Edit details links, nor an amendment, neither shows an error, and cancelling the amendment restores the submitted copy.
requirements.why: A submitted notification is a record of what was declared, and a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED like any other, no separate status being introduced.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-081, trace-e2e-p8-084, trace-e2e-p8-085), with one gap: no source edits a copy during an amendment and then cancels it (trace-e2e-p8-097).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the CPH number question applies when the consignment holds a commodity line for cattle (0102), pigs (0103), sheep (010410), goats (010420) or poultry, whether day-old chicks (01051111, 01051200, 01051300, 01051400, 01051500), adult birds (01059400, 01059910, 01059920, 01059930, 01059950) or hatching eggs (04071100, 04071911, 04071919). The rule is held as a list of the commodities that need a CPH number, in whatever shape the animals frontend chooses, and covers the rest of that list once the MDM catalogue holds them, with no further change. Where it does not apply, the CPH page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The plants frontend has no CPH number and gets nothing from this rule.
requirements.why: The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page names the commodities that need a CPH number, and the 11 November ruling makes it the source of truth for which commodities a conditional rule covers and has its allow-list replace the frontend's exempt list, so a commodity MDM adds no longer defaults to needing one. The page stays out of reach for a consignment whose commodities have no holding. This is the live half of the CPH rule: the 2026-10-09 ruling splits req-699 per set, and the germinal set has no CPH page at all (req-1832). The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling blocks the new catalogue on MDM but lets the CPH page go ahead on today's commodities, and never mirrors CPH into plants.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the rule is an exempt list, so every code MDM adds defaults to needing a CPH number, rabbits, reptiles, parrots, bees and insects among them (ruling-ian-2026-11-11-p1-033). The skip itself is built: a consignment with no CPH commodity cannot open the page and is sent to the consignment addresses page, with the skip logged (repo-frontend-p16-030, repo-frontend-p16-031). The germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 leave the live-animals catalogue, so the live rule no longer names them.

requirements.statement: On the consignment addresses page the CPH section is headed 'County parish holding (CPH) number', described 'The county parish holding (CPH) number identifies the holding where the animals will be kept.', sits after the place of destination, and before a number is saved offers the link 'Add a CPH number'.
requirements.why: The link text is Design Release 2.1's; a bare 'Add' action reads as nothing on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: The heading, description and position already match, and the CPH page is reached from an add control in the section (repo-frontend-p16-002, repo-tests-p1-166, repo-tests-p1-163). No current claim gives that control's text; the e2e trace, an earlier recording of the service, shows an 'Add' link with the hidden suffix ' county parish holding (cph) number' (trace-e2e-p6-073).

requirements.statement: A saved CPH number is shown on the consignment addresses page and on the review page as county/parish/holding with slashes, such as '12/345/6789', with a 'Change' link back to the CPH page.
requirements.why: The slashed form is how traders read and check a CPH number, and it is how Design Release 2.1 shows it everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: The consignment addresses page already shows the slashed form (repo-frontend-p16-027, repo-tests-p1-162, repo-tests-p1-165) and already offers the Change link (trace-e2e-p6-076). No current claim shows the review page's CPH row; the e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows nine bare digits there (trace-e2e-p6-075).

requirements.statement: A valid CPH number is stored as nine bare digits, the three parts joined with no separators, and is split back 2/3/4 into its boxes when the page is shown again.
requirements.why: The stored shape is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: the record, and every stored notification, holds nine digits, so only the display gains slashes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-026: saving stores the nine digits as one value and reopening shows them split back into county, parish and holding.

requirements.statement: The CPH page has the caption 'Addresses', the single h1 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH)', and the browser title 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH) - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The heading and title are Design Release 2.1's and the service's alike, and the caption names the section the page belongs to, which the 17 November ruling words 'Addresses' wherever it appears.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-003 shows the caption 'Addresses' directly above the H1 and repo-frontend-p16-004 that the H1 is the only level-1 heading; repo-tests-p1-157 proves the heading end to end. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows the caption 'Consignment parties' (trace-animals-fit-p13-003).

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages show the notification's 'Draft' tag and reference above the content.
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are changing.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-023 and trace-e2e-p7-008: the journey strip with the Draft tag and reference is on these pages, which all three now share.

requirements.statement: A collapsed 'What is a CPH number?' details component sits above the CPH inputs and, when opened, says 'A county parish holding (CPH) number is a unique 9-digit number used to identify land and buildings where livestock are kept, moved or handled.'
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their CPH number need to know what it is before they look for it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-005 and repo-tests-p1-160 show the same summary and definition.

requirements.statement: The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', in English and Welsh, with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' as a link to the GOV.UK 'Get a county parish holding (CPH) number' guidance (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds a second place to find the number and the prototype wins; its href is only a placeholder, so the link opens the GOV.UK page its text names (c-117).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-006 and repo-tests-p1-160: the paragraph carries the GOV.UK clause and the link to that guidance, opening in the same tab. An earlier recording of the page, the claim c-117 sets aside, showed the second paragraph ending after '(APHA)'.

requirements.statement: The CPH number is asked as one fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number', not as a heading.
requirements.why: One question, one legend, so the page keeps a single h1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-007 and repo-frontend-p16-004: one fieldset group legended 'CPH number', and the legend is not a heading.

requirements.statement: The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and describes the whole group.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's wording of the hint.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-007 and repo-tests-p1-159: the group's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789' with no full stop. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows 'For example, 12/345/6789.' (trace-animals-fit-p13-007).

requirements.statement: The CPH number is entered in three boxes in one row, laid out with the GOV.UK date-input pattern, with visible labels 'County' (2 wide), 'Parish' (3 wide) and 'Holding number' (4 wide), each asking for a numeric keypad. The boxes do not cut typing short.
requirements.why: A CPH number is three parts of 2, 3 and 4 digits; boxes sized to the parts make each part easy to enter and check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-008 and repo-tests-p1-158: three boxes labelled County, Parish and Holding number, two, three and four characters wide, in the GOV.UK date input's item classes; repo-frontend-p16-011 shows a whole number typed into County is kept rather than cut short.

requirements.statement: Each CPH box has autocomplete turned off and the pattern [0-9]* as well as the numeric input mode.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets both so browsers do not offer unrelated saved values and phones show the digit keypad.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-009: each box carries inputmode numeric, pattern [0-9]*, autocomplete off and spellcheck off. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows plain text inputs with neither the pattern nor autocomplete off (trace-animals-fit-p13-014).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, each CPH box drops any non-digit as the trader types and stops at its maximum length.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the interaction designer's 9 November answer has the county parish holding boxes follow the GOV.UK date input with no JavaScript on top and drops the type-behaviour row, and the boxes are built that way; the server's checks catch a non-digit instead (req-715).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010: the CPH page uses no JavaScript and takes and saves the number with JavaScript disabled.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, pasting into a CPH box keeps only the digits and spreads them across that box and the ones after it (2, 3 then 4 digits), so pasting 123456789 or 12/345/6789 into County fills all three boxes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the interaction designer's 9 November answer has the boxes follow the GOV.UK date input with no JavaScript on top and no paste spreading, and drops the type-behaviour row. A whole number pasted into County is kept and split by the server instead (req-2122).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010 and repo-frontend-p16-011: nothing spreads a paste in the browser, and the server splits a whole number on save.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, focus moves to the next CPH box once a box is full, and Backspace in an empty box moves focus back to the previous box and deletes its last digit.
requirements.why: Out of scope: moving focus while the trader types is a change of context accessibility guidance warns against, and the interaction designer's 9 November answer has focus stay where the trader put it, with no JavaScript on the boxes at all.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010 and repo-tests-p1-164: nothing moves focus between the boxes.

requirements.statement: Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty raises no error: it saves no CPH number (clearing any saved before), the trader moves on to the consignment addresses page, and the CPH section stays incomplete, so the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader move on and holds the gap at submission instead; required-to-proceed is a design choice the prototype can express, not a constraint it cannot. The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page agrees: the CPH number is mandatory to submit, not mandatory to proceed. The 26 October ruling makes every save button on a page check the same thing as the others, which leaves this unchanged because there is nothing the page requires before the trader moves on (c-361).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-021 and repo-tests-p1-163: a blank save is allowed, nothing is saved and the trader lands back on the consignment addresses page, which still offers the add link; repo-frontend-p16-093 keeps the CPH number as one of the notification's obligations. The fit and e2e traces, earlier recordings, show the page refusing an empty save (trace-animals-fit-p13-032, trace-e2e-p6-090).

requirements.statement: A partly filled or wrongly formed CPH number is refused with one error per wrong part, in county, parish, holding order: 'Enter the county', 'Enter the parish' or 'Enter the holding number' for a missing part; 'County must be 2 digits', 'Parish must be 3 digits' or 'Holding number must be 4 digits' for a wrong length; 'County must only contain numbers', 'Parish must only contain numbers' or 'Holding number must only contain numbers' for a non-digit. Parts are trimmed first.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 silently drops a part-entered number, which loses what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-012 to repo-frontend-p16-020 hold these nine messages, and repo-frontend-p16-011-m1 trims each part before it is checked. repo-tests-p1-168 records that the end-to-end suite asserts none of them, so the coverage is the fit specs' alone.

requirements.statement: CPH errors re-render the page with every typed value kept: an error summary titled 'There is a problem' links each error to its box and moves focus there, one inline message on the whole question lists every error with a hidden 'Error:' prefix between the hint and the boxes, the group's accessible description includes the error, and every box takes the error border while none carries a message of its own.
requirements.why: A three-part question needs one message on the question, so the trader reads every part to fix in one place.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-022 and repo-frontend-p16-023: one form group carries the error class, one message holds every refusal, all three boxes take the error border, each summary link moves focus to the box it names and the typed values are kept.

requirements.statement: A stored CPH number that is not nine digits is flagged on the page with 'The saved CPH number is no longer valid. Re-enter the county, parish and holding numbers.', linked to the County box, with all three boxes shown empty.
requirements.why: Stored data can predate today's rules; the trader is told to re-enter it rather than shown stray digits.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-025 holds the message against the county box. repo-frontend-p16-035 records that no fit spec exercises it, so the message has no test behind it.

requirements.statement: The CPH page opens with three empty boxes when nothing is saved, and with the saved parts filled back in (County 12, Parish 345, Holding number 6789) when a number is saved, however the page is reached.
requirements.why: The trader can check and change what they entered.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-161 shows the three boxes empty on opening and repo-frontend-p16-026 the saved parts split back into them.

requirements.statement: The CPH page's back link always goes to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the CPH page is a step of the consignment addresses section, opened from it and returning to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-029: the Back link returns to the consignment addresses page, carrying the trail when the trader arrived with one and going to the plain addresses URL when the page was opened by its own address. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows it going to the notification overview (trace-e2e-p6-079).

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the CPH page always returns to the consignment addresses page, never on to the contact address page or the notification overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns every consignment-addresses step to the addresses page, from where 'Save and continue' moves on.
