requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-026 and repo-tests-p1-162: saving a valid number returns the trader to the consignment addresses page, which shows it as 12/345/6789. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows the opening run continuing to the contact page (trace-animals-fit-p13-026).

requirements.statement: The CPH page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, with no return-to-hub button and no cancel link.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): only pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls, and the CPH page is reached from the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-028: the page offers 'Save and continue' alone, with no 'Save and return to overview' button and no 'Cancel and return to overview' link.

requirements.statement: In the journey's first pass, 'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page goes on to the contact address page, whether or not the CPH number applies; opened from its overview task, the consignment addresses page returns to the overview instead (req-1615). The CPH page is reached only from its own link on the addresses page, never as the next step after it.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact address follows the consignment addresses, and the CPH number is one of the addresses page's sections, not a step after it. The 2026-10-09 ruling has a page opened from its overview task return to the overview, and removes the rule that Roles and addresses opened from the overview runs on to the CPH page.
requirements.deltaNote: The CPH page is already a sub-page reached from the addresses page's add link rather than a step of the linear run (repo-frontend-p16-002); no current claim shows where the addresses page's own 'Save and continue' goes, and the e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows it going to the CPH page when a CPH-triggering line exists and otherwise to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address forms, and the plants consignment contact form, post back to their own URL with a CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, and a failed save re-renders the page with status 500, the recoverable-error banner and the trader's values kept. On the plants contact page an unavailable address book raises the error rather than treating the contact as deleted or unselected.
requirements.why: Real persistence and concurrency constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-032, repo-frontend-p16-068 and repo-frontend-p16-088: each of the three animals pages answers a refused submit with 400 and a save it cannot complete with 500 and the page again in its recoverable-error state, values kept. The plants half is already built; this area's working set no longer carries the plants frontend extract, so its evidence is the 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling's plants clauses alone.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages, and the plants consignment contact page, have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA axe violations, clean and in their error states, and each radio group's description names its hint and, on error, its error.
requirements.why: The service must be accessible; the prototype does not test this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-033, repo-frontend-p16-069 and repo-frontend-p16-089: axe passes on the CPH page clean, with the whole number in County and in error; on the permanent address page clean, with a reveal open and in error; and on the contact page.

requirements.statement: Every English string changed or added on the CPH, permanent address and contact address pages, and on the plants consignment contact page, gets a Welsh version in the same change, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: These pages carry a Welsh version of every string, so a changed English string without its Welsh would leave the Welsh page wrong.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-034-m1, repo-frontend-p16-070 and repo-frontend-p16-091: each of the three pages' Welsh copy carries exactly the same key tree as its English twin, with no key missing or extra.

requirements.statement: Cats, dogs and ferrets need a permanent address; 'Other live mammals', which shares their commodity code 01061900, does not. It is asked for cats and dogs now, and the same rule takes in ferrets once the commodity catalogue holds them.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for a permanent address only for pets that APHA must be able to check, and the Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page names the same three commodities, all under the one code 01061900, so the rule needs the commodity name as well as the code. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling builds the permanent address page for cats and dogs now, and ferrets once the commodity catalogue, which waits on MDM, holds them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-047: the Permanent address section is shown for a domestic cat and absent for cattle, and repo-frontend-p16-063 keeps the page out of reach for a consignment that needs none. Ferrets are not in today's commodity catalogue, so the rule reaches them with no further change once MDM's catalogue holds them.

requirements.statement: The permanent address is its own page in the live-animals set's addresses section, opened from the consignment addresses page at a slug of its own (not the prototype's /permanent-address/select path): caption 'Addresses', heading 'Permanent address', browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and a back link to the consignment addresses page. It applies only when the consignment holds commodity 01061900 with at least one species that needs a permanent address; otherwise the page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The address fields are not asked on the animal identification form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 (and DR1 before it) asks for the permanent address as its own step, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back, instead of reopening animal identification. The 2026-10-09 ruling gives the page a real slug in the addresses section, because the prototype never decides URL paths, and the 17 November ruling words that section 'Addresses' wherever it appears.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-036 serves the page at /notifications/{journeyId}/permanent-address as a sub-page of the consignment addresses hub, repo-frontend-p16-037 shows the caption 'Addresses', the H1 and the title, repo-frontend-p16-067 the back link and repo-frontend-p16-063 the redirect when no line needs one; repo-tests-p2-045, repo-tests-p2-048 and repo-tests-p2-059 prove the address, the redirect and the Back link end to end. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows the fields inside the animal identification form (trace-e2e-p6-028).

requirements.statement: When the permanent address applies, the consignment addresses page has a 'Permanent address' section explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; for cats it has no CPH section.
requirements.why: The section is how the trader reaches the permanent address step in Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: The section and its 'Add a permanent address' link are built, shown only while a permanent address is still owed and only for a commodity that needs one (repo-tests-p2-046, repo-tests-p2-047, repo-frontend-p16-059, repo-frontend-p16-063). No current claim quotes the section's explanation or its two bullets.

requirements.statement: Once permanent addresses are saved, the consignment addresses page shows the one address with a 'Change' link when every animal is 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' or only one animal has an address; otherwise it shows the number of animals a permanent address has been added for, with a 'Change' link. Each address reads as the name, then address line 1, then the town, postcode and country separated by commas, with the country named in words. The Change link goes straight to the permanent address page.
requirements.why: The trader sees at a glance what was given for the section, without one row per animal.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-059 counts the animals that have one, shows one shared address once with a single Change link when several animals use the place of destination, and offers the add link only while one is still owed; repo-frontend-p16-060 offers each saved address with its animal's label, the choice and the country name resolved; repo-tests-p2-052 and repo-tests-p2-053 prove the read-back and the Change link end to end.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page shows the GOV.UK warning 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud', with no full stop.
requirements.why: Traders must know a false address is fraud before they give one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-038: the warning sits below the heading on the permanent address page, with no full stop.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page explains 'A permanent address is where an animal:' followed by the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', then asks 'Where will their permanent address be?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's explanation and question for the page.
requirements.deltaNote: No current claim shows the explanation or the question on the permanent address page, whose claimed content runs from the caption and heading to the warning and then straight to the animal cards (repo-frontend-p16-037, repo-frontend-p16-038, repo-frontend-p16-039). The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows the same copy on the animal identification form (trace-e2e-p6-030, trace-e2e-p6-031).

requirements.statement: The permanent address page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as the number of animals entered for that species, each headed with the species' scientific name and a running number, such as 'Felis catus 1'; species that do not need one get no cards.
requirements.why: Each animal can live at a different address, and the page asks for all of them in one place.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-039 shows one GOV.UK summary card per identified animal on a line that needs a permanent address, each a landmark region titled with the species and the animal's number, and repo-tests-p2-049 proves it end to end.

requirements.statement: Each animal card shows, in inset text, the identifiers already entered for that animal as 'label: value' (such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1'), leaving out blank ones, and no inset when none are entered.
requirements.why: The trader can tell which animal each card is for.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-040: each card shows the animal's identifiers in an inset, one line per identifier it has, reading '<identifier label>: <value>'.

requirements.statement: Each animal card has a radio group with the legend 'Select an address' and two options, 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', with neither chosen when the page first opens.
requirements.why: Most pets live at the place of destination; reusing it saves the trader typing the same address again.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-041: each card asks one question legended 'Select an address' with exactly those two options, neither pre-selected until the trader has answered; repo-tests-p2-050 proves both options end to end.

requirements.statement: Once a place of destination is given, the 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' option shows that address on one line as its hint, the party name then its address lines, such as 'Tech Imports Ltd, 18 Dockside Road, London, E14 9GE, United Kingdom', and carries no hint while the notification has no place of destination.
requirements.why: The trader sees which address they are reusing.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-042: the option is hinted with that address on one line, the party name then its address lines joined by commas, and carries no hint while there is no place of destination.

requirements.statement: The 'Enter a new address' option has the hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.'
requirements.why: It tells the trader what the permanent address means for a pet that moves on from the place of destination.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-043 carries the 48-hour hint verbatim on that option.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Enter a new address' reveals that animal's own address fields inside its card, as a GOV.UK conditional reveal.
requirements.why: The fields are only needed when the place of destination is not reused.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044: choosing 'Enter a new address' reveals the address boxes inside that card alone.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Email address' and 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code'), has no country field, and is stored with the country code GB.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 draws these eight fields and no country, and a permanent address is a Great Britain holding, so the country is saved rather than asked (c-360).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044 holds the eight boxes in that order, repo-frontend-p16-045 the phone hint and the email and phone input types, and repo-frontend-p16-046 that no country is asked and the address is stored with country code GB; repo-tests-p2-051 proves the eight labels end to end.

requirements.statement: In a new permanent address, 'Email address' comes before 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's field order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044 lists 'Email address' then 'Phone number' as the last two of the eight boxes. The e2e trace, an earlier recording of the identification form, shows phone before email (trace-e2e-p6-032).

requirements.statement: When 'Enter a new address' is chosen for an animal, its name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, email address and phone number are required, showing 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number' on the blank fields; address line 2 and county are optional.
requirements.why: The choice decides whether an address is needed, so the fields are required exactly when the trader says they will enter one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-047 holds these six messages with address line 2 and county optional, and repo-tests-p2-054 proves a blank new address is refused with HTTP 400. repo-tests-p2-062 records that only the name's message is proven end to end, so the other five rest on the fit specs.

requirements.statement: On the permanent address page, each address error in the error summary names its animal, such as 'Enter a name or organisation name for Felis catus 1' and 'Enter address line 1 for Felis catus 1', and links to the field; the inline message on the field leaves the animal out. The summary lists the refusals in card order and then each card's own field order, and a place-of-destination refusal is not animal-named.
requirements.why: With several animals' forms on one page, the summary must say which animal each error is about.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-051 names the animal in the summary and keeps the field's own message plain, repo-frontend-p16-052 orders the summary by card and field and moves focus to the control each link names, and repo-tests-p2-056 and repo-tests-p2-057 prove both forms of the message end to end.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal before a place of destination is given shows 'Add a place of destination before you can continue' on that animal's radios and in an error summary titled 'There is a problem', linked to the radios.
requirements.why: There is nothing to reuse until the place of destination exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-050 refuses that card's question with the message verbatim and logs the refusal at warn level.

requirements.statement: An animal left with no option chosen raises no error: the page saves the other animals and moves on, and the permanent address section stays incomplete until every identified animal that needs one has an address, which a notification cannot be submitted without.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader save what they know and come back; completeness is checked at the section and at submission. The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page agrees: a permanent address is mandatory to submit, and only for an animal whose commodity is cats, dogs or ferrets (c-363).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-054 saves an unanswered animal as unanswered rather than refusing it and keeps the other animals' answers, repo-frontend-p16-094 completes the task only when every identified animal that needs one holds an address, and repo-tests-p2-060 submits a cat consignment once its permanent address is answered.

requirements.statement: When the permanent address page shows errors, each animal's chosen option stays selected and a chosen 'Enter a new address' keeps its fields open with what was typed, nothing is written to the notification until every card passes its checks, and the page works the same with JavaScript and without; when the page is opened again, each animal's saved choice is selected and its saved address filled back in, the optional county included.
requirements.why: The trader never has to re-enter what they already gave, and a part-refused save never leaves half the page stored.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-053 keeps every other card's option checked and values on the page with JavaScript and without, repo-frontend-p16-053-m1 writes nothing until every card passes, repo-frontend-p16-057 fills each saved choice and address back in, and repo-tests-p2-053 and repo-tests-p2-058 prove both end to end.

requirements.statement: When no animals that need a permanent address have been identified, the permanent address page shows 'Add the number of animals on consignment details before you can continue.', with 'consignment details' linking to that page, instead of the animal cards; saving from that state saves nothing and returns to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: The cards depend on the animals identified for the line, which are given on the consignment details page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-064 shows the message with the middle words linking to the consignment details page, and repo-frontend-p16-065 saves nothing and returns to the consignment addresses page from that state.

requirements.statement: Saving 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal gives that animal the place of destination's address as its permanent address; saving 'Enter a new address' gives it the animal's own name, address lines, town or city, county, postcode, country United Kingdom, email and phone. The answer is written onto the animal's own record on its commodity line, one commit per line that holds an answered animal.
requirements.why: Each animal's permanent address must be held with the notification, whichever way it was given. The 2026-10-09 ruling keeps this behaviour and leaves its storage shape to the real service's model (c-239).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-055 writes the choice and the address onto the animal's record on its line, one commit per line, and repo-frontend-p16-056 stores a copy of the place of destination rather than a pointer to it, which is the shape the plan chose.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address keeps every field in its own place: the county is saved, and a saved address with no address line 2 opens with the town in 'Town or city' and the postcode in 'Postcode or Zip code'.
requirements.why: Persistence is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 loses the county and shifts fields on return, which the real service must not copy.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-057 fills a hand-entered address back into its own boxes, the optional county included, and repo-frontend-p16-044 keeps each box its own named field.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, which saves and returns to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): a page reached from another page, not from the task-list overview, ends with the primary button alone, like the CPH page and the party pickers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-066: the page offers 'Save and continue' alone, with no return-to-overview button and no cancel link, and saving returns the trader to the consignment addresses page.

requirements.statement: The review page shows the permanent address as one row per animal, labelled with the species' common name and number (such as 'Domestic dog 1'), whose value is that animal's saved address; with no animals identified it shows a single row 'Address'.
requirements.why: The trader checks each animal's permanent address before submitting.
requirements.deltaNote: No current claim shows the permanent address on the review page; repo-frontend-p16-060 offers each saved address to the pages that list it, with the animal's label and the country name resolved, which is what the review row needs.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own permanent-address routing is not reproduced: /permanent-address resetting the answer and redirecting to /permanent-address/select, the unused 'Are all the animals going to the place of destination?' page, and the retired /permanent-address/enter-address redirect.
requirements.why: Out of scope: these are prototype internals with no behaviour a trader sees beyond landing on the per-animal page, and the real service has none of these routes to retire.

requirements.statement: The prototype's custom heading, card and layout classes on the contact and permanent address pages, and its /design-release-2.1 mount paths, are not reproduced.
requirements.why: Out of scope: they are how the prototype is built, not behaviour a trader sees, and the real pages use GOV.UK Frontend components.

requirements.statement: The contact address page, in the animals sets and in plants, has the h1 'Contact address for consignment', no section caption, and the browser title 'Contact address for consignment - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and the service agree on the page's identity, and the plants contact page shares it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-072 heads the page 'Contact address for consignment' with no section caption above it, and repo-tests-p2-025 proves the heading end to end. The plants page already shares the heading and title; this area's working set no longer carries the plants frontend extract, so its evidence is the 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling's plants clauses alone.

requirements.statement: Directly under the contact page's heading, body text reads 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.' The plants consignment contact page shows the same text under its heading, in English and Welsh.
requirements.why: It tells the trader whose address this is; DR1 inc-046 judged the copy sentence it replaces loses nothing the trader can act on. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling has plants' contact picker take the new intro in the same increment, because plants has the same page with the same hint.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals contact page already reads the sentence directly below its heading (repo-frontend-p16-073, repo-tests-p2-026); the fit trace, an earlier recording, shows the fieldset hint 'Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification.' instead (trace-animals-fit-p12-042), and c-120 sets aside the e2e trace's record of the same hint. The plants half is still outstanding under ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-043.

requirements.statement: Below the intro, the contact page has the sub-heading 'Select an address' (an h2), and the radios' fieldset legend 'Select an address' is visually hidden, so the page has exactly two headings and the h1 is not the radios legend. The plants consignment contact page shows the same 'Select an address' sub-heading above its results, in English and Welsh.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's page structure: a heading for the page and a heading for the choice. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling gives plants' contact picker the same heading.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals contact page already puts its choice under the 'Select an address' sub-heading and repeats that text as a visually hidden legend, leaving exactly two headings (repo-frontend-p16-074, repo-tests-p2-025). The plants half is still outstanding under ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-043.

requirements.statement: Under 'Select an address', the contact page says 'If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page.', with 'add a new branch address' as the link to add an address.
requirements.why: The contact must be one of the trader's own branches, so the page tells them how to add a missing branch.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-085 and repo-tests-p2-036: outside stub mode the page carries that sentence with the middle words as the add link. An earlier e2e recording showed an 'Add a new address' paragraph link above the heading instead, and c-120 sets that claim aside.

requirements.statement: The contact page's add link opens the address book's add-address page asking for an address that holds the branch address role, and the address book returns the trader to the contact page when the address is saved.
requirements.why: The new address must hold the branch address role to appear in the contact list, and the copy promises a return to this page. The 5 November ruling renames the address book's stored 'use' to 'role', so the add page sets a role rather than a type.
requirements.deltaNote: The link into the INS address book's add-address page and the return to the contact page are built (repo-frontend-p16-085, repo-frontend-p16-086, repo-tests-p2-036, which shows journey-type=gbn-ag on the link). No claim shows the add page being asked for the branch address role, and the fields it collects are the address book's own, County included (ruling-paul-2026-10-14-p1-004).

requirements.statement: Back on the contact page after adding a branch address, the new address is in the list, selected as the contact address, and the page shows the success banner '<name> address added to your address book' once.
requirements.why: The trader added the address to use it here, so it is chosen for them and they are told it was saved.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-086 shows the banner verbatim, once, on return from the address book. No claim shows the new address selected for the trader on that return.

requirements.statement: Coming back from the address book add with a not-found error, the contact page shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.' in the error summary; with an unavailable error it shows 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.' and the recoverable-error state.
requirements.why: The round trip to the address book crosses services and can fail; the prototype cannot express that.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-087 holds both messages, shown as an error summary against the choice.

requirements.statement: When the animals frontend runs in stub mode, the contact page offers no link to add an address.
requirements.why: Stub mode has no address book to add to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-085 and repo-tests-p2-035: in stub mode the page offers no way to add an address at all.

requirements.statement: The contact page offers only the signed-in organisation's address-book records that can play the branch address role, newest added first, and no record that cannot; a record held only for a consignment role such as consignor is not offered as a contact and is still offered in that role's own party picker.
requirements.why: The contact is the trader's own branch responsible for the consignment in Great Britain; offering overseas consignors and other parties is a live defect DR1 recorded. The 5 November ruling makes the branch address one of the six roles an address holds, so the list asks the address book for that role.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-075 offers one radio per record that can play the branch-address role and no record that cannot; repo-tests-p2-037, repo-tests-p2-038 and repo-tests-p2-039 prove the ordering, the exclusion of a consignor-only record and that the same record is still offered in the consignor picker. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows every record in the book offered, overseas ones included (trace-e2e-p7-014).

requirements.statement: Each contact address radio is labelled with the address's name and has its address line, town or city and postcode, joined with commas, as its hint, ending at the postcode with no country, such as '15 Union Street, Aberdeen, AB11 5BN'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's hint; branch addresses are all in Great Britain, so the country adds nothing.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-076 and repo-tests-p2-029: the hint joins the address line, town or city and postcode with commas and ends at the postcode. The fit and e2e traces, earlier recordings, show the country on the end (trace-animals-fit-p12-046, trace-e2e-p7-011).

requirements.statement: The contact addresses are offered as radios whose value is the address record's id, with no search box and no manual entry of its own.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and the service agree: the contact is picked from the address book by its record, and new contacts come only through the address book.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-077 and repo-tests-p2-044: a plain radio group with no search box; repo-tests-p2-037-m1 keys each radio on the address-book record's own id. How many are shown at once is req-2312.

requirements.statement: No contact address is chosen when the page first opens; on return, the saved contact's radio is selected while it still matches a record in the list, and no radio is selected once that record is no longer offered. The plants consignment contact page does the same.
requirements.why: The trader makes the choice, and sees it again when they come back.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-084 shows the saved contact checked on reopening and leaves every option unchecked once the record it was picked from is no longer offered; repo-tests-p2-030, repo-tests-p2-032 and repo-tests-p2-040 prove all three states end to end. The plants half is already built; this area's working set no longer carries the plants frontend extract.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the contact page with no address chosen shows 'Select a contact address' in the error summary and on the radios, linked to the first radio, and saves nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 requires the contact address before the trader moves on to review, and the Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page marks the user-created contact address mandatory to proceed and has the trader select one where more than one address exists. The 26 October ruling puts the same check on the second save button (req-2187).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-079 keeps the trader on the page with that message in the summary and against the options, and repo-tests-p2-033 and repo-tests-p2-041 prove it end to end, the second after the chosen record has been deleted. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows a blank save allowed with no error (trace-e2e-p7-024).

requirements.statement: Submitting a contact that the organisation's address book does not hold, holds as deleted or holds without the branch address role shows 'Select a contact address' in the error summary and on the radios, answers 400, selects no radio and saves nothing; the error link focuses the first radio.
requirements.why: A forged or stale choice must not be saved.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-080 refuses all three cases with the same message, leaves no option chosen and moves focus to the first radio.

requirements.statement: In the journey's first pass, reached from the consignment addresses page, choosing a contact address and pressing 'Save and continue' saves it and goes to the review page ('Review your notification'). Opened from its overview task or from the review page, the contact page returns there instead (req-768). In plants, where the contact page is the opening run's last step, saving it in the opening run likewise goes on to plants' review page, even when the notification is incomplete.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact address is the last step before review. The 2026-10-09 ruling has a page opened from its overview task return to the overview on 'Save and continue', so only the first pass goes on to review. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling has plants' opening run end on its review page too.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-031: choosing a contact and pressing Save and continue already goes on to the draft's check-your-answers review in the animals frontend, which repo-frontend-p16-083 records as the notification view. The plants half is still outstanding under ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-025; this area's working set no longer carries the plants frontend extract.

requirements.statement: The contact page's back link goes to the consignment addresses page, or to the review page when the page was opened from review.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact page follows the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-089: the contact page's Back link returns to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: Opened from its overview task ('Contact address for this consignment'; 'Contact address for consignment' in plants), the contact page returns to the overview on 'Save and continue' as well as on the return-to-hub button, with the task then shown complete; opened from the review page, it returns to the review after saving.
requirements.why: A trader changing one answer goes back to where they started; the 2026-10-09 ruling has every page opened from its overview task return to the overview on 'Save and continue' (req-1615), and plants already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-032: a contact saved with 'Save and return to hub' is still shown as chosen when the trader comes back from the overview task, and saving again from that state keeps the choice; trace-e2e-p7-022 and trace-e2e-p7-030 show the return to the overview.

requirements.statement: Outside amend, the contact page, in the animals sets and in plants, ends with all three controls: 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to hub' side by side in one button group, and 'Cancel and return to hub' on its own line below them.
requirements.why: The hub's task list links to the contact page, so under DR1's inc-161 rule (b) it keeps the three return controls, as Design Release 2.1 shows.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-081 and repo-tests-p2-027: the three controls are laid out that way and already read 'hub' rather than 'overview'. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows them labelled 'overview' (trace-animals-fit-p12-049). The plants half is already built; this area's working set no longer carries the plants frontend extract.

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, the contact, CPH and permanent address pages show the amend controls: 'Save and return' (to the review page) and a secondary 'Save and continue', with no return-to-hub button or cancel link; the plants consignment contact page takes the same two buttons in the same increment. None of them carries a cancel-amend dialog: cancelling the amendment is the Amend bar's 'Cancel amend', which opens the cancel amendment confirmation page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends an amending trader back to review rather than to the hub. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling keeps the amend and cancel confirmations as pages and has plants' pickers take the same amend buttons; the interaction designer's 9 November answer then drops the prototype's amend and cancel pop-ups outright, the CPH page's cancel-amend dialog among them, rather than holding them for design (c-190, c-289).
requirements.deltaNote: No claim shows any of these pages in an amend.

requirements.statement: The contact address task is reached from the hub row 'Contact address for this consignment' under '6. Contact address', is open at any time without the consignment addresses being done, and shows 'To do' until a contact is saved and 'Complete' after.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and the service agree the contact is not gated on the other sections.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p12-039, trace-animals-fit-p12-040 and trace-e2e-p7-004 show the row, its states and that it is not gated; repo-frontend-p16-071 keeps the page a step of the linear run that collects the notification's contact address.

requirements.statement: A notification cannot be submitted without a contact address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 requires the contact address, and the consignment addresses, before submission.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-092 makes the contact address one of the notification's obligations, bound to the single field the page collects, but no claim shows a submit refused without one.

requirements.statement: Choosing a contact, in the animals sets and in plants, saves a copy of that address's name and address into the notification, remembering which record it came from, and replaces any contact saved before; the held copy stays valid, and the task complete, even if the address-book record later changes or is deleted.
requirements.why: Copy semantics is a real persistence and cross-service constraint: the address book is another service, and a submitted notification must keep the address it was submitted with.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-083 stores a copy of the record and keeps the id it was picked from, and repo-tests-p2-042 shows the overview task staying 'Complete' and the notification's Contact address row still naming the address after the record is deleted; repo-frontend-p16-096 is the held-contact fixture the feature tests with. The plants half is already built; this area's working set no longer carries the plants frontend extract.

requirements.statement: The contact page shows the radios list alone, with the current contact pre-selected, and no 'Current contact address' summary card or 'Edit details' link: the only way to alter the answer is to choose a different option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's contact page has no such card and the prototype wins on look and feel; no DR1 judgement covers it, and the 2026-10-09 ruling leaves c-125 unchanged. What happens to the edit route the card linked to is c-241.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-090: the page offers no control to change, edit or remove the address it has chosen. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows a 'Current contact address' card with an 'Edit details' link below the radios (trace-e2e-p7-026), which c-125 sets aside.

requirements.statement: The contact edit route (/consignment/contact/edit) and its edit form stay in the service: saving it changes only this notification's copy of the contact, leaves the address-book record unchanged and adds no record. No page links to it: the contact page shows the radios alone (req-774) and the review drops its 'Edit details' links (c-138), and no new link is added until a later ruling or design names an entry point.
requirements.why: The 2026-10-09 ruling keeps the contact edit route, because removing it to match the prototype would be an architecture change the prototype cannot decide; which links a page offers is look and feel, and Design Release 2.1 offers no way to edit the chosen contact (c-241).
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p8-077 to trace-e2e-p8-080 show the route editing only this notification's copy. The contact feature's current extract covers the page alone and names no edit route (repo-frontend-p16-071 to repo-frontend-p16-096), so nothing says the route has gone.

requirements.statement: The prototype's three seeded branch addresses (Aberdeen Livestock Ltd, West Country Livestock Ltd, Cymru Animal Imports Ltd) and their mismatched radio values are not reproduced; the real list comes from the organisation's address book.
requirements.why: Out of scope: they are prototype data, not the trader's own branches.

requirements.statement: The notification hub's browser title is 'Overview - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and its main heading is 'Overview'.
requirements.why: The hub is the top of the notification in Design Release 2.1, named Overview.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-003 and trace-animals-fit-p4-002 show the title and the extra-large 'Overview' heading today.

requirements.statement: Each live-animals notification has its own hub page in the live-animals set, addressed by the notification at the set's own notification path (/live-animals/notifications/{reference}).
requirements.why: The real service stores many notifications per trader, so the hub must say which one it shows; the prototype holds a single notification in its session and cannot express this, and the prototype never decides URL paths.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-001 serves the hub per notification under the live-animals set, and repo-tests-p3-066 proves it end to end; c-128 keeps it over the prototype's single /notification-hub route for whichever notification is in the session.

requirements.statement: Above the 'Overview' heading the hub shows the notification's status as a tag ('Draft' until it is submitted) followed by the notification reference, which the notification already has before any task is answered, in the form 'GBN-AG-', a two-digit year, a hyphen and six upper-case letters or digits (for example GBN-AG-26-DGWJ47).
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are on and what state it is in.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-061 and trace-animals-fit-p4-003 show the shared journey strip with a 'Draft' tag and the reference above the heading today, and trace-animals-fit-p4-004 shows every reference already in the GBN-AG-26-XXXXXX form from the first page; trace-animals-fit-p4-066 records that no trace shows the hub for a notification that is no longer a draft.

requirements.statement: Opening the hub leaves the notification saved as a draft: nothing a trader has answered is lost by leaving from the hub.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the draft when the hub opens; the real service already saves each page's answers to the notification record as it goes.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-044-m1 shows every saved page committing to the stored notification (the concurrency token rises per save), so the draft is already saved whenever the hub shows.

requirements.statement: While a submitted notification is being amended (status 'Amend'), the hub's status line also shows a 'Cancel amend' link-style control, which goes to the cancel-amendment confirmation page the review page uses. The control comes from the shared status strip, so the live-animals, germinal-products and high-risk plants Overview pages all show it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's shared status line offers Cancel amend on every page that includes it, and the hub's missing modal include is a prototype omission; the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the Amend bar's 'Cancel amend' going to a confirmation page rather than a pop-up, changes it in the shared strip because every set that amends needs it, and holds the pop-up back as a waiting-on-design question. Building it in the shared strip means the plants Overview needs no work of its own.
requirements.deltaNote: The real hub's strip shows only the tag and reference (repo-frontend-p5-061), and the plants hub offers no cancel-amendment link at all (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-008); cancel amend is offered today only from the review page and the dashboard. Built by the shared strip change, which reaches every set's hub at once.

requirements.statement: The hub has no back link; the ways off it are the 'Return to dashboard' button and the service navigation.
requirements.why: The hub is the top of the notification, not a step in it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-060 and trace-animals-fit-p4-005 show no back link on the hub today.

requirements.statement: The hub shows a 'Your commodities' heading (h2) above the commodity total cards, on every visit, including before any commodity is chosen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens the hub with the consignment totals.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-005 and trace-animals-fit-p4-007 show the 'Your commodities' h2 from the first visit today.

requirements.statement: For a live-animals notification the first card shows the total number of animals, labelled 'Animals' with the caption 'Total number of animals in this consignment'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for the animals total card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-007 and trace-animals-fit-p4-008 show the 'Animals' label and caption verbatim today, and trace-animals-fit-p4-013 shows the entered count appearing in the card.

requirements.statement: The hub shows a card for the total number of packages, labelled 'Packages/boxes' with the caption 'Total number of packages in this consignment'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for the packages total card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-008 and trace-animals-fit-p4-009 show the 'Packages/boxes' label and caption verbatim today.

requirements.statement: A commodity total card reads '0' when its total is not above zero, and the animals and packages totals add up only the counts saved against the commodity lines that are in scope for the notification, a blank or non-numeric count adding nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only positive entries, so a card never shows a negative or odd total, and a line the notification no longer covers must not be counted.
requirements.deltaNote: Already met: the totals sum the in-scope lines' counts (repo-frontend-p5-009, repo-frontend-p5-014-m1), a blank or non-numeric count is treated as nothing (repo-frontend-p5-010), and both cards read 0 before any line exists and while a chosen commodity still owes its numbers (repo-frontend-p5-011, trace-animals-fit-p4-011, trace-animals-fit-p4-012, trace-e2e-p13-015). The validation on the commodity details page that keeps a zero, negative or fractional count out of the record belongs to the commodity-details area, not to the hub.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the hub's 'Your commodities' shows the 'Packages/boxes' card and a weight card labelled 'Kilograms' with the caption 'Total weight of packages in this consignment', and no 'Animals' card.
requirements.why: Germinal products are counted by packages and weight, not by animals, in Design Release 2.1; each set holds one category, so the germinal hub never mixes in an animals count.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists today, and the only hub always shows the Animals and Packages/boxes cards (trace-animals-fit-p4-008) with no weight card. Built in the germinal set's copy of the hub.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the 'Kilograms' card totals the gross weight in kilograms entered for the consignment, and shows '0' when the total is not a positive number, a whole number as entered, and otherwise the total rounded to 3 decimal places (for example '2.5').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's rule for displaying the weight total; the weight the germinal set holds is a total gross weight in kilograms, as a decimal.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set or weight card exists today.

requirements.statement: Each commodity total card is a static panel (no link or button) that reads the number, then the label, then the caption, with the number and the label larger than the caption and the caption wrapping to no more than two lines; the cards sit side by side on a wide screen and stack with no horizontal scrolling on a 360px screen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the totals as value, label and caption tiles; the real hub already draws them that way from GOV.UK design tokens, because no GOV.UK Frontend component renders such a panel.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-006 and repo-frontend-p5-012 to p5-014, with trace-animals-fit-p4-014 to p4-018, show static number-label-caption panels, side by side and stacking on a small screen, built as a custom block from GOV.UK tokens, today.
