requirements.statement: The Main import reason card shows 'Destination country' for transhipment or onward travel, 'Exit date' and 'Port of exit' for temporary admission horses, and no exit rows for a reason that asks none; a port reads back by its label, falling back to the stored port code when reference data has no label for it.
requirements.why: Both sources show the exit answers only where the reason asked for them, and a port with no label must still be readable.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-041, p6-042 and p6-043 show each exit row only when asked and read a port back by its label.

requirements.statement: On an editable review each card's Change link opens the page that collected that card's answers, pre-filled, and saving there returns the trader to the review.
requirements.why: Both sources link each card to its page, and Design Release 2.1 returns the trader to the review rather than pushing them onward through the journey.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every Change link from the review carries the review as its return marker, but after saving the changed page the trader goes on to the journey's next page rather than back to the review (repo-frontend-p6-084, repo-frontend-p6-082-m1).
requirements.blockedBy: The EUDPA-774 save and continue work must merge first: the 10 November ruling holds the return links until it lands, because the two changes touch the same save path.

requirements.statement: Each Change link names its card for screen readers in visually hidden text (for example 'Change origin of import', 'Change commodity <card title>').
requirements.why: The real frontend does this for accessibility and Design Release 2.1 shows nothing against it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-082 names the nine hidden Change labels in card order and repo-tests-p3-052 asserts two of them.

requirements.statement: '2. Description of the goods' has one card per commodity, holding one block per species headed with the species name, and the card's header Change link goes to that commodity's details page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups species under their commodity.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-045 gives one card per commodity group and p6-048 one species block per line inside it.

requirements.statement: A commodity card's species block for live animals shows 'Number of animals' and no 'Commodity code', 'Common name' or 'Species' rows.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reads those three answers back in the What are you importing? card instead.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-049: a species block's first row is 'Number of animals', and p6-134 reads the stored count back as digits.

requirements.statement: Where packaging applies to a species, its block shows a 'Number of packages (when required)' row, reading 'Not applicable' when blank.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels the packaging row 'Number of packages (when required)'.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-050 adds the row only for a commodity code that asks for a package count, and p6-086 reads a blank back as 'Not applicable'.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set's review, each species block shows 'Total gross weight' as '<n> kg' (the total gross weight in kilograms, which may be a decimal) and 'Number of packages'; the first block of the first commodity card shows a 'Temperature' row, which always shows because the germinal set always asks for temperature; and identification details read back as a list of each identifier field and its saved value.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reads germinal product answers back this way, and the 9 October ruling builds this content in the germinal set's copy of the review.
requirements.deltaNote: The germinal products set has its own root (repo-tests-p3-110) but no review of its own, and the live-animals species block carries no gross weight, temperature or germinal identification rows (repo-frontend-p6-049, p6-050).

requirements.statement: On an editable review, the first row of each species block carries its own Change link to the commodity details page, as well as the card's header Change link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts a row-level Change link on the first row of each species block.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-049: the 'Number of animals' row carries its own Change link reading 'Change number of animals for <species>'.

requirements.statement: A live-animal species block's identifier table is headed 'Identification details', marked up as a GOV.UK heading one level below the species heading, with its own Change link to the animal identification page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the table 'Identification details', and the 19 November ruling makes it a real heading in a sensible hierarchy under the species heading rather than bold body text.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-051: the block shows an 'Identification details' heading one level below the species heading, with its own Change link.

requirements.statement: Each row of the identification table is labelled with the species name and the animal's number (for example 'Felis catus 1'), under an 'Animal' column, with one column per identifier field in scope that at least one animal has a value for.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels each animal by species and number.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-052: the first column is headed 'Animal' and names each animal '<species display name> <number from 1>'.

requirements.statement: On an editable review, Identification details carries its own Change link to the animal identification page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader change identifiers straight from the review.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-051: the Identification details heading carries a Change link reading 'Change identification details for <species>'.

requirements.statement: A species with no saved identifiers shows no identification details, and identifier columns follow the order the identification page asks for them, using the same labels.
requirements.why: Both sources agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-053 leaves the heading and table out for a species with no identified animals, and p6-052 takes the columns from the identifier fields in scope.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, pets' permanent addresses read back in the Consignment addresses card as a 'Permanent address' subsection, one entry per animal labelled by that animal, with the full address and its country, and the identifier table has no Permanent address column; an animal with no permanent address contributes no entry and no saved addresses at all leaves the subsection out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows permanent addresses with the consignment addresses, in full.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-077: the card ends with a 'Permanent address' subsection, one row per animal that has one.

requirements.statement: The additional details card is titled 'Additional details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles the card 'Additional details'.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-045: the Description of the goods section ends with the 'Additional details' card.

requirements.statement: The Additional details card shows only when it has a row to show, and carries a Change link only when the additional details page is part of the journey.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides an empty card and does not link to a page the journey skips.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card always stands at the end of the section and is marked 'Complete additional details' when its task row is not ready (repo-frontend-p6-045, repo-frontend-p6-094).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the Additional details card shows 'Certified for' with the certification purpose when that question applies, and 'Includes unweaned animals' reading Yes or No when that question applies.
requirements.why: Both sources show the same rows. Each set holds one category, so a live-animals notification never reads 'Germinal products' here.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-054 and p6-055 already show both rows, and repo-tests-p3-014 and p3-015 assert them.

requirements.statement: The Arrival details card labels the arrival date row 'Arrival date at port of entry'.
requirements.why: The 17 November ruling settles the arrival date's wording as 'Arrival date at port of entry' everywhere, check your answers included.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-057 lists 'Arrival date at port of entry' as the card's second row.

requirements.statement: The Arrival details card shows 'Port of entry', the arrival date, 'Means of transport to the port of entry', 'Transport identification' and 'Transport document reference', with dates written day/month/year without leading zeros and a blank date left blank.
requirements.why: Both sources agree on these rows and the date form.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-057 gives the five rows in that order and p6-044 writes every date as day/month/year with no leading zeros.

requirements.statement: The review reads the means of transport back with the option labels the transport page offers, for example 'Air'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows 'Air' where the real review shows 'Airplane'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review maps the stored values to 'Airplane', 'Railway', 'Road Vehicle' and 'Vessel' (trace-animals-fit-p25-036, trace-e2e-p13-061); repo-frontend-p6-057 names the row but says nothing about the mapping.

requirements.statement: When transit countries apply, they read back inside the Arrival details card as a 'Transit countries' subsection with the row 'Countries that the consignment will travel through' (comma-separated, in the order added), and that row carries its own Change link to the transit countries page; there is no separate Transit countries card.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps transit countries inside Arrival details with a row-level Change link, which settles the card-structure question DR1 parity row inc-146 left open.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-058: the Arrival details card ends with a 'Transit countries' sub-heading holding that row with its own Change link.

requirements.statement: The Transport details card always shows 'Name', 'Address', 'Country', 'Approval number' and 'Type', writing an empty answer as 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists every transporter row.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-060 gives the card five rows in that order, and p6-062 and p6-063 read a missing address or approval number back as 'Not applicable'.

requirements.statement: The Transport details card shows the transporter's address one part per line, the transporter's stored country, and the transporter type as recorded; the transporter read back is the commercial one when that answer is in scope and the private one when that one is.
requirements.why: The real service holds the transporter's country; the prototype's guess from the approval-number prefix is a stand-in the real data replaces.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-062 lists the address lines one per line, p6-063 reads the stored country back as entered and p6-060-m1 reads the type back as it is held.

requirements.statement: Each uploaded document has its own card in '4. Uploaded documents', titled 'Document <n>' in upload order, whose header Change link opens the accompanying documents page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives every document its own card with its own Change link.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-064 and p6-067 give each document its own card and Change link, and repo-tests-p3-047 asserts the card titles.

requirements.statement: Each document card shows 'Document reference', 'Document type', 'Date of issue' and 'Attachment', where Attachment is the uploaded file's name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the attached file's name.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-065 gives the four rows in that order with the file name as the Attachment value.

requirements.statement: With no documents uploaded, '4. Uploaded documents' shows a single 'Document 1' card whose 'Document reference' reads 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's empty state.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-066 shows the single 'Document 1' card with 'Not applicable', and repo-tests-p3-048 asserts it.

requirements.statement: A document's type reads back by its full name, for example 'ITAHC (Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate)'.
requirements.why: Both sources show the full document type name.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-065 shows the type's label and repo-tests-p3-049 asserts the full name on a submitted notification.

requirements.statement: '5. Addresses' holds one card titled 'Consignment addresses' with a single header Change link to the addresses page.
requirements.why: The 17 November ruling settles the card title as 'Consignment addresses', the same words as the page's own heading and the overview's task row, and Design Release 2.1 gives the card one header link.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-068 holds one 'Consignment addresses' card and p6-082 gives it one Change link; repo-tests-p3-114 finds the card by that title.

requirements.statement: The Consignment addresses card has one row per consignment role (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) and a 'County parish holding (CPH) number' row only when a chosen commodity asks for one.
requirements.why: Both sources show the same role rows and conditional CPH row.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-068 gives the five role rows in that order and p6-076 adds the CPH row only when a commodity asks for one.

requirements.statement: The CPH number reads back with its parts separated by slashes, for example '12/345/6789'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 writes the CPH as 12/345/6789.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the parts are run together, '123456789' (trace-animals-fit-p25-041, trace-e2e-p13-072); repo-frontend-p6-076 says only that the row shows the CPH as it is displayed.

requirements.statement: Party rows and the contact address row on the review carry no 'Edit details' row action; the Consignment addresses and Contact address cards' header Change links are their only links.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the Addresses card one header link and no row actions.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an answered party row carries an 'Edit details' link (repo-frontend-p6-070 withholds it only from a party with no name) and the contact address row carries one that opens the contact party's edit page and returns to the review (repo-frontend-p6-079, p6-080); repo-tests-p3-113 records the page object that reads it.

requirements.statement: A trader who changes the CPH number from the review's Consignment addresses card is returned to the review after saving, not sent onward through the journey.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reaches the CPH from the card's one link; DR1 parity row inc-146 recorded that the real route pushes the trader onward.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a change made from the review goes on to the journey's next page rather than back to the review (repo-frontend-p6-084, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p8-044).
requirements.blockedBy: The EUDPA-774 save and continue work must merge first: the 10 November ruling holds the return links until it lands.

requirements.statement: '6. Contact address' holds one card titled 'Contact address' with a single 'Contact address' row and a header Change link to the consignment contact select page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles the card 'Contact address', which also ends the heading repeated twice that DR1 parity row inc-147 flagged.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-078 holds one 'Contact address' card with a single row of the same name, and p6-081 gives it its Change link.

requirements.statement: On a finished card or a read-only review, an empty answer reads 'Not applicable', and a free-text answer the trader typed as 'Not applicable' is kept.
requirements.why: Both sources write blanks as 'Not applicable'.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-086: a row whose answer is blank because it does not apply reads 'Not applicable'.

requirements.statement: Inside a card that still has answers outstanding, every empty row shows no visible text and tells screen readers 'Missing'.
requirements.why: Both sources mark missing answers this way, so an outstanding answer does not read as one that does not apply.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-087 shows the hidden 'Missing' in place of 'Not applicable', and repo-tests-p3-016 asserts it.

requirements.statement: An unfinished card is styled as an error card and shows its message under its title, prefixed for screen readers with 'Error:'.
requirements.why: Both sources mark unfinished cards this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-088 shows the message as an error paragraph inside the card, prefixed by a visually hidden 'Error:', with the card given an error style.

requirements.statement: An editable review of an unfinished notification shows a 'There is a problem' error summary as soon as it opens, with one 'Complete <card title in lower case>' entry per unfinished card linking to that card's own place on the page, the same words inside the card, and 'Error: ' before the page title; the cards are checked and listed in page order.
requirements.why: Both sources name what is left before the trader presses Continue.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-101 and p6-100 name every unfinished card in page order with the same message on the card, repo-frontend-p6-118 shows it after a refused Continue and repo-tests-p3-012 and p3-036 pin the six entries and the 'Error: ' title prefix.

requirements.statement: An unfinished Origin of import card's message is 'Complete origin of import'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's message follows the card title.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-089: the card shows 'Complete origin of import' against the origin-of-import anchor.

requirements.statement: An unfinished Main import reason card's message is 'Complete main import reason'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's message.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-091 and repo-tests-p3-013: the message reads 'Complete main import reason'.

requirements.statement: An unfinished Additional details card's message is 'Complete additional details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's message, asserted by its specs.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-094 and repo-tests-p3-014: the message reads 'Complete additional details'.

requirements.statement: The unfinished-card messages 'Complete arrival details', 'Complete transport details' and 'Complete contact address for this consignment' stay as they are.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps these three messages, even though it renames the cards they sit on. The addresses card's message is its own requirement, because the 17 November ruling changed it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-095, p6-096 and p6-099 already use these three messages, and repo-tests-p3-012 asserts them.

requirements.statement: When no commodity has been selected, the What are you importing? card is marked unfinished with 'Complete what are you importing?', and the error summary links to it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names a missing commodity selection against its own card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-090: the card shows 'Complete what are you importing?' against the what-are-you-importing anchor.

requirements.statement: When the consignment details or the animal identification are incomplete, the error summary shows 'Complete commodity details', linking to the first commodity card, and falls back to the section heading when no commodity card is on the page; commodity cards themselves are not marked as error cards.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names incomplete consignment details as 'Complete commodity details' and never marks a commodity card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-092 reports 'Complete commodity details' against the commodity-details anchor with the section heading as its fallback, p6-046 puts that anchor on the first commodity card and p6-093 keeps the message off the cards.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, when more than one species is selected and identifiers are required, the review names each short species: 'Enter the number of animals for <species>' when it has no count, and 'Enter at least 1 animal identifier for <species>' when it has a count but no identifier, with the species name in lower case, in commodity line order, each entry linking to that species block and moving focus to it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 settles the per-species marking that DR1 parity row inc-150 deferred for a design ruling. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement by set; the germinal set's wording is its own requirement.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-105, p6-106 and p6-107 give both messages, in line order, each linking to the species block and moving focus to it.

requirements.statement: Transit countries are optional for submission: the review never marks them unfinished on their own account and an empty transit-countries answer does not stop Continue, reading back as 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats transit countries as optional.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-059: a draft by road with no transit country reads the row back as 'Not applicable', shows no 'Complete arrival details' message and continues to the declaration.

requirements.statement: Uploaded documents are optional to proceed and to submit: the trader can pass the upload documents step without adding one, and a notification with none can be submitted.
requirements.why: Both sources treat documents as optional.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p3-022 and p3-026 submit a notification with no document and then with one, and trace-animals-fit-p26-038 submits with none.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, a notification is complete enough to submit when origin, commodity selection, consignment details, import reason, additional details, arrival, transport, consignment addresses and contact address are complete, and, when more than one species is selected, every species has at least one identified animal record, a record counting as identified once one identifier is filled; the review's 'nothing unfinished' verdict uses exactly this test.
requirements.why: Both sources gate submission on the same sections, with identifiers required only for multiple species.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-115 and p6-139 make readiness one test that refuses Continue, and p6-105 sets the identifier bar per species.

requirements.statement: The trader reaches the review from the overview's 'Review and submit' and a submitted notification's view from the notification list's View link; Continue on an unfinished notification re-shows the review with its errors and a 400 status, and Continue on a complete one goes to the declaration page.
requirements.why: Both sources behave this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-117 keeps the trader on the review after a refusal, p6-124 posts Continue on to the declaration, and repo-tests-p3-064, p3-054 and p3-056 drive both paths.

requirements.statement: The review names a rejected document on every visit and a document still being scanned once Continue is refused, and either message stops Continue and the declaration submit.
requirements.why: The virus scan is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-112 marks a rejected document's card as soon as the review opens, p6-113 holds the still-scanning message until Continue is refused and p7-041 refuses the declaration for a document still being scanned.

requirements.statement: An unanswered consignment role makes the Consignment addresses card unfinished, so the review's error summary carries the single 'Complete consignment addresses' entry linking to that card and names no party separately; a role the trader has not answered is never reported as an address error.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's summary has one entry per unfinished card and DR1 made no judgement here (inc-150 deferred it); keeping the card entry means a second unanswered role in the same card is never hidden (c-135).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-073 checks only answered roles and p6-098 gives the card the single 'Complete consignment addresses' message, which repo-tests-p3-012 pins in the full six-entry list.

requirements.statement: The review's error summary takes focus only after a refused Continue, not on a plain visit, and every card and section heading can take focus from a summary link.
requirements.why: The real frontend does this so a plain visit does not pull focus from the heading; Design Release 2.1 shows nothing against it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-121 takes focus only after a refusal and repo-tests-p3-065 proves focus moving to the summary on a second refused Continue.

requirements.statement: A draft review ends with 'Continue' alone, with nothing after it, its Delete being the warning control in the view header.
requirements.why: A draft's review carries the view header (c-246), whose Delete gives the trader the action Design Release 2.1 draws beside Continue on its header-less journey review.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-122 ends a draft review with Continue alone, p6-016 and p6-021 put 'Delete notification' in the header, and repo-tests-p3-053 and p3-040 assert both.

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, the review ends with three actions in order: 'Continue' (submits), a secondary 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel-amendment confirmation, and a red 'Delete' control leading to the delete confirmation.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers 'Cancel amend' as a button beside Continue. What the confirmation does is the manage-notifications area's.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-123 ends an amendment review with Continue, Cancel amend and Delete notification, and repo-tests-p3-057 asserts that order.

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, the review is headed and titled 'Review your notification' when first opened, and 'Review before re-submitting' once any answer differs from the submitted version; putting a changed answer back returns the heading to 'Review your notification', and a fresh amendment raised after a cancelled one opens with that heading too.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader they are about to resubmit.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-005 and p6-006 switch the heading and title on whether the amendment's answers differ from the submitted version.

requirements.statement: An amendment's review opens with no error summary and no card errors; if the trader presses Continue on an amendment that is not complete, it is refused and the re-shown review names the card that is missing an answer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides errors on an amendment's review, but real validation must still refuse an incomplete resubmission and say why.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-119 holds every answer error silently on an amendment until Continue is refused, and p6-120 then reveals the summary.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification's view shows the review page header in place of the journey heading: the notification reference as the h1, with the status tag 'Submitted' beside it and no caption above. The header is keyed on the real route and the stored status, and is drawn in the set's own review template with the shared status strip switched off; the shared layout is not changed.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads a viewed notification with its reference and status; the 9 October ruling keeps that content without the prototype's query-string lookup, and the 16 November ruling settles the tag as 'Submitted'.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-003, p6-011 and p6-012 head a submitted notification by its reference with a 'Submitted' tag and no journey strip, and repo-tests-p3-033 and p3-062 assert it.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification's view has the page title '<reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', a draft's unfinished view is titled 'Error: <reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and the journey review of an amendment keeps 'Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: A page title names the page before the service, a GOV.UK accessibility duty that overrides Design Release 2.1's title with no page name (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p3-037 and p3-036 assert both titles, and repo-frontend-p6-003 makes the reference the browser title for a draft and a submitted notification.

requirements.statement: Under its header, a submitted notification's view shows 'Date submitted: <d Month yyyy>' from the notification's stored submission instant, naming the day in the service's own time zone with the month in full, and shows no date line at all when the notification holds no submission instant.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 dates every viewed notification; the real service shows its stored date rather than the prototype's fallback to today.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-014 and p6-013-m1 show 'Date submitted' from the stored instant in the service's time zone, p6-015 leaves the line out when there is none, and repo-tests-p3-039 proves it survives a reload.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification's view header shows a primary 'Amend this notification' button, and a draft's header shows none.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers amend from the viewed notification; what the button opens is the manage-notifications area's.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-017 offers Amend first on a submitted notification, p6-016 withholds it from a draft, and repo-tests-p3-041 and p3-040 assert both.

requirements.statement: A notification's view header offers 'Copy as new': a secondary button beside 'Amend this notification' when that shows, otherwise the default button. It reuses the shared notification actions wording 'Copy as new'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Copy as new on every viewed notification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-016, p6-017 and p6-018 offer it on a draft and on a submitted notification with the styling switching on whether Amend is there, and repo-tests-p3-061 proves it copies into a new draft.

requirements.statement: A notification's view header shows a red 'Delete' warning control leading to the notification's delete confirmation, on a draft, a submitted notification and an amendment review alike. It reuses the shared notification actions wording 'Delete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Delete on every viewed notification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-021 puts the warning-styled Delete in the header for all three states, and repo-tests-p3-059 proves where it leads.

requirements.statement: A notification's view header holds an 'Import reference numbers' section, named as its own region by that heading, warning once that 'You must use the correct reference and code on the customs declaration or your consignment will be delayed.' above a 'Notification reference' row holding the notification's reference and a 'Customs document code' row reading C640, each value plain text the trader can select, with JavaScript on or off. It shows on a draft and on a submitted notification.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the trader the two values the customs declaration needs; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the section without its JavaScript-only Copy buttons, which design then dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-023 to p6-027 build the region, its single warning and the two rows as plain text, and repo-tests-p3-042 to p3-045 assert them on a draft and on a submitted notification.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification's view has a Back link to the set's own notification list in the animals frontend (the live-animals set root for live animals, the germinal products set root for germinal products), and a draft or an amendment opened with no trail goes back to the notification's overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the Back link to the overall dashboard; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends every such link to the set's own list, which stays in the animals frontend (c-143).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-008: the Back link returns to the notification list when the trader arrived without a trail, and to the overview while the notification is being amended.

requirements.why: It is the prototype kit's own version picker, not part of the service; the goal brings the real services up to one release.

requirements.statement: The prototype's fixed glance counts and seeded demonstration notifications (such as GBN-AG-26-7K8M2W and GBN-GP-26-7K8M2T) are not reproduced.
requirements.why: They are prototype data, not behaviour: the real home and drill-downs show the organisation's real notifications. Sam's 11 November ruling bars any row from resting on the prototype's demo fixtures for what data a notification captures.

requirements.statement: The home's counts and every drill-down list count and show only the signed-in organisation's notifications.
requirements.why: Who may see which notifications is an authorisation constraint the prototype cannot express; the read model already answers for one organisation, but the INS front door's own read carries no organisation to scope by.
requirements.deltaNote: The read model already scopes by organisation: the asking organisation travels in a 'Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id' request header, a notification is returned to its own organisation's list exactly once, and another organisation searching its exact reference is returned none of it (repo-tests-p14-023, repo-tests-p14-024, repo-tests-p14-025). The INS front door's own request for notifications carries no organisation or user (repo-insfrontend-p1-068), and in the stub stack a freshly generated organisation sees another organisation's notifications (trace-ins-fit-p4-046).

requirements.statement: Signing in to the INS front door lands the trader on the home, which only a signed-in trader can open.
requirements.why: The home is the signed-in landing page in Design Release 2.1 and today.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p4-001: sign-in redirects straight to the service root.

requirements.statement: The INS aggregated read model holds one document per notification, created when the notification is created and updated as it is edited and submitted, and can lag the journey a little. The home's table, the home's counts and the drill-downs all read it.
requirements.why: The read model is the cross-journey source the home was handed off to; its eventual consistency means a list or count can briefly trail a change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p14-027 and repo-tests-p14-036: one aggregated document per notification, written as soon as its answers are saved and updated on submit rather than duplicated; repo-tests-p14-018 and trace-e2e-p15-094: a submitted notification reaches the INS home only after a wait, so the store is eventually consistent.

requirements.why: The front door already reads the read model this way for its table; the home and drill-downs need new reads (counts by category, filtered lists) on the same terms.

requirements.deltaNote: Today's Welsh dashboard copy covers the table page's keys (repo-insfrontend-p1-086); the new button needs its own entry.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the category dashboards' own content — the animals and plants dashboards' intro text, filters, sort options and empty states.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the submission confirmation page, the read-only notification view and the declaration step.
requirements.why: They belong to the live-animals journey's own requirements; here they only show how a notification reaches the read model.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the address book pages reached from the home's navigation, their titles and the journey into them.
requirements.why: The address book has its own requirements.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an 'At a glance' band of Alerts, Errors and Messages cards with 'View alerts', 'View errors' and 'View messages' links, and a 'Create a new notification' button label on the home.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements; the per-category glance cards and 'Create new' of the current design replace that earlier design.

requirements.statement: The live animals notification list is the page at the live-animals set root in the animals frontend, and it reads the animals backend's notification list.
requirements.why: The afternoon rulings of 9 October keep each notification list in its own frontend and reframe it in place, built on the animals frontend and animals backend; this replaces, for this programme, the move to the INS frontend that the morning ruling had kept from Rhys's DR1 judgement (c-159).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-001 and repo-backend-p3-001 (proven by trace-e2e-p3-001 and repo-tests-p3-067): the list is already the animals frontend's page at the live-animals set root, backed by the animals backend's GET /notifications; what the page shows changes under the requirements that follow.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's browser title is 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK', with the caption 'Dashboard' above an h1 naming the category, 'Live animals'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every list 'Dashboard' and heads it with the category, so a trader can tell which category's notifications they are looking at; the 9 October afternoon ruling names this frame for the reframed list. requirements.deltaNote: Today the page title and the h1 are both 'Import notification service', so the browser title reads 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK' (repo-frontend-p4-004-m1); the 'Dashboard' caption already exists.

requirements.deltaNote: Today one paragraph about telling the authorities about imported live animals sits under the animals heading, and plants' list has its own intro paragraph about high-risk plants (its guidance-link sentence renders only when a guidance address is supplied, and none is). requirements.statement: The list page has a 'Back' link to the overall home.

requirements.statement: The live animals list has a primary 'Create new' button, which starts a live animals notification and carries the list's category into the create journey. Where it points and how the category is carried are the services' to name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 starts a notification from 'Create new', carrying the category the trader was looking at; the 9 October rulings keep the destination and the category, not the prototype's create-notification?category= address (c-251), and name 'Create new' starting a notification as part of the reframed list's frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a GOV.UK start button 'Start a new notification' posts to the set's notifications path, which creates a draft and its reference on every press and redirects straight to its origin page (repo-frontend-p4-007, p4-008).

requirements.statement: The live animals and germinal products lists have a secondary 'Use template' button beside 'Create new' that goes to the templates page.
requirements.why: Not built: Design Release 2.1 offers starting from a saved template on every category list, but templates are parked and dropped for now, so the lists offer no way into them (c-420). Plants was never in scope for templates.

requirements.statement: The list page has an h2 'Summary' section with two glance cards: 'Action needed' with 'Tasks requiring your attention' and a 'View tasks' link to the action-needed page filtered to the category, and 'Status updated' with 'Changes in the past 24 hours' and a 'View updates' link to the changes page filtered to the category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts what needs the trader's attention at the top of each category list; the 9 October afternoon ruling counts the list's Summary cards (inc-139) as the INS dashboard's summary information, blocked until its requirements firm up.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October): the counts, glance cards and drill-downs are summary information, re-distilled once those requirements exist.

requirements.statement: The list's 'Action needed' glance card shows a live count for the category of the notifications that need something from the trader, matching the Action needed list its link opens.
requirements.why: The count is only useful if it agrees with the drill-down page. It is summary information, blocked with the Summary cards, and what counts as needing action now waits on the outstanding-actions banner the dashboard designs under test introduce (16 November ruling).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October) and the outstanding-actions banner the dashboard designs under test introduce is agreed (Sam, 16 November), because nothing action-required is shown until then.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list the notifications sit under an h2 'Notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the list section 'Notifications'; DR1's 'My notifications' row was only deferred, never judged; plants takes the same frame. DR1's inc-021 also left open whether the breadcrumb label that shares these words on the delete and cancel-amendment pages follows the heading, which those pages' own area settles.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use the medium h2 'Your notifications' (Welsh 'Eich hysbysiadau'), which the animals frontend also uses as the breadcrumb label on the delete and cancel-amendment pages.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list the search and sort sit in one column above the cards inside the 'Notifications' section, with no 'Filter notifications' heading and no separate one-third filter aside beside the results; on the live animals list the 'Additional filters' disclosure follows them, above the tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays the list out as one column: search and sort, then the filters disclosure, then the tabs and cards. Plants takes the same frame in the same increment, its filters aside (9 October afternoon ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists are two columns inside the full-width content column: a one-third aside headed 'Filter notifications' (h3) holding the search, and a two-thirds column holding the results count, sort and cards (repo-frontend-p4-013, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-054).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search field is labelled 'Search by'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label; today's 'Keyword or reference' promises a keyword search the service does not give.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is labelled 'Keyword or reference' (small bold label) and named referenceNumber.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search field has the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'.
requirements.why: The hint tells the trader what the search matches.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search is submitted by a real submit button that shows only a magnifying-glass icon and whose accessible name is 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control; the 9 October afternoon ruling lets the icon-only button stand as long as it is a real submit button of the GET form (c-299).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button is a standard primary GOV.UK button with the visible text 'Search'.

requirements.statement: A search on the live animals list lists the notifications whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains the searched text, ignoring case.
requirements.why: The hint promises a keyword search over those facts, and DR1's own inc-019 row read the same three things as searchable. The prototype cannot persist or query, so its search is inert; a real search box that does nothing would mislead the trader, so the real service applies it (c-162).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the term is passed to the listing only as referenceNumber, an exact match on a complete reference, so a commodity or a party name finds nothing (repo-frontend-p4-016, repo-tests-p3-089).

requirements.statement: After a search the field keeps the searched text, and searching with an empty or whitespace-only field clears the search and lists everything again.
requirements.why: The trader can see and change what they searched for; both Design Release 2.1 and today keep the text.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-017, p4-022 and p4-023: the field is filled with the current term, and a blank or whitespace-only term means no filter.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list, search, sort and every additional filter are one GET form to the list's own path, submitted by the search button; it carries the current tab (unless 'In progress') and the current page (when above 1) as hidden fields, so the result stays on that tab. Changing a select or a radio submits nothing by itself.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts sort and filters inside the search form with one submit control, and the 9 October afternoon ruling makes it one GET form whose submit button searches and sorts on the server, so the page works without JavaScript; today search and sort are two forms and a search always restarts at page 1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form carries only the sort as a hidden field (no page, no tab), and the sort is a separate GET form (repo-frontend-p4-018, p4-036).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's sort select is labelled 'Sort by:'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the sort control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the select is labelled 'Sort by' with no colon (small bold label).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's sort select offers exactly 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', in that order, with no unselected 'Select one' option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the sort three orderings; DR1 already rejected an unsorted 'Select one' state, so the list is always sorted, and its own sort-label row was deferred while the list was thought temporary, never judged (c-167).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the options are 'Arrival (newest to oldest)', 'Arrival (oldest to newest)', 'Date created (newest to oldest)' and 'Date created (oldest to newest)'.

requirements.statement: The live animals list is always sorted and the sort is applied for real: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by when the notification was created, 'Arrival date' orders by arrival date newest first, and with no sort chosen the list is ordered by arrival date newest first with 'Arrival date' selected.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the list always sorted; the prototype never orders its list, so the real service applies the orderings, keeping today's default order (which the prototype's completed tab also shows).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the default is 'Arrival (newest to oldest)' and any unknown value falls back to it; no end-to-end test proves the order of the cards (repo-tests-p3-098).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has no 'Update sort' button: the chosen sort is applied by the search button with the rest of the form, and the chosen option stays selected after the page reloads.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's sort has no button of its own; DR1 only deferred this difference, and the 9 October afternoon ruling has one submit button for the whole form, with no select submitting on change.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a separate GET sort form with a secondary 'Update sort' button applies the sort, carrying the page and the search as hidden fields (repo-frontend-p4-029, p4-034).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has an 'Additional filters' disclosure built from the GOV.UK details component inside the search form, closed on load and open whenever an arrival-date, date-range or status filter is set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the extra filters out of the way until the trader needs them; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the disclosure from GOV.UK details rather than the prototype's custom chevron markup (c-299).

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By arrival date' column of small GOV.UK radios 'Today', 'Tomorrow' and 'Next 7 days' (legend visually hidden, the same words shown as its heading); choosing one and searching lists only notifications arriving in that range, and the choice stays checked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader find what is arriving soon; the prototype's filter is inert, so the real service applies it.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By date range' column with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and two MoJ date pickers, 'Start date' and 'End date' (a 'Choose date' calendar opening on the current month, weeks starting Monday, each a plain text field without JavaScript); the list shows only notifications arriving between the two dates, and the entered dates are kept.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's date range. DR1's own row records that the design never says which date a date filter narrows, so three things settle it on the arrival date: the radios beside it name the arrival date in their legend and heading, DR1's row has those radios built on this same range rather than on parameters of their own, and the arrival date is the only date Design Release 2.1's card shows at all. The 9 October afternoon ruling accepts the MoJ date picker here, because the range is a search filter, not a date read from a document, and the interaction designer keeps that picker as the one every other date in both frontends uses.

requirements.statement: When the start or end date cannot be read as a date, or the end date is before the start date, the list shows a GOV.UK error summary and an inline error on the date field ('Enter a real start date', 'Enter a real end date' or 'End date must be the same as or after the start date'), opens 'Additional filters', keeps the entered text in the 'Start date' and 'End date' pickers, and lists notifications without the date-range filter.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so a date the filter cannot use is answered with an error rather than silently ignored; the prototype still sets the labels and keeps the entered dates, and the GOV.UK date-input error pattern supplies the messages (c-166, which the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps). The 26 October ruling sets the same shape for any answer that is missing or not valid: an error message for each one, the trader kept on the page, and what they typed never dropped.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'Status' select offering 'Select one', 'Submitted' and 'Completed'; choosing a status and searching lists only notifications in it, and the choice stays selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's status filter offers the statuses a trader acts on; drafts have their own tab, so Draft is not offered. 'Completed' matches nothing until the authorities' outcomes reach the notification record, and the select still offers it, because the prototype names it. Whether 'Action required' is offered while nothing action-required is shown is its own question (req-2346).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has three tabs, 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', built as MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the page with that tab chosen; 'In progress' is the list with no tab chosen, an unknown or missing tab shows 'In progress', and following a tab drops the search, sort and filters. The tab parameter's name and values are the animals frontend's.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 separates work in flight, unfinished drafts and finished notifications, and drafts keep a home on the list, which DR1 said must not be lost; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the tabs as MoJ sub navigation on the animals frontend's own list, naming all three tabs even though the 'Completed' tab holds nothing until the authorities' outcomes reach the notification record, and the prototype never names query parameters (c-251).

requirements.statement: The 'In progress' tab lists submitted and action-required notifications, 'Draft' lists drafts and 'Completed' lists completed notifications.
requirements.why: Each tab holds the notifications at that stage, as Design Release 2.1 sets them out; a notification being amended goes in 'In progress' (c-165).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended is listed in the 'In progress' tab with the shared status kit's yellow amendment tag and its status-driven actions (Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no amending state and its catch-all status mapping would file one as a draft only by fallback, while the backend persists an amendment as a submitted notification in AMEND that never returns to DRAFT and publishes it as an amendment of a submission: a persistence and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (c-165).
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amending notification is listed with every other notification and there are no tabs. Its tag's word now comes from the shared status kit, which reads 'Amend' (repo-frontend-p4-049) where the older traces render 'Amending' (trace-animals-fit-p2-035, trace-e2e-p3-031); the list shows whatever word the kit gives.

requirements.statement: Only the 'In progress' tab shows a count, in bold brackets, such as 'In progress (2)'; 'Draft' and 'Completed' show none, even when selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only the notifications in flight; the count belongs to the tabs, which the 9 October afternoon ruling builds now, not to the blocked Summary cards.

requirements.statement: Under the tabs the cards sit under an h3 naming the tab: 'Notifications in progress', 'Draft notifications' or 'Completed notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's subheading for each tab panel.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows 8 notifications a page.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling pages the reframed list 8 at a time, which is also Design Release 2.1's page size for every list and the figure the rest of the estate pages at; how many rows a page holds over a dataset that grows is not the prototype's to set (23 November ruling), so the ruling is the authority and the prototype agrees with it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page size comes from the listing: 25 from the animals backend (end to end) and 20 from the frontend stub (fit), and the page reports the size it is given (repo-frontend-p4-070).

requirements.statement: A list of more than one page shows GOV.UK pagination with numbered page links, a 'Previous' link from page 2 and a 'Next' link before the last page; a list of one page, or no results, shows no pagination. This holds on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses numbered pagination; today both lists have only Previous and Next. Pagination is kept and wanted wherever a list is paged (25 November ruling), and plants takes the same paging in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use block-style pagination with only Previous and Next links and no page numbers, reading 'Next' and 'Previous' rather than the 'Next page' and 'Previous page' the suite's other lists use (repo-tests-p3-082).

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and a page past the last shows the last page, on the live animals list as on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 clamps the page, so a stale or hand-typed page never shows an empty list; plants' list already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-075, p4-076 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-033: both lists already ignore a page that is not a whole number of at least one and clamp a page past the last to the last page.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's page links keep the tab (unless 'In progress'), the sort (unless the default), the search text and every additional filter.
requirements.why: Because the real search and filters apply, a page link that dropped them would show a different, unfiltered list on page 2 (c-163).
requirements.deltaNote: Today Previous and Next keep the sort (unless the default) and the reference search, and the list's address carries only what differs from the default view; there are no tabs or filters to keep (repo-frontend-p4-035, p4-074).

requirements.statement: Neither the live animals list nor plants' list shows a count of the results, on any tab or page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list shows no results count; DR1 only deferred its rewrite of the count; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a small bold line above both lists' cards reads 'No Results', 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing N of T Results' or 'Showing S to E of T Results' (Welsh twins on plants), worked out from the page, the size and the total, so it can disagree with the cards shown when deleted rows are dropped after the page is cut (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-057).

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a search or filter that matches nothing shows an empty list with no message about it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message on any list; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a search with no match on either list replaces the results line with 'No notifications found' and shows no cards.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a tab or list holding no notifications shows an empty list with no message about it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message; today's sentence also wrongly says the animals list is session-scoped. Plants' own copy quoted the same sentence, but the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same frame (c-300).
requirements.deltaNote: Today a user with no notifications who is not searching sees 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' on both lists (repo-frontend-p4-068; on plants the same English sentence and the Welsh 'Nid ydych wedi dechrau unrhyw hysbysiadau yn y sesiwn hon.'), and the animals list shows 'No Results' beside it.

requirements.statement: Each notification card on the live animals list and on plants' list is labelled for screen readers 'Notification <reference>' and has the reference as its h3.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card names itself to assistive technology, and the 9 October afternoon ruling names the cards for screen readers in the reframed frame; the reference heading already exists on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each card on both lists is a GOV.UK summary card with the reference (or the notification's own id before a reference is issued) as its level-3 title, but no 'Notification <reference>' accessible name.

requirements.statement: A live animals card shows its facts in two rows: 'Commodity', 'Arrival date', 'Consignee' and 'Notification status', then the quantity, 'Origin', 'Consignor' and, when inspection is required, 'Inspection'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card leads with what is coming, when, to whom and its status.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows eight facts in three rows: Commodity, Origin, 'Arrival at destination'; Consignee, Consignor, Status; 'Date created', 'Date submitted' (repo-frontend-p4-039).

requirements.statement: The card labels the arrival date 'Arrival date', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the card, and DR1's own rename row was deferred rather than judged; but the 17 November ruling words the arrival date 'Arrival date at port of entry' everywhere it appears, and nothing says whether the card is one of those places (c-421).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Arrival at destination' on the animals card and 'Arrival' on plants' card.

requirements.statement: The card labels the status 'Notification status', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the status fact; plants takes the same card layout.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Status' on both cards.

requirements.statement: A live animals notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of animals', from the notification's own count in the animals backend's record.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows how much is coming on every card; today no card shows a quantity, and the 9 October afternoon ruling takes the card's facts from the animals backend's record.

requirements.statement: The card shows no 'Date created' and no 'Date submitted', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card has no dates other than arrival; today's 'Date submitted' is also blank on every card, submitted ones included, on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards show 'Date created' and 'Date submitted', each the day the event happened in the service's own time zone; 'Date submitted' is blank in every end-to-end trace, and blank on a plants draft (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-077, trace-e2e-p3-033).

requirements.statement: The card writes the arrival date as the day, the full month name and the year, such as '21 June 2026', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card writes the arrival date with the full month name, in its code and its render alike, and nothing overrides the prototype here (c-164).
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards write the arrival date as day, short month name and year, such as '7 Nov 2026' and '5 Mar 2026' (trace-animals-fit-p2-031, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-058); the tests repo already reads the animals card's date as 'd Month yyyy' (repo-tests-p3-073).

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a card whose notification has no commodity, no arrival date or no quantity yet shows 'Not applicable' for that fact.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows an empty fact; today a draft card is mostly empty labels.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a fact with no answer yet is shown with an empty value and no placeholder on both lists (repo-frontend-p4-045, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-061).

requirements.statement: The live animals card's commodity is the notification's commodity name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the commodity as the trader chose it; germinal products need the product type as well as the species (req-1738).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows the commodity's name, falling back to its commodity code and then to nothing (repo-frontend-p4-041, p4-047); a commodity chosen as Bos taurus shows 'Cow'.

requirements.statement: A draft's status is a 'Draft' tag, while 'Submitted' is plain styled text and not a tag; plants' card follows the same styles for Draft and Submitted and keeps its 'Late' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses a tag only for statuses that ask something of the trader; plants mirrors the components (c-301). The 'Action required' tag the prototype also shows is withdrawn until the outstanding-actions banner is agreed (c-418).
requirements.deltaNote: Today every status on both lists is a tag: Draft blue, Submitted green, Amend yellow, Deleted grey and never shown (repo-frontend-p4-049, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-025). The 'Completed' style is req-1739.

requirements.statement: A delayed notification shows a 'Delayed' tag on an error card, with the reason for the delay as its message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows delays on the list; its own message there is placeholder copy, so the reason the record carries is shown instead.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no delay status or reason reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification the authorities have finished with shows the status 'Completed' and is listed in the 'Completed' tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 moves finished notifications out of the in-progress list; the completed status waits for a real source of completion, which the 16 November ruling confirms does not exist yet.
requirements.blockedBy: A real source of completion exists (Sam, 16 November): the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes back to the notification record, and no completed status reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification chosen for inspection shows an extra 'Inspection' fact with a 'Required' tag at the end of the card's second row.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 warns the trader on the list that the consignment will be inspected.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no inspection decision reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A live animals card keeps its status-driven actions, each named for screen readers with ' notification <reference>': a draft offers Resume, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a submitted notification offers View, Amend, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a notification being amended offers Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete. Amend and 'Copy as new' stay link-styled buttons that post, each in its own form and in the same typeface as the links, while View, Resume, 'Cancel amendment' and Delete are links.
requirements.why: DR1 judged that the card keeps its status-driven links rather than DR1's flat 'Copy as new' and 'View', and that judgement wins over Design Release 2.1's same flat pair. Without it a trader could not resume a draft from the list. The 19 November ruling's one-form-each rule for posting buttons is what the card already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-051, p4-052 and p4-053 (proven by trace-animals-fit-p2-037, p2-042 and p2-044 and by repo-tests-p3-075 and p3-076): the card already offers these sets in this order, each posting action in its own form with the CSRF crumb and visually hidden ' notification <reference>' text.

requirements.statement: A card whose notification is delayed, completed, or needs something from the trader without a status-driven action set of its own offers 'Copy as new' then 'View', View opening the notification's review page.
requirements.why: DR1's judgement covers only the card links the animals frontend builds today; for these statuses nothing overrides Design Release 2.1, whose card offers 'Copy as new' and 'View'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a notification in any status other than Draft, Submitted or Amend has no actions on its card (repo-frontend-p4-054).
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; until it does, no card is in these statuses.

requirements.statement: After an action that sends the trader back to the list with that action's flag on the redirect (such as a delete), the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', carrying that action's message; plants' deletion banner carries the same 'Success' title. Each list feature holds this wording in its own copy, and the shared notificationActions wording that other pages use stays as it is.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one success banner titled 'Success'; the message itself is set by the action. The 9 October ruling keeps the flag on the redirect (such as ?deleted=1) rather than a message held for the trader (c-252), and the afternoon ruling gives plants' banner the same title in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners are titled for the action: 'Notification deleted' with 'The notification has been deleted.' on both lists (repo-frontend-p4-066, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-034), and each banner shows only when its own flag is on the address (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-034-m1).

requirements.statement: The list's success message is held for the trader, shown once and then cleared.
requirements.why: The 2026-10-09 ruling drops moving the success banner to a message held for the trader and shown once (inc-140 criteria 2 and 3): the flag on the redirect, such as ?deleted=1, stays, so the banner shows whenever the list is opened with it (c-252).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners show whenever the list is opened with the action's flag on the address, and that stays.

requirements.statement: The notification list's success banner, the deletion message included, does not dismiss itself on the live animals list or on plants' list: it stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: A message that disappears on a timer can vanish before a screen reader or a slow reader reaches it (WCAG 2.2.1); this accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1's 5-second auto-dismiss, and the 9 October afternoon ruling confirms it (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-066 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-034: today's deletion banners are GOV.UK success banners announced to assistive technology, with no timer that dismisses them.

requirements.statement: The live animals list keeps its stale-action banner and its 'There is a problem' banner when an action started from a card fails.
requirements.why: Concurrency and failure handling are real constraints the prototype cannot express, so they stay although Design Release 2.1 shows neither.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-067: when an action on a notification fails for a reason worth retrying, the list is shown again with the service's recoverable-error banner above it.

requirements.statement: Every list string has a Welsh version, on the animals lists and on plants' list, marked as a machine draft that ships only after a translator signs it off under the Welsh Language Standards, and no label is left blank in either language.
requirements.why: Both real services are bilingual and their list Welsh is an unreviewed machine draft; Design Release 2.1's new strings need Welsh twins too.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every English list key on both lists has a machine-drafted Welsh twin, not yet reviewed by a translator, and the sort options are paired with their wording by position rather than by name (repo-frontend-p4-084, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-063).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, empty or with cards, and does not scroll sideways at 1280px or at 769px wide; plants' list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, with or without its amend-refused banner.
requirements.why: Both real lists meet this today and the reframed lists must keep meeting it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-079 and p4-080, and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-084 and p1-085: fit tests prove no serious or critical axe violations on either list and no sideways scroll on the animals list.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's root in the animals frontend renders its own copy of the reframed list: the caption 'Dashboard', the h1 'Germinal products', the same search, sort, additional filters and tabs pointed at its own address, and a 'Create new' button that starts a germinal products notification in the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each category of animal notification its own list; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal list as the germinal set's own copy of the reframed live animals list (inc-141), instead of an INS germinal list.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows only live animals notifications: a germinal products notification never appears on it, and a notification whose record holds no category counts as live animals.
requirements.why: A trader looking at one category must not see another's notifications; the animals backend stores each notification's category on its record, an absent category meaning live animals, and the reframed list reads that record.

requirements.statement: Deleted notifications never appear on any list or in a search.
requirements.why: A deleted notification is gone for the trader; both Design Release 2.1 and the real services leave it out.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p3-002, repo-frontend-p4-050 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-030: the animals backend's list leaves out DELETED notifications, and both frontends drop a deleted row even when the service returns it.

requirements.statement: A newly started notification appears on the list straight away.
requirements.why: A trader must find their new draft on the list as soon as they have started it; the list reads the animals backend's own record, not an event-populated read model that lags writes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p3-069 and trace-e2e-p3-049: a newly started notification is found on the list by its reference, though the suite still reopens the list and searches again for up to 15 seconds before the card shows (repo-tests-p3-070, req-2351).

requirements.statement: A list shows only the notifications of the signed-in trader's organisation, and the animals backend's list API refuses a caller that does not say which organisation it acts for.
requirements.why: Authentication and data separation are real constraints the prototype cannot express; today the animals backend's list serves every trader's notifications to every caller, while both frontends show only what the trader's own session knows about.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals backend's list takes no user or organisation input, so every caller is served every trader's notifications (repo-backend-p3-003), and each frontend narrows the list to the notifications its own session knows about instead (repo-frontend-p4-069, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-029).

requirements.statement: The INS backend's notification read model and its GET /notifications list API keep their record fields, event handling, paging, sorts, reference search and scoping as they stand, and no notification list reads them.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the reframed lists on the animals frontend and animals backend and drops the INS read model's part of the list rows; the INS dashboard that does read it is blocked until its requirements firm up, and its category gap (germinal notifications listed without their category) is a known gap until then.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the INS backend as it is today.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list returns, for each notification, every fact the card shows: the reference number, status, commodity name, arrival date, origin, consignee name, consignor name, the notification's category, and its number of animals or, for germinal products, its number of packages with each line's species and product type. A fact the notification does not hold is returned as empty.
requirements.why: The card cannot show facts its list API does not return; the 9 October afternoon ruling takes the card facts from the animals backend's record, and that list item carries no category or quantity today.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each animals backend list item carries the reference number, concurrency token, status, created timestamp, origin, commodity, consignor, consignee and transport, but no category or quantity of its own (repo-backend-p3-015, p3-016); the card also reads the arrival date only from the top level of the row, so an arrival date nested under transport would leave the card blank (repo-frontend-p4-045-m1).

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API filters by category (live animals or germinal products, absent meaning live animals) and by tab (the in-progress statuses, drafts, or completed), and reports how many notifications the 'In progress' tab holds.
requirements.why: Each set's list and each tab shows only its own notifications, and the 'In progress' tab shows its count; with both lists built on the animals backend, the category filter belongs to its list (c-159).

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API takes a search text and returns every notification whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains it, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, paged like any other list.
requirements.why: The list's search matches a keyword across those facts; today the list API matches only one exact, case-sensitive, whole reference and returns at most one notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today referenceNumber is trimmed and matched exactly against a whole reference; a match holds exactly one notification, and a miss answers 200 with an empty page.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API filters by status and by an arrival-date range (from and to dates, either optional).
requirements.why: The status select and both arrival-date filters need the API to narrow the list; today the list API has no filter beyond an exact reference.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API sorts by creation date (newest or oldest first) and by arrival date, defaults to arrival date newest first, and breaks ties on a second key so no notification repeats or goes missing between pages.
requirements.why: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by creation date and 'Arrival date' by arrival; a single-key sort with ties (such as drafts with no arrival date) is unstable across pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals backend already sorts on arrivalDate or createdAt, defaulting to arrival date newest first, but on one field only, with no tie-breaker.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API serves 8 notifications a page, numbered from 1, and reports the page, size, number of elements, total elements and total pages.
requirements.why: The list shows 8 a page and builds numbered pagination from the totals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals backend serves 25 a page, set by configuration; the response shape and the 1-based page already exist.

requirements.statement: The INS backend's list API answers a bad request, such as a page below 1, with a 400 validation problem response naming the field, and an unexpected failure with a 500 problem response that hides the underlying error.
requirements.why: This is the INS list API's behaviour today; the notification lists no longer call that API in this programme (req-1097), so nothing here is built or changed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insbackend-p1-029 and p1-104: a page below 1 answers 400 'Validation Error' with an errors map keyed 'page', proven by repo-insbackend-p1-118.
