requirements.why: This is shared page chrome that already exists. The afternoon ruling keeps it as it is for every set: a page that needs another header switches it off, and only the Amend bar changes it in place. Each page's use of it belongs to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-023 to p2-025 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-021 to p13-026 render the strip, its tag and its Cancel amend link, and a page can leave it out (repo-insfrontend-p4-022, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-025, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-061).

requirements.statement: Every page's footer on every frontend offers 'Privacy', 'Cookies' and 'Accessibility statement' links to the GOV.UK help pages, with the OGL v3.0 licence line and Crown copyright, and Welsh twins for the three labels. The service has no cookies page, privacy notice or accessibility statement of its own.

requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-030 records the link; the three layouts inherit it from the GOV.UK template (repo-frontend-p2-001, repo-insfrontend-p4-027, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-001).

requirements.statement: No page shows who is signed in: no email, name or 'signed in as' strip, and no 'Sign out' link apart from the navigation's Log out.

requirements.statement: On the animals and plants frontends, when sign-in fails the user sees a page titled 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in' and headed 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in.', asking them to 'Please try again', where 'try again' links to sign-in. In Welsh the title and heading read 'Mae'n ddrwg gennym, ni allwn eich mewngofnodi', with 'Rhowch' before the link 'gynnig arall arni'.
requirements.why: A failed Defra ID sign-in is an authentication case the prototype cannot express, and the page already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-031 gives the animals page and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-056 and p13-090-m1 the plants page with its Welsh twin; repo-tests-p6-079, p14-084 and p16-034 show the suite waiting for either the landing page or this page before deciding to try again.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, a failed sign-in shows the unauthorised page: browser title 'Unable to sign in', heading 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in.' and body 'Please try again.', where 'try again' links to /auth/sign-in. The page has no back link. It is shown when the Defra ID callback fails, the token carries no organisation or fails verification, or the user's role and permissions cannot be loaded.
requirements.why: These are authentication failures the prototype cannot express, and the page already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-080 and p4-083 to p4-086 give the page and when it shows.

requirements.statement: An error response on every frontend is shown as the shared error page with the error's own HTTP status. The page's large heading is the status number, and a paragraph below it, which is also the browser title, reads 'Page not found' (404), 'Forbidden' (403), 'You need to sign in to view this page' (401), 'There is a problem with your request' (400) or 'Something went wrong' (any other). Its content holds only that heading and message: no back link and no error summary, with the service navigation still there for a signed-in user. A notification that cannot be found shows that standard page not found, like every other page in the service. An error on a path inside a journey set, routed or not, uses that set's chrome; a path under no set uses set-free chrome whose home link is the site root and which shows no status strip, no success banner and no recoverable-error banner.
requirements.why: Real errors are a constraint the prototype cannot express, and every frontend already shares this page; the owner's 19 November ruling makes a missing notification take it too.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-029 and p2-030, repo-insfrontend-p4-072 to p4-078 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-053, p13-054 and p13-055-m1 render the page; repo-plantsfrontend-p13-057 and p13-058 and repo-frontend-p2-135-m1 decide which set's chrome an error takes; repo-tests-p10-111 and p15-073 scan the 404 page. The ruling's missing-notification clause is the only part not yet proven for the review page (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-030).

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, the service root / sends a signed-in user to the default set's dashboard, /live-animals, and a journey can also be entered at /start.
requirements.why: This is how the animals frontend reaches its home today.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-047 and repo-tests-p6-072 record the redirect, and repo-frontend-p2-129 the /start entry.

requirements.statement: The shared notification actions read 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' on the animals and plants frontends. After a copy, a success message titled 'Notification copied' reads 'A new draft notification has been created.' After a delete, one titled 'Notification deleted' reads 'The notification has been deleted.' Each has a Welsh twin. This shared copy is never reworded in place: a page whose wording differs adds keys in its feature's own copy.
requirements.why: This is shared copy the lists and notification pages already use, and the afternoon ruling forbids rewording it in place because the notification list uses it too. Comparing it with the target design belongs to the dashboard and notification-actions areas.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-062 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-092 give the copy, with the Welsh twins in repo-plantsfrontend-p13-090.

requirements.statement: Address pickers offer a shared 'Add a new address' link, and a success banner titled 'Success' says the named address was added to your address book. When a chosen address is not in the user's address book, the error reads 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.' When the address book cannot be reached, it reads 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: This is shared copy the journey's address pickers already use. Comparing the pickers with the target design belongs to the addresses area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-063 and p2-064 give the copy.

requirements.statement: Sign-in hands off to Defra ID with an OpenID Connect authorisation-code request (scope openid offline_access, query response mode, policy b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi), naming each frontend's own serviceId and its own /auth/sign-in-oidc callback. On success, the user's organisation, CRN and name are taken from the token and held in a server-side session.
requirements.why: Real sign-in through Defra ID is an authentication constraint the prototype's sign-in page cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-002 to p1-004 and trace-e2e-p15-012 record the handoff.

requirements.statement: After signing in, a user who belongs to more than one organisation is asked to 'Choose your organisation' from radios labelled with each organisation's name and SBI, with a Continue button. A user with one organisation never sees that choice. The chosen organisation reaches the service through the sign-in callback, and the user lands on the page they asked for. No page in the service offers a way to switch organisation, and a page that needs an organisation returns 403 when the session has none.
requirements.why: Organisation choice is part of real Defra ID authentication, which the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p15-016 to p15-020 record the single-organisation and multi-organisation paths on the INS frontend, repo-tests-p6-080 and p14-083 the picker's heading and options, and repo-tests-p16-163 to p16-165 the two identities the suite signs in as, one of them in two organisations.

requirements.statement: Signing in to one frontend signs the user in to the others without asking for credentials again, because Defra ID answers their requests straight away. Each frontend keeps its own session cookie on the shared host (sid for animals, ins-sid for INS, plants-sid for plants, unless a run names one), so all three sessions are kept side by side, and the three homes sit at different paths. Each service has its own landing page after sign-in, the INS frontend's checked landing page being the address book.
requirements.why: Moving between the animals journey and the INS dashboard and address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express. It already works.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p14-078 to p14-081 and trace-e2e-p15-111 and p15-113 prove single sign-on and kept sessions across the three frontends from a browser with no cookies, and repo-tests-p16-055 shows a new context can carry only the auth cookie so no journey state travels with it.

requirements.statement: A session is valid only while it is in the server-side cache (Redis when deployed). The session cookie lasts 4 hours and is HttpOnly. An expired token is refreshed when refresh is on, and otherwise the user is treated as signed out. Every route needs a signed-in user unless it opts out, on the request that shows a page and on the request that saves it alike.
requirements.why: Real sessions are an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, and they already work this way.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-031 and p1-032 record the cookies, repo-insfrontend-p4-102 and p4-103 the session rules and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-033-m1 that both the show and the save request need a session. What a user sees when a session lapses is not recorded (trace-e2e-p1-062).

requirements.statement: In stub mode the INS frontend signs a user in at once with no sign-in page, as 'Stub User' in the organisation given by an organisationId parameter (default 'stub-org-1'). The stub session lasts four hours, sign-out goes straight to /, and the Defra ID callback and organisation routes do not exist. Stub mode is refused in production.
requirements.why: This is how the INS frontend runs locally and in its own browser tests. It is part of today's real authentication set-up.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-106 to p4-113 give the stub mode.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, every form post must carry a valid CSRF token (except under /health, /assets and /public). Every page carries the token in a csrf-token meta tag in its head, every form has a hidden 'crumb' input, and the CSRF cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite Strict.
requirements.why: Protection against cross-site request forgery is a real security constraint, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-027, trace-e2e-p1-033-m1, repo-insfrontend-p4-114 to p4-116 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-029 show the token.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend sends a Content-Security-Policy on its pages, redirects and sign-in callback. It limits scripts, styles, fonts, images and the base URL to its own origin (plus one hashed inline script), lets forms post to itself and the address book origin, and forbids framing and plugins. It also sends Strict-Transport-Security for a year, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Download-Options noopen, X-XSS-Protection and Cache-Control no-cache.
requirements.why: Security headers are a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and they already exist.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-052 to p1-060 record the headers.

requirements.statement: Security-header and cookie defects found on the way are not fixed by this programme: the CSP's connect-src lists 'wss' without a colon, the animals frontend sends no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP or COEP header, and the animals and plants frontends share one 'crumb' CSRF cookie on localhost.
requirements.why: These are problems in today's services that bringing the services up to the target design does not touch. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The Defra ID stub's own pages are not changed by this programme: its sign-in page ('Sign in using Government Gateway', user ID and password, 'Help signing in', the 'I have forgotten my password' placeholder, the CRN error message that names neither field as the wrong one, and its non-standard error summary), its title, phase banner and doubled service name, its signed-out page and its own security headers. The stub is observed through the security proxy but never attacked, and its error summary list is left out of accessibility scans, while the service's own sign-in and callback handlers stay in scope.
requirements.why: The stub stands in for Defra ID and is not one of the programme's repos. Its defects go to the report, and the suites already treat it as somebody else's code.
requirements.deltaNote: The stub's pages are as trace-e2e-p1-005 to p1-027 and repo-tests-p6-068, p6-070 and p6-071 record them; repo-tests-p11-084, p15-078 and p16-122 show the suites already exclude the stub's own markup and traffic from attack and from accessibility scans.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's accessibility suite holds every scanned page to WCAG 2.2 AA. Every test carries the @a11y tag and is reported under that standard, read from the fixture so the title and the rule set cannot drift apart, and every scan passes the five axe tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa explicitly, because axe's own default leaves target-size out. A scan waits for the DOM and then allows a bounded settling period, scanning anyway if that wait times out; it is recorded against the page's path; a test runs every one of its scans before failing and reports them together with each violation's severity, rule, description, node count and help link, attaching them to the report as JSON; a failing scan fails its test and a test that takes the scan but never runs one fails too. A test is allowed five minutes. Pages whose layout matters at small sizes are scanned again at 320 by 568 and at 568 by 320, and a narrow scan also proves the page does not scroll sideways once its tables are discounted. A scan may be narrowed per page, and the only exclusions are the two conditional-reveal radio groups whose aria-expanded attribute axe rejects and the sign-in stub's own error list: upstream disagreements in code the service does not own. A clean scan is not full conformance, and a state earns its own scan only where its value outweighs the set-up it needs.
requirements.why: Every page this programme changes must keep passing this suite, and a new scan has to be written to these rules. It already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p10-001 to p10-022 and p15-058 to p15-060 define the suite, p10-142 to p10-144 and p15-080 to p15-082 prove the scanner itself catches a real fault, and p10-013 to p10-017, p15-091 and p16-029 give the only exclusions.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite walks the live-animals journey from the notification list to the declaration and scans every journey page as it first opens, and walks it again filling each page in and ending at the submitted confirmation, scanning every page with its answers on it. Each page is reached through the journey flow's own steps and page objects rather than by the spec's own navigation.
requirements.why: This is the existing end-to-end accessibility proof of the journey. Each page the target design changes must still pass it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p10-023 and p10-044 define the two walks, and p10-024 to p10-065 the pages and states each scans.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite walks the live-animals journey a third time and scans every page that validates input while its errors are on screen, starting from a brand-new notification at the origin page, and a scan runs only once the error summary headed 'There is a problem' is visible.
requirements.why: This is the existing accessibility proof of the shared error summary on journey pages.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p10-066 and p10-067 define the walk and the wait, and p10-068 to p10-086 the error states it scans.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite also scans the rest of the animals service: the reason-gated pages and both transporter forms, the commodity details page with two species and the identification page with the horse and cat identifier sets, the long journey pages at both narrow viewports from seeded drafts, the notification list in its default, sorted, searched, empty-result, paged and narrow-viewport views, the not-found page, check your answers in its draft, refused and submitted states with the submission confirmation, the overview with every task complete, the cancel-amendment and delete confirmations with their success banners, the consignment addresses page and the consignor edit page filled and refused, the contact address page, and the unauthorised page from a cold start.
requirements.why: This is the existing accessibility proof of the rest of the animals service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p10-087 to p10-141 define the scans.

requirements.statement: Each frontend's own browser tests check accessibility in the repo as well. The animals frontend checks that a captioned page and the dashboard with its service navigation have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA violations, excluding the conditional-reveal false positive. The INS frontend checks every page's initial render and validation-error state against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 AA. The plants frontend builds every shared chrome component from GOV.UK Frontend apart from the Ministry of Justice date picker, and its own pages are checked the same way. Review cards and other grouped content get their accessible names the way the rest of the service does.
requirements.why: These are the existing in-repo accessibility checks that a navigation or layout change must keep passing, and the owner's 19 November ruling makes a card's accessible name follow the service's own pattern rather than a one-off.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-013, p1-014 and p1-026 record the passing animals checks, repo-insfrontend-p4-167 the INS checks, and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-001 and p13-095 that plants' chrome is GOV.UK Frontend components only. The accessible-name clause is the ruling's, not yet proven (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-029).

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's accessibility proof are not closed by this programme. On the animals side no scan covers the permanent address page, four of the five party pickers and four of the five party edit pages, the contact address edit page, the sign-in page or the organisation picker, the add-address hand-off to the address book, or the germinal-products set, and the narrow-viewport scan of the notification list does not check for sideways scrolling. On the INS side the empty dashboard, the empty address book, the address book's load-failure state, the notification type page and every transporter page go unscanned, and the dashboard's narrow-viewport scans do not check for sideways scrolling. The organisation-scoped API refusals are proven by status code only, the sign-in error is proven only for present-but-invalid values, no test drives the organisation picker as a journey of its own, and nothing proves another organisation's user is refused a notification's view page as well as its overview.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps in today's suites, not differences from the target design. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's security suite is a traffic-driven OWASP ZAP scan of six services, each its own named ZAP context with its own address: the animals frontend, the animals admin, the INS frontend, the animals backend, the plants backend and the address book. Playwright drives real signed-in journeys through the proxy rather than letting ZAP crawl, so coverage is traffic-driven and the attacking corpus is curated by hand. There are two profiles: a passive one that runs the end-to-end suite without attacking, and an attacking one that runs only the @active corpus, is deliberate, runs on the compose stack alone and is refused on the deployed platform because its journeys delete records the scan then re-fires with fuzzed payloads. Anything but the exact attacking profile name is treated as passive. Identifiers in a page or API address are declared to ZAP as data rather than structure, from a context plan registered before any traffic exists; all three plans must declare the same contexts; diagnostics are excluded rather than scanned; the DOM cross-site-scripting rule is off; the uploader and the queue-consuming INS backend are out of scope with their reasons; and the three APIs are scanned because every API client inherits the run's proxy. The attacking corpus drives sign-in and sign-out, a whole submitted journey, the reason-gated pages and a private transporter, amend, copy, cancel and delete, a document upload with its scan and download, a draft validation error, the notification list's search, paging and sorting, the review page's Change trail, and the INS address book's whole record lifecycle with its role filter, its refused hand-off guard and the INS dashboard. A run fails on a FAIL-rated alert from the rules file (an unlisted alert failing only if it is high risk), on a scan that finished at or within half a minute of its 60-minute cap, or on a declared context that saw no traffic; a per-domain run gates only that domain's contexts and is labelled scoped, and an unknown domain is refused by name. Each run clears its report folder but never removes it, writes a landing page before failing with a row per site, its request count and alert counts, publishes ZAP's log and machine-readable report as HTML, and the pass-or-fail decision is made by the suite's own gate rather than by the plans.
requirements.why: Every route this programme adds or changes must be driven through this scan to be attacked, and a new spec has to be written to these rules. The suite already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p11-037 to p11-102, p15-094 to p15-116 and p16-106 to p16-134 define the suite, its profiles, its contexts, its corpus and its three failure conditions; p16-144 to p16-148 give how a deployed run starts ZAP itself and publishes its report.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's security scan are not closed by this programme. No attacking spec drives the high-risk plants journey, so the plants backend is a declared context that nothing reaches and a full attacking run cannot pass the no-traffic gate as things stand; only a per-domain run avoids it. No transporter route is driven through the proxy. Only the refused side of the address book's cross-service hand-off is in scope, because no accepted token can be seeded. The attacking plan's note that the animals frontend's upload identifier is never reached is out of date.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps and a stale note in today's suite, not differences from the target design. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo signs each worker in once per domain and its tests restore that session, the saved state holding only the auth cookie and never written until a fresh context has proved it restores to a signed-in landing page; a spec that must start unauthenticated opts out with a cold-start state, and session reuse can be switched off, which caps the deployed run's workers. Only the session cookie is carried between a worker's tests, so each test starts signed in with no part-answered notification. Reuse was proved against one deployed environment by a probe that mints one session and reuses it across twenty fresh contexts, refuses to run against production, and is to be re-run before relying on reuse elsewhere. The sign-in password comes from the environment with a local stub default and is never written into a trace, the sign-in fixtures have their own longer timeout, no spec wipes the database because every spec creates the state it asserts on, and only internet-bound calls go through the platform's proxy.
requirements.why: Any new end-to-end proof of sign-in or navigation has to work within these existing suite rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-053 to p16-059 and p14-087 give the session rules, p14-082-m1 and p16-166 the password handling, p16-093 that nothing is wiped and p16-152 the proxy rule.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend serves a fixed list of routes, all behind sign-in: the dashboard at /, and the address book list, add, view, edit and delete pages. It also serves /health, /auth/* and static files, plus a dev-only address lookup spike. It owns no journey, notification editing, upload or event publishing, and no database. Its target direction is to become the front door for every journey.
requirements.why: This is the shell that the dashboard, templates and address book pages the target design changes are added to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-119 and p4-124 list the routes.

requirements.statement: Each INS dashboard row links out to the animals frontend, which owns that notification: to /notifications/{reference}, or to .../notification-view when it is submitted. Only the animals journey is linked today.
requirements.why: This is how the INS dashboard hands off across services today. The target design's dashboard is weighed in the dashboard area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-127 and p4-128 give the links.

requirements.statement: The INS dashboard at / is not scoped to the user's organisation: a signed-in user sees every organisation's notifications. This area does not fix that.
requirements.why: Organisation scoping of the dashboard is an authorisation defect owned by the dashboard area and an existing security ticket, not a layout or sign-in change. It goes to the report.

requirements.statement: The INS address book always sends the signed-in organisation to the address book API, and refuses to call it with none. Its ids are 24-character hex, and an unknown or deleted id gives 404. API field errors are mapped back to the form. Only the nine validated address fields are saved. The country list comes from reference data with GB first. A success banner shows once. A journey hand-off (journeyType, notificationId, fulfilmentId, handshakeToken) returns to the animals frontend for 'gbn-ag'.
requirements.why: These are the real persistence, validation and authorisation rules behind the address book that the navigation leads to. The address book area weighs its pages against the target design.

requirements.statement: Every change to the INS frontend follows its build rules. It stays in the govuk-frontend toolbox and keeps its four import boundaries. Each new page gets a URL builder, a route-list entry, English and Welsh copy with tests, unit tests mocked only at the network boundary, a browser test with axe checks and a Lighthouse audit. Format, lint, unit and browser suites must all pass, with cross-repo branches sharing one name. Every outside call is measured.
requirements.why: Templates and the navigation change land in the INS frontend, and these are the rules it holds every change to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-158, p4-163 and p4-163-m1 state the rules.

requirements.statement: Drift in the INS frontend's documentation and dependencies is not fixed by this programme. The workspace page names INS_MODE and AUTH_STUB_MODE where the repo uses STUB_MODE, and Vite where the repo uses webpack. It also calls the README template text when the README now describes the service. Some code imports Joi without declaring it as a dependency.
requirements.why: These are housekeeping defects, not differences from the target design. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The earlier parity programme's judgements and build notes that meet no difference in this area between a deployed service and the target design build nothing here. These are the section-caption rows, the navigation row's details, the return-control rename and the rule on which pages end with the return controls, the animals admin app keeping its own 'Sign out', and the notes on how that programme's backlog was run, numbered, banded, deferred and verified. Each stands only where its own area finds a deployed service and the target design clashing on that same difference.
requirements.why: The owner's ruling makes the DR1 parity backlog a source of judgements, never of requirements. Nothing is built because DR1 says so on its own. req-2082 records the same judgement over the DR1 notes' own run organisation and is carried here, so the two are one decision.

requirements.statement: The list's 'Status updated' glance card shows a live count for the category: the notifications whose status changed in the past 24 hours, matching the Status updated list its link opens.
requirements.why: The count is only useful if it agrees with the drill-down page; it depends on outcomes the authorities set after submission, and it is summary information, blocked with the Summary cards.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October), and the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes back to the notification record; no such feed exists today, so no real notification can be counted as status-updated.

requirements.statement: The germinal products list shows only germinal products notifications.
requirements.why: A trader looking at one category must not see another's notifications; the germinal list reads the category the animals backend stores on each notification's record.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of packages', from the notification's package count.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products in packages, not animals; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal cards from the animals backend's record, packages included.

requirements.statement: On a germinal products notification's card the commodity is the species then the product type, separated by a comma, such as 'Cattle, Semen'.
requirements.why: Germinal products need the product type as well as the species to say what is coming; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal cards from the animals backend's record (species and product type).

requirements.statement: A completed notification's status 'Completed' is plain styled text, not a tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses a tag only for statuses that ask something of the trader; no completed status reaches the service until the authorities' outcomes do (req-1082).
requirements.blockedBy: A real source of completion exists (Sam, 16 November) and the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes, completed among them, back to the notification record; no completed status reaches the service today (as req-1082).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the origin page's Back link goes to the notification type question when the notification was started from it, to the germinal products set's own notifications list when started from that list, and to the notification overview when the page was opened from the overview.
requirements.why: The target design ties the Back link to where the user came from, and its germinal journey returns to the germinal products list; the 9 October ruling splits req-013 by set, and each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals page plus the prototype's germinal differences. The afternoon ruling gives the germinal set its own list at its root. Templates are dropped for now, so no template review is a destination.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products set exists in the animals frontend today, and the notification type question offers no germinal option (repo-tests-p14-095).

requirements.statement: Out of scope: copying how the prototype starts a notification internally: clearing its session journey and template-creation flag on a new start, its marker for a journey started from a category dashboard, the redirect of the type page outside Design Release 2.1, its error clearing on showing the type page, the list of type labels it accepts as values, and its time-based reference fallback with no clash check.
requirements.why: The prototype decides look and feel only; these are its session and data mechanics, and no requirement is adopted because the prototype is built a certain way (9 October ruling). The real services start a notification by creating a record whose reference the backend keeps unique.

requirements.statement: Answering Yes and entering a region code with no country chosen keeps the typed code on the page but saves no region of origin code until a country gives it its prefix.
requirements.why: The target design's rule for a code with no country; without a country there is no prefix to make a full code. The afternoon ruling says it stands.

requirements.statement: The live-animals set's commodity catalogue holds only live-animal commodities: the germinal-product lines in it come out, so the live-animals commodity search never offers semen, embryos or ova.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling 10 November puts commodity search in a separate ticket's hands and names a 'cattle' search listing germinal codes as that ticket's work rather than this backlog's, which outranks the 9 October afternoon reading that splitting today's lines between sets is set architecture and goes ahead here. Ruling 2026-10-09's intent that each set's catalogue holds only its own commodities still stands as the target state; it is the separate ticket that reaches it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 12 germinal lines sit in the live-animals commodity catalogue (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026).

requirements.statement: The commodity choice is saved as the notification's commodity lines, one per chosen commodity-and-species pair, in commodity-code then Latin-name order with duplicates dropped: saving keeps the line of a pair still chosen with its quantities and identifier records, adds a line with blank quantities for a newly chosen pair, and drops the line of a pair no longer chosen, and each line is published with its commodity code, Latin name, common name, number of animals and number of packages. The prototype's hidden selection fields, its 'main commodity' and its generated species ids are not copied.
requirements.why: The commodity line is the real service's data model, which quantities and identifier records hang off; ruling 2026-10-09 says the prototype never decides field names or data-model shape (c-223).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-046 and -p9-047 write one line per commodity-and-species pair and reconcile the lines by key so an answered line keeps its details, -p9-037 and -p9-038 hold the commodity-code then Latin-name order, -p9-026 and repo-tests-p1-129 the code-and-Latin-name key, and -p9-087 what a line publishes.

requirements.statement: Every form on the commodity page and Commodity details (the quantities form and the Remove table form) posts the CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, with the browser's own validation switched off so every refusal is the service's own message.
requirements.why: Saves must be protected against forged posts and against two sessions overwriting each other, a real persistence constraint the prototype does not model, and server-side checks must be the only ones a trader meets.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-077 and -p10-156 carry the crumb and the concurrency token on both pages' forms, and -p9-078 and -p10-157 turn the browser's validation off.

requirements.why: Ruling 2026-10-09 keeps every real URL path and says no increment changes one to match the prototype (c-224).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-001 and -p10-001 serve the pages at the journey slugs commodities and consignment-details, repo-tests-p1-073 and -p1-110 address them the same way, and repo-frontend-p9-096 opens the search page from the overview task 'What are you importing?'.

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 clears the search text on every visit and save; the trader starts from their saved selection, not an old query.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-028 and repo-tests-p1-086 show the typed-but-unsaved counts kept after a removal now, and repo-frontend-p10-029 the surviving line falling back to its stored value with a warning logged; trace-animals-fit-p9-068 captured the earlier loss (c-374).

requirements.statement: Commodity details shows no total of animals or packages; the numbers saved on it are what the overview adds up into its commodity totals (for example '27 Animals' and '6 Packages/boxes').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 carries totals for the overview only; the trader sees the totals on the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p9-078 shows no totals on the page and trace-animals-fit-p9-040 shows the overview summing them today.

requirements.statement: The k6 performance suite's live-animals walk keeps working after the step-order change: it walks the main import reason page between the commodity page and Commodity details.
requirements.why: Moving the reason page (req-118) changes the step list the suite walks; trade-imports-performance-tests changes in each increment whose change breaks one of its k6 scripts, because the 7 October ruling works out which repos change from the evidence (c-225).

requirements.statement: On the germinal-products set's Commodity details the error summary lists errors by question, all species for one question before the next: every total gross weight error, then every number of packages error. Temperature is optional and raises no error (c-232).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 orders the error summary by field type; ruling 2026-10-09 splits req-114 per set. The V4 germinal data fields make temperature optional, so its error is not built.

requirements.statement: On the germinal products set the overview's Commodity details task shows Complete only when every chosen species has a valid number of packages (a whole number of 1 or more, within the limit req-1789 sets) and any total gross weight entered is valid; total gross weight and temperature are optional and do not hold it back. With no species chosen it is not complete.
requirements.why: The task status tells the trader what is left to do; ruling 2026-10-09 splits req-126 per set. The V4 germinal data fields make the number of packages mandatory to proceed and total gross weight and temperature optional (c-232), so Design Release 2.1's bar of a weight above 0 and a temperature is not built.

requirements.statement: Choosing a commodity for plants for planting, potatoes or wood products.
requirements.why: Out of scope: Design Release 2.1 offers nothing to choose for the plants types, and the high-risk plants frontend's own commodity type, list and details pages stay as they are, since no row in this area changes a page in the form plants has it.

requirements.statement: Prototype data these pages never show: per-commodity certification purpose lists, clearing a package type on save, and the 'code (common name - Latin name)' species title.
requirements.why: Out of scope here: Design Release 2.1 does not render any of them on the commodity page or Commodity details (the additional details page uses one global purpose list, and package type is de-scoped), so there is nothing a user can see to build.

requirements.statement: The destination country list is not edited in code to the 41 entries the target design holds, such as its Crown Dependencies shown with '(United Kingdom)' or its 'Republic of Ireland'. Where reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries and subdivisions differ from them, the difference goes to the list's owner as an MDM content question.
requirements.why: The 9 October ruling makes list content MDM's: a difference from the target design is never a reason to block a row or edit a list in code. DR1's deferral to the MDM integration no longer holds back the change, and gives no date for it.

requirements.statement: No exit-only list of animal-approved border control posts is built for the port of exit: neither the ten posts the target design holds (for example 'Holyhead POE - GBHLY') nor a new reference-data endpoint. Nor is the hint 'Exit and entry share the same port list.' that DR1 expected while its block stood.

requirements.why: The target design shows each exit port as its name then its code, after a hyphen. It wins by default on how an option reads, and no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers the label. The stored value stays the code.

requirements.statement: The 'Port of exit' questions list the ports in the same order as the ports-of-entry list: airports first, then seaports, then rail ports in their own group. Within each group, ports are sorted A to Z by name, ignoring letter case, with non-breaking and doubled spaces normalised before comparing.

The traffic value reaches /ports-of-entry under req-304's row, which this follows.

requirements.statement: The main import reason page stays at the slug import-reason and Additional details at additional-details. Their form fields stay reasonForImport, purposeInInternalMarket, temporaryAdmissionExitDate, animalsCertifiedFor and containsUnweanedAnimals, and every radio keeps a label tied to its input by id.

The performance-test suite also drives these pages by these slugs, field names and labels.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the identification page's 'Selected commodities' quantity column is headed 'Number of packages' and shows each species' saved count, where live animals show Number of animals.
requirements.why: The germinal half of req-209, split by the 9 October ruling. DR2.1 counts germinal products in packages, and each set now holds one category, so the germinal set always shows this heading.

requirements.statement: How a germinal notification's identification details show on the review page (rows for Donor name/ID, Collection date, Production date and Identification number/mark).
requirements.why: Weighed here and left out: the review page's rows belong to the review-and-submit area.

requirements.statement: The ruling's germinal architecture as it touches this page: the germinal set has its own copy of the identification page, taken from the live-animals feature folder once this programme has built the live twin, at the live-animals slug under the germinal set; where donor details are stored is decided from the real model, not the prototype.
requirements.why: Every germinal requirement in this area (req-252, req-255 to req-259 and the germinal halves) is built in that copy, not in the live page. The copy itself is the germinal-products area's to build.

requirements.statement: Germinal products is its own set in trade-imports-animals-frontend, SET_ID 'germinal-products', mounted at /germinal-products beside live-animals, with its own journey, obligations, flow, cookies, gateway (routes-germinal-products.js) and set services. Its journey pages sit at /germinal-products/notifications/{journeyId}/{slug} using the live-animals slugs, each a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the germinal differences; its overview, check answers, declaration and confirmation pages are its own copies too. Every live-animal field not marked as applying to the animal journey only is carried over; the CPH number and permanent address, which apply to the animal journey only, are not, so the set has no CPH number page and no permanent address page. The plants frontend has no germinal set, so no germinal-only difference changes plants.
requirements.why: Duplicating pages via features is the app's architecture and is desired, and option B of the germinal options paper was chosen over option A; the prototype's flat paths are not copied. V4's germinal section marks its seven fields as affecting the germinal journey only and names only the CPH number and permanent address as not required for germinal products, without saying which other live-animal fields the germinal journey drops or keeps and without a header row of its own, so the germinal field list is read from the ruling's copy rule plus V4's own per-field markings rather than from the germinal table alone (req-1832, req-1833). The copy of each live-animals page is taken after this programme has built the live twin. The 9 October afternoon ruling leaves plants unchanged by rows it has no equivalent of and never mirrors animals-only data into it.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification is created with Draft status and the same kind of reference as a live-animals one, GBN-AG followed by the two-digit year and six characters, shown in the status strip from the first page; no GBN-GP reference is ever issued.
requirements.why: Germinal notifications keep GBN-AG references; GBN-GP references are demonstration data only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today only live-animals notifications exist; each is minted a GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX reference at creation (repo-frontend-p2-009, trace-e2e-p13-004, repo-tests-p2-115).

requirements.statement: Searching 'semen' in the germinal set lists the eight semen commodities in name order (Cat, Semen; Cattle, Semen (05111000); Dog, Semen; Goat, Semen; Horse, Semen; Pig, Semen; Rabbit/Rodent, Semen; Sheep, Semen, all others 05119985), offering 12 species rows, and the live region announces '12 results available'; Cattle, Semen offers 'Bovidae' and Rabbit/Rodent, Semen offers 'Rabbit/Rodent' as group rows.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the commodity search is handled by a separate ticket rather than by this work, and a search listing germinal codes belongs to that ticket (ruling:sam-2026-11-10, c-382). What the search would list is a commodity catalogue's content, which is MDM's and is never edited in code (c-282, req-093).

requirements.statement: Ticking a germinal species, such as Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) under Cattle, Semen, shows '1 selected' with a 'Cattle, Semen (05111000):' line and a 'Bos taurus' chip, as the live-animal search does.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows germinal selections the same way as live-animal ones, and the germinal commodity page is a copy of its live-animals twin, so its selected panel is the live page's panel over the germinal lines the catalogue holds.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight that is not a number greater than 0 (digits with an optional decimal part; no sign, commas or units), such as 0, shows 'Enter a number greater than 0', linked from the error summary to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 and Design Release 2.1 both require the weight to be above 0; Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight over 1,000 shows 'Total gross weight must be 1,000kg or less', linked to that species' field and shown inline; 1,000 itself is accepted.
requirements.why: V4 caps the total gross weight at 1,000 kg. Its conditions cell is empty, so neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 gives the message or says what happens at exactly 1,000; the message and the inclusive limit follow the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight accepts up to 2 decimal places (1.5 and 24.50 are accepted); more shows 'Total gross weight must have 2 decimal places or fewer', linked to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 gives the weight to 2 decimal places, with 24.50 as its example, and the ruling holds it as a decimal; Design Release 2.1 accepts 1.5. V4 states no rounding rule, so a figure with more decimal places is refused with a message rather than rounded, following the GOV.UK pattern.

requirements.statement: Number of packages is required: left blank, it shows 'Enter the number of packages', linked from the error summary to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 makes the line's quantity mandatory to proceed, the only mandatory field in its germinal section, and Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: A Number of packages that is not a whole number of 1 or more, such as 'x', shows 'Enter a whole number greater than 0', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts packages in whole numbers from 1; V4 gives the quantity a maximum but no minimum, no decimal-place rule and an empty conditions cell, so it sets no minimum of its own and the prototype decides.

requirements.statement: A Number of packages over 1,000 shows 'Number of packages must be 1,000 or less', linked to that species' field and shown inline; 1,000 itself is accepted.

requirements.statement: Each germinal products trade line in the published GBN-AG payload carries the typeCode for its product type: SEMEN for a semen line, EMBRYO for an embryos line and OVA for an ova line. A commodity that is embryos and a commodity that is ova are separate commodities, each its own trade line, never one 'Embryos/Ova' line.
requirements.why: The GBN-AG schema names these codes, and the 9 October ruling makes the schema, not the prototype's mock data, decide them. The rule is written by product type, so a separate ova commodity takes OVA as soon as the catalogue holds one; a combined 'Embryos/Ova' line, while the catalogue holds one, takes EMBRYO (req-1928). A catalogue's content is MDM's and is never a reason to block a row (c-282). Live-animal lines carry LIVE_ANIMAL (req-1894).
requirements.deltaNote: Today trade lines carry no typeCode (repo-backend-p6-109, c-273). Until this lands, today's lines carry the interim codes of req-1928.

requirements.statement: The roles an address can hold read, in order, with these hints: 'Place of Origin' ('The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'), 'Consignor' ('This is the sender of the consignment.'), 'Consignee' ('This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'), 'Importer' ('This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.'), 'Place of Destination' ('This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.'), then, after a divider, 'Branch Address' ('This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's address type list is the wording for the six roles an address can hold, and it also names the categories the list's tabs and Type filter group by; the choice itself is made on the add-and-edit area's roles step.

requirements.statement: The stored notification record holds its category, live animals or germinal products, beside its status and reference at the document root, and a record with no category is read everywhere as live animals, so every notification stored before the germinal set exists stays a live-animals notification without a data migration. The category is held on the record only and travels on no notification event, so the event envelope and the shared event schemas stay as they are. The field's name and values are the animals backend's to choose in its own conventions.
requirements.why: Germinal products is a sibling set of live animals in the animals frontend and both keep their records in the one animals backend; the stored category is what tells the two apart.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-002 shows the record today holds identity and metadata at the root and content under notification, with no category. Keeping the category off the event, and trade-imports-schemas unchanged, is what c-272 and c-296 settled.

requirements.statement: The backend's create (POST /notifications with no reference number) takes the category the set starting the notification sends and stores it, and no later save, submit, amend, cancel-amend or copy changes it. A notification holds commodities of its one category only, never a mix of live animals and germinal products, so choosing the other type in the journey starts a new notification of that category and the abandoned draft keeps the category it was created with.
requirements.why: One category per set and per notification is what lets each set open only its own notifications, and the ruling drops every mixed-load case.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-001 shows create today takes no category. The sets send it under req-1856 and req-1857, and the change of type that starts the other category's notification is req-008.

requirements.statement: The read the frontend opens a notification with, the fulfilments view GET /notifications/{referenceNumber}/fulfilments, returns the stored category, an absent one read as live animals, so each set's cross-set guard can refuse to open the other category's notifications.
requirements.why: The frontend's cross-set guard reads the stored category, so the backend must hand it back where the frontend already rehydrates from.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p3-019 lists what the fulfilments view returns today, which has no category; that view is req-1557's.

requirements.statement: Every outbox event the backend publishes for a notification would carry the notification's category as an optional top-level category field, with trade-imports-schemas gaining it as an optional property on event-envelope-v1, so the INS backend could file it under live animals or germinal products.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling withdraws the morning ruling's event publishing: the category is stored on the record only, trade-imports-schemas does not change, and every INS reader of the category is blocked or moved to the animals frontend. Until the INS dashboard is re-distilled, today's INS table lists germinal notifications without their category; c-272 is reopened then.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p5-011 shows today's event envelope: no category anywhere on it.

Where they sit on the record, on the per-item identifier entries of each line as the record holds animal identifiers, or on the species line, is decided in the build from the real model rather than from the prototype's shape.

requirements.statement: Journey pages keep today's URL paths: the live-animals set at /live-animals, a notification's overview at /live-animals/notifications/{reference} with no slug, a new notification created at /live-animals/notifications, and each page at /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/{slug} with today's slugs (origin, commodities, consignment-details, commodities/identification, import-reason, additional-details, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, accompanying-documents, addresses, cph-number, permanent-address, the five party pickers, consignment/contact/select, notification-view, declaration, confirmation). requirements.statement: The performance suite signs in as a browser does: it follows a frontend's redirect chain through that frontend's /auth/sign-in, the Defra ID stub's sign-in form (posting the stub identity's CRN 2100010101 and a password) and /auth/callback back to the page asked for. It counts any hop through /auth/, an identity-provider path containing /oauth2/ or /idphub/, or /organisations as sign-in, counts a chain that lands with 200 without showing the form as sign-in, and never counts one that ends in a server error. It tags the post 'sign-in' and any later sign-in as re-authentication, checks that the INS sign-in went through Defra ID, and shares one cookie jar between the INS frontend and the journey frontend so the INS sign-in carries over to the live-animals dashboard.

A stale concurrency token answered with a redirect counts as handled, and a request that is still redirecting after 10 hops fails its check.

requirements.statement: Plants keeps its own arrival date rules: the date must be a real calendar date given with a four-digit year, a blank date gives 'Enter the arrival date', a date that names no real day gives 'Enter a real arrival date', and only when the consignment has already arrived may it not be after today in Europe/London ('The date the consignment arrived cannot be in the future', with the date picker capped at today); potatoes and not-yet-arrived plants or wood have no bound in either direction, and a notification made outside a timing window is accepted, never refused.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps arrival details' own rules to animals and lets plants keep its own questions and data. Plants' panel ruled out the animals window, which would refuse a late potato notification.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers keep their own questions and place in the journey. The place of destination is asked in one of three states: for potatoes and for a consignment not yet arrived it is headed 'Place of destination' and reads 'Where the goods will be kept after arrival. This is where a plant health inspector may carry out a spot check.'; once arrived it is headed 'Where is the consignment now?' and reads 'Give the address where the consignment is being kept. If it is still on its way to its intended destination, give that destination. A plant health inspector may carry out a spot check here.' The consignor is headed 'Consignor' and reads 'This is the sender of the consignment.', is asked only while it is in the notification's scope, and on a potatoes notification is skipped with its answer purged and its path redirected to the overview, logged once. Each is opened from its own overview task row, sits on the full-width surface, shows the held copy in a summary card titled 'Current consignor' or 'Current place of destination' with an 'Edit details' link, ends with 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub', and replaces any earlier choice when saved.
requirements.why: Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm mirrors structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour into plants while plants keeps its own questions, sections, step order and data; plants' pickers are overview tasks, so under DR1 rule (b) they keep the three return controls that the animals pickers, reached from the consignment addresses page, do not have.

A status is mirrored in the plants frontend only where plants has the same lifecycle. 'Completed' is a status only once a real source of completion exists.
requirements.why: The animals frontend throws on a status it does not know, and the INS dashboard sends only SUBMITTED notifications to the review, so a status the backend sends before they know it breaks every page that reads it; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes statuses add-only, and the 16 November ruling keeps the enum at four by withdrawing the one status this programme would have added and holding 'Completed' out until a real source of completion exists.

The one status the 9 October afternoon ruling named is withdrawn by the 16 November ruling, recorded as this area's conflict on that status; 'Completed' waits on a real source of completion (req-1082), and whether plants takes a status is decided when the row that adds one unblocks.
