requirements.why: Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling makes inc-004 (page endings while amending, req-1624 and req-1403) change plants in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today plants' pages end the same whether or not the notification is being amended: the commodities list page offers 'Save and continue' alone (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-103), and a question page's way out of the overview is a 'Cancel and return to overview' link that saves nothing (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-104). Plants amends a submitted notification from its dashboard card (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-108).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey has its own sections, steps and step order: five ordered sections — start, about the consignment, arrival and destination, consignment parties and review — with the notification list and the task-list hub in none of them; an opening run of commodity type, the commodities list, origin, arrival status, arrival details, place of destination, consignor, identification numbers and the consignment contact picker, skipping any step whose question does not apply, so a potato notification leaves out the arrival status question and the consignor picker; a commodity details sub-page reached from the commodities list that is never a run step and leaves by the journey's own order; every page after commodity type needing it answered; and the declaration held as the journey's only flow-only answer, which never counts as progress. Animals-only data (species, animal identification, CPH, transit countries) is never mirrored into plants.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling has plants mirror structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour while keeping its own questions, sections, step order and data, and never mirrors animals-only data; plants' flow already works this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p2-074 to repo-plantsfrontend-p2-079: plants' five sections and the pages in each; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-084 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-085: the opening run and the potato branch that leaves out the arrival status and the consignor; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-086 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-087: the commodity details sub-page is not a run step; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-081: the declaration is the journey's only flow-only answer.

requirements.statement: In the high-risk plants frontend, opening a notification's hub or any journey page other than commodity type by URL sends the trader to that notification's commodity type page when the notification holds no answer they entered; the create path, the commodity type page and anything beneath it, and the amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete actions are exempt, a path naming a notification that does not exist is refused as not found, and the guard runs only on the plants set's own notification routes.
requirements.why: Real notifications are server records reachable by URL, a real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express; plants' entry guard is the same rule as live animals' and already in place.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p2-098 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-100: the hub and every journey page past the commodity type page are guarded, and a notification with no entered answer is sent to its commodity type page; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-096 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-097: the commodity type page and the four actions are exempt; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-094 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-095: the guard runs only on the set's own notification paths.

requirements.statement: Each plants journey page carries its section's caption above its heading, set per section: 'Dashboard' on the notification list, 'About the consignment' on commodity type, the commodities list, commodity details and origin, 'Arrival' on arrival status and arrival details, 'Destination' on the place of destination, and 'Addresses' on the consignor picker and identification numbers; the task-list hub, the consignment contact picker, check your answers, the declaration and the confirmation carry none, and a page the caption map does not name carries none. Every page in the flow is either captioned or listed as deliberately bare, each page files under exactly one caption section, and no caption string goes unused. The Welsh captions are machine-drafted and do not ship to users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: A caption names where a page sits in the notification, one per section. Plants keeps its own sections, so its captions stay its own, and the owner's 17 November ruling words the addresses section 'Addresses'.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p2-107 to repo-plantsfrontend-p2-111: plants' pages carry these captions today, the consignor picker and identification numbers reading 'Addresses'; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-112 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-113: the five bare pages and an unnamed page; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-114: the completeness checks; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-115: the Welsh sign-off constraint.

requirements.statement: The plants set's structure holds: thirteen journey pages are dispatch pages that take part in gating and task rows, the notification list and the task-list hub are not, deleting a notification and cancelling an amendment are actions rather than steps, and the party-edit page is reached only from a picked address's Edit details link; the notification's rule manifest holds twenty-five obligations with the commodity lines as its only group; ten features collect the answers and every obligation is collected by exactly one page, with no two pages claiming the same one; no two obligations share an id or a name, no chain of nested obligations loops, and every conditional obligation declares the answers its condition reads; and the set refuses to start when a configuration seam is unfilled, a journey cookie is unregistered or an obligation carries display wording.
requirements.why: These are the plants frontend's recorded structure and boot checks; every plants flow change in this area lands through them, as live animals' do, and each set keeps owning its own pages.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p12-027 to repo-plantsfrontend-p12-029: the thirteen dispatch pages and what is not one; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-035 and repo-plantsfrontend-p12-061: the twenty-five obligations and the single group; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-080 and repo-plantsfrontend-p12-083: one page per obligation; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-031 and repo-plantsfrontend-p12-034: the boot checks.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants set keeps its own questions and data: the commodity type, the commodity lines and their category-driven fields, the country of origin, the arrival status, the arrival date, the expected time of arrival and proposed place of landing, the place of destination, the consignor, the identification numbers and the contact address, each applying only to the commodity types the set says it does; which categories ask for a per-line field, and which countries a category may come from, are the set's own commodity service's content, read when a rule is checked rather than at start-up; each notification window is held in one place so every hint that names it and every lateness decision read the same figure; the obligation manifest holds no length, character set or error wording; and every plants string lands in both locale files with no invented Welsh.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling has plants keep its own questions and data while mirroring structure and behaviour, so plants' own decisions bound what a mirrored change may do.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p12-037 to repo-plantsfrontend-p12-059: the questions a plants notification owes and the commodity types each applies to; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-048 and repo-plantsfrontend-p12-052: the per-line fields and the origin restrictions come from the set's own commodity service; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-086: each notification window is held in one place; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-118: the manifest holds no length, character set or error wording.

requirements.statement: The behaviours the plants rulings ledger parks are not built by this programme: users, sign-in models, agents and delegation; internal-user login; bulk upload, reusing a previous consignment and importing from existing documents; plant-operator registration; regulator, inspector and analyst screens, captures or exports; list maintenance, risk classification and spot-check scheduling; document uploads; lawful basis, privacy notice and retention; refinements from the pre-2021 scheme and the Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland services; and a meaning for 'sustainable'.
requirements.why: The plants ledger parks each of these until policy or a plants source supplies what is missing, and the goal brings plants in only where it shares a page or behaviour with the animals sets. The ledger itself is no longer in this area's working set, so the parked list is recorded here and the ledger is read where it now sits.

requirements.statement: Every journey page works fully without JavaScript, and CSS and JavaScript only enhance a page that already works: every state change is a form post, every search or filter is a form with a submitting button that keeps the term the trader typed, and nothing a trader needs is shown only by script. Journey behaviour is built from GOV.UK Frontend first, then the accepted government components (the accessible autocomplete over a native select, and the Ministry of Justice date picker and sub navigation); no increment writes custom JavaScript to copy the prototype, the Ministry of Justice Modal dialog and Copy button are not used, and any other component needs design's case. A prototype behaviour that needs JavaScript no accepted component gives is built in its no-JavaScript version, with the JavaScript-only part its own increment in the waiting-on-design theme, one per design question, changing plants too where the row does.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling sets the toolbox and graceful-degradation rule for every page. Today's journey pages already use GOV.UK Frontend with the Ministry of Justice date picker and the accessible autocomplete, and render on the server.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-114 and trace-animals-fit-p1-091: today's pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components with a few app-specific hooks; repo-frontend-p3-012 and repo-plantsfrontend-p12-103: a reference-list field is an enhanced search box with JavaScript and a plain select without it; repo-frontend-p3-067, repo-frontend-p3-102 and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-062: a search submits on the server and a page can be reopened with JavaScript switched off; repo-frontend-p3-115: pages are held to the GOV.UK toolbox's own styles.

requirements.statement: In every set, readiness works like this: a task row whose question does not apply reads 'Not applicable' and owes nothing; a row with no mandatory part reads 'Optional' while untouched and then 'In progress' or 'Complete'; a row whose stored answers no longer pass its own pages' rules reads 'To do' however complete the engine counts it; a row's link opens the first of its pages whose gate passes and falls back to the row's first page; a card on the review page shows one broken-answer message; the rows roll up into readiness for check your answers; and the overview's 'Review and submit' button reaches the review page whatever is still owed. A row is held back only by the answers a later page is enforced to have — the country of origin and at least one commodity line — and the page that asks for the earliest missing one is offered instead.
requirements.why: The target design enforces completeness through the overview's statuses and the review page, which is how the real journey already works; the step-order and return changes in this area rely on it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-087 to repo-frontend-p1-091: the five row statuses, the roll-up and the demotion of a row whose saved answers no longer pass; repo-frontend-p1-070: a row's link opens the first of its pages whose gate passes; repo-frontend-p1-061 and repo-frontend-p3-109: the country of origin and a commodity line are the only answers a later page is held back for; trace-e2e-p14-097 and repo-tests-p8-018: 'Review and submit' reaches the review whatever is still owed.

requirements.statement: The live-animals obligation model's scope and mandatory rules for the journey's shared answers are these: the country of origin, whether a region-of-origin code is required, the reason for import, the arrival date at the port, the port of entry, the means of transport, the transport identification, the transport document reference, the five consignment parties, the contact address and what the animals are certified for are always asked and mandatory; the country-of-origin subdivision code and the trader's internal reference are always in scope and optional; the region-of-origin code is always in scope and switches from optional to mandatory when the trader says a code is required, keeping its stored value when the answer changes; the transporter type is always mandatory while the commercial and private transporter records are mutually exclusive and each in scope only for its own type; the transited countries are asked of rail and road consignments only and are never compulsory; a conditional answer whose in-scope decision names no mandate counts as mandatory; a notification must hold at least one commodity line; and the notification's reference number is system-populated, mandatory and asked by no page.
requirements.why: These are today's obligation rules for the journey's shared answers; nothing in the target design or the rulings changes them, and the step-order and return changes must not either.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-123 to repo-frontend-p1-148: the country of origin, the arrival date, the port of entry, the means of transport, the transport identification and document reference, the five consignment parties, the contact address and the reason for import are always asked and mandatory; repo-frontend-p1-124 and repo-frontend-p1-149: the subdivision code and the internal reference are optional; repo-frontend-p1-126 and repo-frontend-p1-178: the region-of-origin code stays in scope and only its mandate swaps; repo-frontend-p1-153: at least one commodity line is required; repo-frontend-p1-151: the reference number is system-populated and no page asks for it.

requirements.statement: Claims in this area's working set that describe one page's own content, one page's own data or one page's own rules are weighed in that page's area, not here: the type question, the overview's headings, groups, row names, hints and commodity totals, the review page's sections, cards and Change and Edit links, commodity lines, species, identifiers and their panels, documents and their cap, the CPH number boxes, transporters and their add pages, party pickers, same-as buttons and add-address hand-offs, the address book, the dashboards and drill-downs, amend, copy and delete landings, template mode's endings and skipped steps, the germinal hub and dashboard, the service header, navigation, phase banner and security headers, the reference lists each field offers, plants' own page content, and DR1's judgements on the dashboard, the address pickers, the reference lists and the identifier rule.
requirements.why: This area stops at any one page's own content; those pages' areas weigh the same behaviours against Design Release 2.1 and the rulings.

requirements.statement: How the DR1 parity build run was organised is not a requirement: its union of runs A and C, increment numbering and provenance blocks, corpus profiles and report locations, frozen source backlogs and the commits its findings were authored against, build target and verification ladder, the address-space and disputed-band holds and their parked branches, and the build order and code touch points of its own increments.
requirements.why: The DR1 notes count only for DR1 judgements on a difference the real frontend and Design Release 2.1 clash on; these notes record how that earlier programme was run, which judges no difference. This is the same judgement as req-1734, which now carries it: both say that DR1's own records build nothing on their own, and this id stays so that it still resolves.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, the Address book navigation item goes to the address-book URL its page context supplies, and this programme does not point it at the INS address book.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps plants off the INS address book, and where plants' Address book link goes is a decision parked with the plants service owner.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p13-007 renders the item with the address-book URL the page is given, so nothing here changes it.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, a page with errors shows a GOV.UK error summary titled 'There is a problem' ('Mae problem' in Welsh) at the top of the content, above the caption and heading. It lists one entry per field in the order the page's error map gives them, each carrying the first failing rule's message and linking to its field or, where a page asks, to another page. Each field shows the same message inline. The summary takes focus when shown, except on a page that shows it without the user having just been refused. A page with no errors shows none.
requirements.why: This is the GOV.UK error pattern every page shares, and it already exists. Each page's own messages against the target design belong to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-041 to p2-045, repo-insfrontend-p4-068 to p4-071 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-048 to p13-052 render the summary, trace-animals-fit-p1-005 shows it rendered, and repo-tests-p10-067 waits for it before scanning an error state.

requirements.statement: A signed-out user who opens any page of a frontend is sent through sign-in, with the page asked for (path and query) carried in a redirect parameter. After signing in they return to that page, or to the frontend's dashboard home when none was asked for, headed 'Import notification service' on the animals frontend. Only a relative path on the same service is followed, once; anything else goes to the home. Every page of a set is behind the session, and a draft's saved answers are still there after signing out and back in.
requirements.why: The target design's pretend sign-in always lands on its dashboard. The deployed services send the user back to where they were going, a real authentication behaviour the prototype cannot express, and it already works.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-001, p1-029, p1-048 and p1-049 show the animals round trip back to the page asked for, trace-e2e-p15-013 and p15-017 the INS one, repo-insfrontend-p4-088 to p4-092 the INS rules, and repo-tests-p6-067, p6-076 and p6-077 that a page part-way through the journey is protected and returned to.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, every page's browser title reads the page name, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - ', as on the animals frontend.
requirements.why: One title pattern on every page is the target design's, and the owner's rule is that a change to something plants also has changes plants in the same increment, mirroring wording patterns.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants frontend now joins the page name, the service name and GOV.UK with hyphens (repo-plantsfrontend-p13-003), as the animals frontend does (repo-frontend-p2-003), so the pipe pattern it had is already gone and only the INS frontend is left to change.

requirements.statement: The plants frontend's high-risk plants set mounts as its own plugin at /high-risk-plants, registering one flat route table assembled from its feature route modules: the notification list at the set base, the create and start paths, the task-list hub, each journey page as a GET and POST pair at its own slug, the three party pickers and their edit pages, and the delete-notification and cancel-amend actions. Its route extensions, the entry guard among them, are sandboxed to that plugin, so another set's routes never run its guards, and the guard runs before every route handler in the set.
requirements.why: This is the plants shell that every mirrored change lands in. It already exists, and the programme keeps plants' architecture as it is, with each set owning its own pages.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p12-001 and repo-plantsfrontend-p12-004: the set serves one flat route table under /high-risk-plants assembled from eighteen feature route modules; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-033-m1: every route is registered inside the set's own context; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-030 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-094: the guard runs before every route handler and only on the set's own notification paths.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, a question page the overview links to ends with three controls in one GOV.UK button group: the primary button ('Save and continue' unless the page names its own), a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link on its own line below them that leaves without saving. A page may add extra buttons or button-styled links straight after the primary one. Both save buttons make exactly the same checks: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one, and with none the answers are saved, 'Save and return to overview' showing the overview. A page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone, whichever primary label it uses. Saving a valid page goes to the next page of the journey that applies, or to the review page at the slug notification-view when none is left, and opens the page that asks for a required earlier answer when the next page needs one; the page just saved is recorded on the trail the next page carries. The labels come from the shared copy, with Welsh twins.
requirements.why: These are plants' save actions and return paths, built to the same rule as the animals frontend. The owner's 26 October ruling makes 'Save and return to overview' check exactly what 'Save and continue' checks, on every page that has both buttons, with no page an exception, so plants' shared save actions keep the checks they run today.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p13-036 to p13-044 give the page endings and their wording, p13-045 to p13-047 the destinations and the trail, and p13-090 the Welsh twins. The 26 October ruling withdraws the lenient save the 9 October afternoon ruling asked for, under which the secondary button would have saved past a blank required answer (c-313), so plants' shared save actions stay as built.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, a date is one text input about ten characters wide, in d/m/yyyy form, shown through the Ministry of Justice date picker, with a small bold label the page may ask to enlarge, an optional hint and an optional earliest and latest date. A date written in that form is read back as its day, month and year, a blank box comes back empty, and a date written any other way is kept as typed and shown back in the field.
requirements.why: This is the shared date field of plants' page kit. It already exists, and no row in this area changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p13-065 to p13-067 describe the field.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, a signed-in Defra ID session is the only precondition to notifying: every page the shared kit wires for a notification needs one, on the request that shows the page and on the request that saves it alike, and a page shown to anyone else carries the service name with no navigation. Each page, pre-handler and extension runs with its own set and the signed-in trader's verified organisation bound to the request, so no page can read another set's configuration or another organisation's data.
requirements.why: Sign-in is a real authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, and organisation scoping of a request is a persistence and authorisation constraint it cannot express either.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p13-033-m1 puts both the show and the save request behind the session, p13-009 hides the navigation from anyone else, and p13-081 binds the set and the verified organisation to every request.

requirements.statement: Plants' chrome mirrors the animals frontend's: the same service name 'Import notification service', the same APHA service-desk feedback address, the same GOV.UK privacy, cookies and accessibility-statement footer links, a placeholder Manage account and an Address book item whose destination its page context supplies. Nothing in this area settles a plants-specific service name, feedback address, helpdesk contact line, Address book or Manage account home, accessibility statement or privacy notice.
requirements.why: Those plants-specific destinations wait on the plants service owner, not on the target design. The programme mirrors the animals frontend's chrome, which plants already matches.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p13-002, p13-014 and p13-027 show plants already carrying the animals frontend's service name, feedback address and footer links, and p13-007 and p13-008 that the Address book and Manage account destinations are supplied from outside the chrome.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: a plants eligibility checker ('Is my consignment high-risk?') or a before-you-start page ahead of the plants journey's first page. The plants journey starts on its own commodity type question.
requirements.why: No source asks for one: the target design has no such page for plants, no ruling asks for it, and the afternoon ruling has plants keep its own questions and step order, with the opening run starting on commodity type.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set's identification page, Collection date and Production date are each a single text input with the hint 'For example, 27/03/2026', which works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives both dates this hint, and the 9 October afternoon ruling builds them now as single text inputs. Same change as req-252 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, an Identification number/mark over 58 characters shows 'Identification number/mark must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline; any characters are accepted up to that length.
requirements.why: V4 limits the identification number or mark to 58 characters and sets no character set, pattern or minimum length, its example GB1238765 being an example rather than a format; Design Release 2.1 gives the message in the Donor name/ID pattern. Same change as req-255 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Collection date not in the form day/month/four-digit year shows 'Enter a collection date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid DD/MM/YYYY collection date; the message follows Design Release 2.1's production date message. Same change as req-256 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Production date not in the form day/month/four-digit year, such as 2026-09-01, shows 'Enter a production date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid DD/MM/YYYY production date and Design Release 2.1 gives the message. Same change as req-257 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Collection date in the right format that is not a real date, such as 99/99/2026, shows 'Collection date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid collection date and Design Release 2.1 gives the message. Same change as req-258 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Production date in the right format that is not a real date shows 'Production date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid production date; the message follows Design Release 2.1's collection date message. Same change as req-259 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the identification page's 'Selected commodities' quantity column is headed 'Number of packages' and shows each species' saved count, where live animals show Number of animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products by package on the identification page too. Same change as req-1776 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: Plants' confirmation page carries a 'What happens next' sentence saying the relevant plant health authority may carry out a spot check.
requirements.why: Out of scope: Design Release 2.1 asks for no such sentence, and a plants change that needs trade-imports-plants-backend is left out of this programme. The sentence plants' own decision keeps but the built page lacks is a plants-internal gap, which goes to the report.

requirements.statement: Without JavaScript, and until the commercial transporter's address search is built, every address and contact field on 'Add a commercial transporter' shows from the start, so a trader can always enter the address by hand.
requirements.why: Every page works fully without JavaScript, and manual address entry is never blocked on the address lookup; the hidden-fields layout is only an enhancement on top (req-458).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-017 asks every address and contact field on the commercial form in order with nothing hidden, which trace-animals-fit-p20-036 shows as rendered.

requirements.statement: Claims in this area's working set about pages next to the consignment addresses page and the pickers are built in their own areas, not here: the success banner, the hand-off to the INS address book and the return from it, and the 'Edit details' link on a copied party (party-address-add-and-edit); the CPH number page and the permanent address page behind their sections, and the contact address page's own content, page size and restatement (cph-permanent-and-contact); the review page's addresses and contact cards, their Change and Edit details links, the 'Complete consignment addresses' error and the 'Correct the address details for the consignor' error (review-and-submit); the page endings while amending or editing a template (journey-flow, templates); the transit countries and transport details task rows and the transporter list (transport-and-transporters); the INS address book's own pages and the dashboard link to them (address-book); and plants' confirmation page copy (review-and-submit).
requirements.why: Recorded so every claim in this area is weighed: each describes another page's content, and its own area's requirements carry what is built.

requirements.statement: While a trader is creating or changing a live animals or germinal products template, each party picker's 'Add a new address' round trip and each role's 'Edit details' page work as they do in a notification, on the same pages: the handshake identifies the template being worked on, saving or cancelling on the INS add page returns to that template's own picker or Consignment addresses page with the template's answer set as it would be for a notification, and an edit changes only the template's copy, never the address book record. Nothing returns the trader to a notification.
requirements.why: Template mode is another way of walking the same journey pages and captures the same data; it never copies or forks the pages, and later page changes carry into it without rework (ruling 2026-10-09 templates). Today's handshake and edit pages are built around a notification, so without this a trader adding an address while building a template would lose their place.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no template mode: the add-an-address handshake sends the notification id and the return lands on that notification's picker. The pickers' paging at eight a page and their 'Selected address' restatement come with the pages template mode walks, rather than being set again here. Which checks template mode relaxes is settled by the template-mode checks question, not by this row. Animals only: template mode is not added to plants.
requirements.blockedBy: Sam decides to pick templates up again: templates are de-prioritised and the templates rows are parked and not built now (ruling:sam-2026-11-04), and templates are dropped for now (ruling:interaction-designer-2026-11-09), with no condition named for their return.

requirements.statement: The plants review page's contact card re-reads the contact from the organisation's address book by its id instead of showing the copy the contact page saved.
requirements.why: Out of scope, and no longer the case: plants' review now shows the name held on the notification's own copy of the address rather than the address book record it was picked from, which is the copy semantics plants' own decision and the animals contact page keep.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p10-067: a party card shows the name held on the notification's own copy of the address, not the name of the address book record it was picked from.

requirements.statement: Fit tests for plants' check answers, declaration and confirmation that the suite lacks: the already-arrived labels and the plants and wood late rule, the outstanding-party errors, a refused or failed submission, and an accessibility check on the review tests that run none.
requirements.why: A gap in the plants test suite, not a look-and-feel difference from Design Release 2.1. It goes to the report; each increment that changes one of these pages proves its own change with its own tests.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p10-143 covers only the draft review and the origin error, p10-162 to p10-164 name what the slice leaves unsaid, and p11-023, p11-039 and p11-062 cover only the declaration, the late view and the confirmation.

requirements.statement: Inspector-side live access to a submitted plants notification, and a late-notification indicator projected into the plants backend's notification record for the regulator side, are not built.

The two ledger claims this rested on left this area in the re-extraction; req-2025 now carries the inspector-side half, and this id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list, a submitted notification that still has items outstanding shows what is outstanding as plain text on its card under the reference.
requirements.why: Not built: the 16 November ruling withdraws the 'Action required' tag and everything action-required from the list until the outstanding-actions banner the dashboard designs under test introduce is agreed, and the 19 November ruling has the animals backend stop storing the outstanding items the message was read from (c-418).

requirements.statement: A live animals template holds the transit countries as answered on the set's own transit countries page, shows them on the template page in a card whose Change link changes them, and seeds them into a notification started from it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's template page offers a Change link for transit countries and its 'use template' seeds them, yet its template never saves them; the templates ruling says template mode captures the same data as a notification on the same pages, so the default holds them (c-318).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, a 'Submitted action required' notification can be amended, copied and deleted as a Submitted one can: 'Amend this notification' and the amend confirmation start its amendment (the backend's amend takes it to AMEND with the same snapshots), cancelling that amendment restores it to 'Submitted action required' with its submitted answers, Copy as new copies it into a new draft, and Delete soft-deletes it with a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event. Resubmitting the amendment records the status the outstanding items give at that moment.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the 16 November ruling withdraws the 'Submitted action required' status, so a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED like any other and already takes every one of these actions; nothing action-required is shown until the banner design is agreed (c-439).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, a 'Completed' notification can be copied (Copy as new makes a new draft from it) and deleted (soft delete, with a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event), but not amended: its view offers no 'Amend this notification', and amend for it is refused like any other status that cannot be amended.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Copy as new and Delete, and no Amend, on a Completed notification. The 16 November ruling holds the status out until a real source of completion exists, and it arrives only once the authorities' outcomes reach the service, so the actions wait with it.
requirements.deltaNote: No Completed status exists today: the suite models four statuses (repo-tests-p6-052), and copy and soft delete accept only DRAFT, SUBMITTED and AMEND (repo-backend-p2-038, repo-backend-p3-034). Design Release 2.1 does not trace copying or deleting a Completed notification (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-104, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-119). Whether plants takes the status is decided when it unblocks (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-065).
requirements.blockedBy: A real source of completion must reach the notification record: the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sending post-submission outcomes, including completed, as req-1082 waits on. The 16 November ruling holds the status out until one exists (ruling-sam-2026-11-16-p1-017).

requirements.why: Nothing in this area's working set supports it any more: the plants ledger claim on plants' synchronous submit left this area in the re-extraction and recorded-decisions-plants now carries it. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve; the GBN-AG events and PIMS route this area records are the animals backend's, and plants publishing needs trade-imports-plants-backend, which is not one of the programme's repos.

requirements.statement: Publishing plants notifications (an outbox, GBN-AG or another event, PIMS routing) and a plants backend mapper that carries every SI matter instead of only the reference number are not built in this programme.
requirements.why: Plants' ledger parks publishing (d-047), and it needs trade-imports-plants-backend, which is not one of the programme's repos.

requirements.statement: The plants journey keeps supplying coded values and its created and submitted times for management information and asks no question for it; 'time taken per notification' reads as created to submitted.

The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve, and Design Release 2.1 changes none of it.

requirements.statement: Which items the service navigation holds, and in what order, is weighed with the dashboard home rather than here: Dashboard, Templates, Address book, Manage account and Log out on every frontend, with Welsh labels. This area keeps each item's destination and its current-item rule.

requirements.statement: The Alpha phase banner itself, its grey tag, its wording 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.' and its Welsh twin on every page of every frontend, signed-out pages included, is weighed with the dashboard home rather than here. This area keeps only the feedback link's destination.
requirements.why: The banner already matches the target design and the earlier parity programme's built row on every frontend. The dashboard-home area already carries it in req-956, so it is recorded once.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-014, repo-insfrontend-p4-015 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-013 and p13-015 render the banner on every page, signed out as well as signed in.

requirements.statement: The plants set is mounted at /high-risk-plants, every plants link carries that prefix, and every plants page renders in the shared layout, loading one application stylesheet and one application script module. A notification's list sits at the set's base URL, a new notification is created at /notifications under it, a notification's overview at /notifications/<id> and each of its pages at /notifications/<id>/<slug>, and the journey can also be entered at /start. More than one set can run side by side, each under its own prefix; a request is answered by the set whose prefix is the longest match for its path, and its routes, guards and chrome resolve inside that set, while a path under no prefix takes the site-wide chrome. A set must mount at a path starting with a slash and must configure everything the platform requires of it, or it is refused at mount with the missing piece and the call that would supply it named. Where only one set is mounted, pages built outside a request still resolve to it. A page inside a set renders through the layout that set names, so a set can give its own pages different chrome.
requirements.why: This is how the shared chrome finds each set's home link, current item and error chrome, which the germinal-products set relies on when it is mounted beside live-animals. It already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p13-068 and p13-069 give the URLs under the mount, p13-080 to p13-084 the set resolution and its refusals, p13-057, p13-057-m1 and p13-058 the chrome a page takes, and repo-tests-p14-080 that the plants home is /high-risk-plants.

requirements.statement: The plants set's own engine and test wiring is not shared page chrome and no layout or sign-in row changes it: the shared kit beyond the save controls and the section caption is view-model building and route wiring rather than markup, a GOV.UK component can be rendered into a table cell with its text escaped, the shared paging helpers hold no page size, and every page of a notification carries that notification's overview link and version token.
requirements.why: These claims sit in this area's slice of the plants frontend but describe the journey engine, its data and its tests. The journey-flow, consignment-parties and plants rows weigh them where a row changes them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p13-094 records that the shared kit is two macros and otherwise wiring, p13-085 the table-cell component rendering, p13-072 that paging holds no page size and p13-061 the per-page overview link and token.

requirements.statement: Typing or pasting the whole CPH number into County, as 123456789, 12/345/6789 or 12 345 6789, keeps every digit, and on save the server splits it into County, Parish and Holding when those two are empty. Focus never moves on its own. It works the same with or without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Typing the nine digits straight through used to keep only '12'. Sam ruled on 20 October: three labelled boxes as drawn, no cursor jump, and the whole number kept when typed or pasted in one go. The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page has the field accept up to 11 characters, so a slash-separated number typed in one go is accepted too. Moving focus while someone types fails WCAG 3.2.2 unless users are told first, and GOV.UK forms do not do it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-011 splits a whole nine-digit number typed or pasted into County alone, with or without slashes, when the page is saved; repo-frontend-p16-010 keeps the page free of JavaScript so nothing moves focus; repo-tests-p1-164 and repo-tests-p1-165 prove the keep, the focus and the save with and without JavaScript.

requirements.statement: A missing country of origin on the animals origin page is refused with 'Select a country of origin', in the error summary and inline against the country control, which is its own message and not the one a country outside the list gets.
requirements.why: The V4 data page makes the country of origin mandatory to proceed but gives no message for a missing one, and Design Release 2.1 writes none, so the wording is the service's own; the animals frontend already words it this way and nothing higher-ranked contradicts it (c-320).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-013 holds 'Select a country of origin' for a blank country and repo-frontend-p8-014 the separate 'Select a country from the list' for one outside the list; repo-tests-p1-034 proves the blank-country message end to end.

requirements.statement: On the origin page, in the live-animals and germinal products sets and in the high-risk plants frontend, Save and return to overview makes exactly the checks Save and continue makes: a country of origin that is one of the listed countries, a region of origin code when the answer is Yes, a code of five characters or fewer and an internal reference of 58 characters or fewer. A failure keeps the trader on the page with an error for each answer that is missing or not valid and what they entered still shown; with nothing missing or invalid the answers are saved and the overview is shown.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling, the most authoritative source on Save and return: the two save buttons behave the same way and no page is an exception. The checks are the page's own, so a blank answer to the region of origin code requirement is not refused: the V4 data page makes that field mandatory to submit rather than mandatory to proceed. The germinal products set takes it because each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals twin, which settles the set scope the ruling leaves open.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals origin page carries no Save and return to overview at all today (repo-frontend-p8-043), so the button and its checks arrive together with req-051. In plants the button already saves the country through the page's own checks and refuses a blank or barred country with HTTP 400, saving nothing (repo-plantsfrontend-p5-017, repo-plantsfrontend-p5-021-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p5-049-m1), so the loosening once planned for plants' pages with an exit to the overview is withdrawn.
requirements.blockedBy: The EUDPA-774 save and continue work merges to the animals frontend's main, which the 10 November ruling makes the condition for the return links; the plants half needs nothing.

requirements.statement: A notification holds its origin answers at notification level: the country of origin as a single choice from the country list (for example France), whether a region of origin code is required as Yes or No (for example No), the region of origin code, and the internal reference number (for example Imports456_GB), in the live animals and the germinal products journeys alike. The region of origin code requirement and the internal reference are the trader's own answers, drawn from no reference list.
requirements.why: The V4 data page specifies each origin field's level and type and marks each as impacting both journeys, and the real record already holds them that way, which is what lets one origin page carry all four answers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-055 shows the five answers the page collects and repo-frontend-p8-056 each bound to its own obligation on the notification, with repo-frontend-p8-045 showing them all offered back when the page is reopened.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's origin page asks for and records the same four origin answers as the live-animals set: the country of origin, whether a region of origin code is required, the region of origin code and the internal reference number.
requirements.why: Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences, and the data page's germinal section names only the county parish holding number and the permanent address as not required for germinal products, saying nothing about the origin page's fields, so the germinal origin page asks what the live-animals origin page asks.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products set exists in the animals frontend today.

requirements.statement: The region of origin code on the origin page is chosen from the regions the reference data service serves for the chosen country.
requirements.why: The V4 data page gives the region of origin code a source of MDM, which reads either as the country prefix coming from MDM's country list or as a list of regions the trader picks from; the two build different things and nothing ranks them.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the trader types the part after the fixed country prefix and no region list is read anywhere (repo-frontend-p8-020, repo-frontend-p8-031).

requirements.why: Plants keeps its own journey and start under the afternoon ruling's mirror rule, and it has no notification type question, so the animals back-link change does not reach it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p5-019 and repo-plantsfrontend-p5-020 show both destinations, and repo-plantsfrontend-p5-057-m1 that a refusal keeps the trail.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: a high-risk plants eligibility checker, a before-you-start page, and the GOV.UK guidance links a plants start section would carry.
requirements.why: The plants frontend parks its own start section, and Design Release 2.1 has no plants start page: this programme's start work is the notification type question in the INS front door and each set's own notification list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p14-063 shows a plants notification started from the type question opening straight at the commodity type page, with no start section before it.

requirements.statement: The commodity page's commodity, type and species lists come from MDM through trade-imports-reference-data, so what the commodity search offers is whatever MDM serves.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals data fields page names MDM as the source of the commodity, type and species values, and ruling 2026-10-09 makes a reference list's content MDM's to change rather than something edited in code.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals frontend answers the search from the set's own commodity list, a stub in the fit environment (repo-frontend-p9-079, -p9-093), and trade-imports-reference-data serves no commodities or species list at all (repo-referencedata-p1-089); repo-tests-p1-117 and -p1-130 check the search against that list's own answers and copy its fixture (c-377).
requirements.blockedBy: MDM serves the commodity, type and species lists and trade-imports-reference-data passes them to the animals frontend; the commodity catalogue area is re-distilled once it does (ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon, point on MDM commodities).

requirements.statement: Where a type applies to the chosen commodity, the commodity page offers that commodity's types from MDM's type list and narrows the species on offer to the type the trader picks, and records that type against the commodity line; an example type is Game.

The page names no commodity that carries a type and says nothing about a commodity that carries none, so which commodities offer the question, and whether an answer is required where no type applies, are settled against MDM's own list when this area is re-distilled.
requirements.blockedBy: MDM serves the commodity types and which commodities carry them, through trade-imports-reference-data; the commodity catalogue area is re-distilled once it does (ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon, point on MDM commodities).

requirements.statement: A number of animals above 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 is refused with an error naming that figure on that species' number of animals field, and the service that stores the count holds a whole number that large.
requirements.why: The data fields page caps the number of animals at that whole number and the data dictionary decides a field's limits, so the real service must accept every count the specification allows and refuse only what it cannot store.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a number of animals above 2,147,483,647 is refused with 'Number of animals must be 2,147,483,647 or fewer' and exactly 2,147,483,647 is accepted, because that is the largest whole number the service storing it holds (repo-frontend-p10-045, -p10-045-m1, -p10-046, repo-tests-p1-081, -p1-082).

requirements.statement: A number of packages above the largest whole number the notification stores is refused with an error naming that figure on that species' number of packages field, and no cap of 10 packages is enforced.
requirements.why: The data fields page types the live-animal number of packages 'numeric - max 10' while giving 25 and 5000 as its own examples, so whether 10 limits the digits or the packages is unsettled; refusing only what cannot be stored keeps an example the specification itself gives savable, and the figure the service stores is ten digits long.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-048 refuses a number of packages above 2,147,483,647 with 'Number of packages must be 2,147,483,647 or fewer', which repo-frontend-p10-046 gives as the largest whole number the storing service holds and which is ten digits long; nothing in the end-to-end suite asserts that upper limit yet (repo-tests-p1-089).

requirements.statement: The commodity page accepts every species a commodity offers, with no maximum on how many a trader chooses and no cap on how many commodity lines a notification holds.
requirements.why: The data fields page says a trader may select one or more species up to the agreed maximum but never gives the number, so nothing says what to enforce; keeping today's behaviour refuses nobody while the number is missing.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-036 builds a selection up across searches, -p10-161 records that nothing on either page limits how many commodity lines a notification may hold, and repo-tests-p1-131 that nothing asserts any limit on how many commodities may be chosen.

requirements.statement: On Commodity details the number of animals and the number of packages are each asked once for every chosen species, in that species' own block.
requirements.why: The data fields page puts both fields at commodity level, which reads either as one count per commodity covering all its species or as one count per commodity line; the real service's commodity line is one commodity plus one species and each line's species travels downstream on its own, so a count per species is what the default keeps.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-088 posts one numberOfAnimalsQuantity and numberOfPackages pair per commodity line and -p1-075-m1 finds each species' pair under its own level-three heading, and repo-frontend-p10-037 and -p10-039 ask both fields of every species line.

requirements.statement: On the high-risk plants commodity type page 'Save and return to overview' makes the same checks as 'Save and continue': with nothing chosen, or a type the service does not offer, it shows 'Select what you are importing' in the error summary and inline and keeps the trader on the page, saving nothing and leaving the commodity lines already saved untouched; with a type chosen it saves the answer and goes to the notification overview.
requirements.why: Ruling 26 October makes the two save buttons behave the same on every page that has both, in live animals and in high-risk plants, with no page an exception. The commodity type page is the one page in this area that has both buttons; the plants commodities list and the per-line Commodity details page offer 'Save and continue' alone, so the rule does not reach them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p3-047-m1 shows 'Save and return to overview' already refusing a blank or unoffered answer at 400 with 'Select what you are importing' in the summary and beside the options, saving nothing and leaving the saved lines alone, and -p3-047 the valid save opening the overview.

requirements.statement: The unweaned question is also asked when at least one selected commodity is a pig, sheep or goat.
requirements.why: The policy page names equines, cattle, pigs, sheep and goats as the commodities the unweaned rule covers, and it outranks the prototype, which names cattle and pig only. Pigs, sheep and goats are the three of the five that today's live-animal catalogue does not hold, so they are asked once the catalogue does.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's live-animal catalogue holds five commodities and none of them is a pig, sheep or goat (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-025), and the page's unweaned list reaches bovines and equines only (repo-frontend-p8-130), so no consignment can reach this rule yet.
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities come from MDM: the live-animal catalogue that adds pigs, sheep and goats is blocked on the MDM commodity integration, for which the 9 October afternoon ruling names no owner, ticket or date (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-030-m1). This area is re-distilled once it lands.

requirements.statement: A notification cannot be submitted without a main import reason, the follow-up answers that reason calls for, and what the animals are certified for; where the unweaned question is asked, the unweaned answer is needed too. Each one still missing is reported when the trader tries to submit, not when they leave the page.
requirements.why: The policy page marks the reason field block, the internal market purpose, the destination country, the port of exit, the exit date, the certified-for answer and the unweaned answer as mandatory to submit, and says the conditional fields a reason brings in must be completed before the notification can be submitted, while the trader may still move past the pages without them.
requirements.deltaNote: The import reason page already weighs each of its five answers, and the additional details page each of its two, against that answer's own obligation (repo-frontend-p8-121, repo-frontend-p8-143), but no today source in this area shows the submission check itself; the review and declaration area owns that check, and this names which of this area's answers it must require.

requirements.statement: The exit date field accepts a typed day/month/year date with a four-digit year and with or without a leading zero on the day or month, and its hint reads 'For example, 27/3/2026'.
requirements.why: The policy page is the authority on a field's format and example and gives DD/MM/YYYY with the example 27/03/2026, while the target design and the real service accept one or two digits for the day and month and show the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026'. The accepted MOJ date picker itself fills the field without leading zeros, so the stricter reading cannot be met by the component the page uses.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is typed as day/month/year text, the picker fills it without leading zeros (trace-animals-fit-p7-041) and the hint reads 'For example, 27/3/2026' (trace-animals-fit-p7-038, trace-e2e-p4-109); the re-extracted page takes its hint from the service's shared date example (repo-frontend-p8-096). Under the stricter reading the hint example and the accepted form both change.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, choosing Transit on the main import reason reveals the same two selects as the live-animals set, in the same order, 'Port of exit' then 'Destination country': the same lists, the same 'Select one' placeholder, the same labels with no hint, and the same 'Select a port of exit' and 'Select a destination country' messages when either is missing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's germinal reason page offers Transit, and its Transit reveal holds the same exit port and destination country selects as live animals, with the same hint about moving through Great Britain via different entry and exit ports. The prototype decides which questions are asked of which goods, and each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals twin plus the prototype's germinal differences, so a germinal Transit notification captures both.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set has no exit date question, and no germinal page asks when the consignment leaves Great Britain.
requirements.why: The only main import reasons the germinal set offers are Internal market and Transit, and neither asks for an exit date, while the copy rule would otherwise carry the live-animals exit date page across; the data page's germinal section names only the county parish holding number and the permanent address as not required for germinal products and says nothing about an exit date. The two readings build different germinal journeys and nothing ranks them.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today.

requirements.statement: Each identifier belongs to one animal: the page holds a set of identifier values per animal, not one set for the commodity line or for the notification.
requirements.why: V4 applies every animal identifier at unit level, so the trader is asked to identify each animal in turn rather than the line as a whole.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-107 and repo-frontend-p10-112 show one row per animal with its own identifier values, numbered from one in the order they were saved, and repo-frontend-p10-154 that each line's records are stored under that line.

requirements.statement: Every identifier value comes from the trader: the fields start empty and none is filled in from another system.
requirements.why: V4 names the user as the source of every animal identifier, so no identifier is looked up or prefilled.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-100 shows a fresh card's identifier fields blank and repo-tests-p1-136 the ear tag and passport empty when the page opens.

requirements.statement: A species panel shows only the identifier fields its commodity requires; a field for an identifier the commodity does not require is absent from the page, not hidden.
requirements.why: V4 makes each identifier conditional on the selected commodity requiring it, which is also how the real service and DR2.1 build the panel.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-090 builds a card's fields from the commodity code's declared identifiers filtered by what applies to the species, and repo-frontend-p10-096 and repo-frontend-p10-097 show a pet line and a pig line asked for those fields and nothing else.

requirements.statement: A species may be asked for more than one kind of identifier at once, and no rule limits how many of them one animal's record holds.
requirements.why: V4's identifier commodity lists overlap, so one commodity can require a passport, a tattoo and an ear tag together, and the page sets no upper bound on how many a trader fills in.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-093 shows a cattle line asked for three identifiers at once, repo-frontend-p10-109 a column for each of them, and repo-frontend-p10-144 that an animal may be saved on one of them alone with no upper bound on how many are filled in.

requirements.statement: Which identifier fields a species panel shows follows the species, not the commodity code alone, so two species sharing a code can be asked for different identifiers: on 0101 a horse panel asks for a horse name while a donkey, pony, zebra or mule panel does not.
requirements.why: The policy page's identifier commodity lists name a species beside each code, and code 0101 appears five times in the passport list but once in the horse name list, so a panel built on the code alone would ask the wrong questions.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-095 shows a donkey line on the same commodity code as a horse asked for a microchip and a passport but not a horse name, and repo-frontend-p10-090 that a card's fields are the code's declared identifiers filtered by what applies to that species.

requirements.statement: A 'Passport' identifier is asked for on every species whose commodity V4 names: 0101 donkeys and asses, horses, ponies, zebras, and mules, hinnies or other hybrids; 0102 cattle; and 01061900 cats, dogs and ferrets.
requirements.why: V4 is the specification of which commodities each identifier rule covers, and its passport list agrees with DR2.1 on every commodity today's catalogue holds.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-093 to repo-frontend-p10-096 and repo-tests-p1-153 show the passport asked on cattle, horses, donkeys, cats and dogs today; whether a ferret, pony, zebra or mule line is in the catalogue is unseen in this working set (trace-animals-fit-p10-089).

requirements.statement: An identifier value is free text: within its length limit any value is accepted, and no identifier has a format rule.
requirements.why: V4 types every animal identifier as a string with a maximum length and gives its example values as examples only, setting no pattern; the real service checks nothing but the length.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-125 makes length the only check on an identifier, repo-tests-p1-137 accepts an ear tag such as UK123456789012 with no error, and repo-frontend-p10-144 saves an animal on a free-text description alone.

requirements.statement: A species whose commodity requires none of passport, tattoo, ear tag or horse name is asked for 'Identification details', a 20-character-wide text input with a label and no hint, holding free text that identifies the animals.
requirements.why: V4 gives every commodity without a specific identifier type a free-text identifier, so a trader importing salmon, bees or poultry can still say what identifies the animals; V4 is the specification of which data a notification captures and outranks DR2.1, which asks nothing of such a species.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-091 and repo-frontend-p10-092 show the field offered for any commodity and labelled 'Identification details', repo-frontend-p10-099 its twenty-character width and absent hint, and repo-tests-p1-153 an ostrich line answering it end to end.

requirements.statement: The same species is asked for 'Description', a 20-character-wide text input with a label and no hint, holding a free-text description of the animals.
requirements.why: V4 pairs a description with the free-text identification details for a commodity with no specific identifier type, so the pair together identifies the animals.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-091 and repo-frontend-p10-092 show 'Description' offered beside 'Identification details' for any commodity, and repo-frontend-p10-099 its twenty-character width and absent hint.

requirements.statement: 'Identification details' and 'Description' are each limited to 58 characters, and a longer value shows 'Identification details must be 58 characters or less' or 'Description must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 types both free-text identifiers as strings of at most 58 characters, and DR2.1's wording for a length rule is used where a length rule is kept.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-125 applies the 58-character limit to every identifier and repo-frontend-p10-126 holds both messages.

requirements.statement: The page asks for no wing ring identifier.
requirements.why: V4's change log de-scoped the wing ring on 29 May 2026, and a de-scoped row outranks any source that still describes the field.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-092 and repo-tests-p1-134 list today's identifier labels, microchip, passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, identification details and description, with no wing ring.

requirements.statement: 'Microchip' is the first identifier a cat, dog or ferret panel (01061900) and a horse panel (0101) asks for.
requirements.why: DR2.1 and the real service both ask for a microchip first on these species. V4's six animal identifier fields leave the microchip out altogether, so whether the notification still captures one rests on the open question c-335.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-094 and repo-frontend-p10-096 show the microchip asked first on a horse line and a pet line today, and repo-frontend-p10-092 that 'Microchip' is one of the page's labels.

requirements.statement: A cattle panel (0102) asks for a 'Tattoo' identifier after 'Ear tag' and 'Passport'.
requirements.why: The policy page's tattoo commodity list names 0102 as well as the pets, and the 11 November ruling settles the point: the entries listed beat the list title's count, the policy page outranks every judgement on which commodities a rule covers, and the earlier removal of the tattoo from cattle is reversed. The tattoo goes last because that is where the target design puts it on the species that already ask for one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-093 shows a cattle line asked for an ear tag, then a passport, then a tattoo today.

requirements.statement: A pig panel (0103) asks for a 'Tattoo' identifier after its 'Ear tag'.
requirements.why: The policy page's tattoo commodity list names 0103 as well as the pets, and the 11 November ruling settles the point: the entries listed beat the list title's count of two, and naming the code 'Pigs' in the tattoo list and 'Pig (Domestic)' in the ear tag list is a label difference rather than a difference of scope. No source gives the tattoo a place in the pig panel's order, so it follows the ear tag, as the target design puts it last on every species that already asks for one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-097 shows a pig line asked for an ear tag and a tattoo today.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the identification page asks for none of the live-animal identifiers: it asks only for the germinal fields, donor name or ID, collection date, production date and identification number or mark.
requirements.why: The data page's germinal section defines the data elements that apply to germinal products only, every one of its fields impacts the germinal journey alone, and the county parish holding number and permanent address apply to the animal journey only; Design Release 2.1's germinal commodities carry no animal identifiers and its germinal identification panel asks only the four germinal fields, so the germinal set's copy of the page carries only those.

requirements.statement: On the identification page, 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' make the same checks: either button shows an error for each identifier that is not valid, the trader stays on the page and what they entered is kept. The germinal products set's copy of the page behaves the same way.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling: the two save buttons behave consistently and no page is an exception. Nothing on this page is mandatory to answer, so neither button asks for a missing identifier; only a value that is not valid, such as one over the length limit, raises an error. The germinal copy is taken from the live page, so it inherits the behaviour although the ruling names only live animals and plants.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-124 and repo-tests-p1-142 show Save and return to overview accepted with every identifier blank, and repo-frontend-p10-141-m1 that both buttons read the same cards, so the two already check the same things; no trace drives 'Save and return to overview' on this page (trace-animals-fit-p10-088, trace-animals-fit-p11-061).

requirements.statement: Pressing Enter in a field of a species panel that takes more than one animal saves that panel's current animal, as the panel's own save button does, and the trader stays on the page with what they entered kept.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling, which accepted the engineering review's recommendation on this behaviour, so a trader who types an animal's identifiers and presses Enter keeps the entry.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-118 and repo-tests-p1-144 show Enter in a card's identifier box saving that animal, keeping the trader on the page, moving the counter on and clearing the box; the traces were captured before the change, when Enter submitted the page through one hidden button at the top of the form (trace-animals-fit-p10-081).

requirements.statement: Pressing Enter in a field of a species panel that takes a single animal, or in a field outside any species panel, submits the page as 'Save and continue'.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling rules on Enter only in a panel for several animals, so what Enter does elsewhere on the page rests on the open question c-338; the default keeps what the service does today.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-140 shows Enter anywhere in the form behaving as the page's own Save and finish today.

requirements.statement: The 26 October ruling's decisions on other pages: the Identification details page saving a card when Enter is pressed in one of its fields, the Notification submitted page listing the ITAHC as still to upload, and which earlier conflicts the ruling replaces.
requirements.why: Weighed here and left out: the Identification details page belongs to the identification area, the Notification submitted page to the review-and-submit area, and the conflicts the ruling replaces to the journey-flow area that owns them. Recorded so the ruling's claims are weighed.

requirements.statement: How the data specification lays out each field, in eight headings: field name, type, conditions or values, the level it applies at, source, whether it is mandatory, an example, and the journeys it impacts.
requirements.why: Weighed here and left out: it describes how the source is written, not anything a user or another system can observe. This is the same judgement as req-2211, which now carries it; this id stays so that it still resolves.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, 'Save and return to overview' makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue' on every page that shows both buttons, the set's own Commodity details and Identification details pages included: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error in the summary and inline for each one and what they entered kept, and with nothing missing or invalid the answers are saved and the overview is shown.
requirements.why: The two save buttons behaving alike, with no page an exception, is what the owner decided; a trader who saves and returns otherwise leaves a page holding answers the service has not checked, and the germinal-only weight, package, length and date rules would be made by one button and not the other. The 26 October ruling's 'no page is an exception' and the 9 October ruling's copy rule between them carry the rule into this set, which c-339 settles.

requirements.statement: A notification cannot be submitted until all five arrival answers are given: the arrival date at the port of entry, the port of entry, the means of transport, the transport identification and the transport document reference.
requirements.why: The data dictionary marks the means of transport mandatory to proceed and the other four mandatory to submit, so a trader may move through the journey with four of them blank but cannot submit without them; where the dictionary sets a field's level and whether it is mandatory, it decides those and the prototype decides how the field reads.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-038 declares all five mandatory for a notification whatever the page lets a trader save part-way, p11-039 binds each to its own obligation, and repo-tests-p1-101 and p1-104 show the overview task reading Complete only once all five are saved.

requirements.statement: A notification captures nothing about how the consignment travels on from the border control post: neither arrival details nor any other page in the arrival step asks for it.
requirements.why: The data dictionary's out-of-scope table de-scoped the transport after BCP field on 14 May 2026, and a de-scoped row outranks any source that still describes the field.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-006 shows arrival details collecting the five arrival answers only, with no onward-transport question, and p11-052 shows nothing beyond them in the template, the validation or the copy.

requirements.statement: The arrival and transit answers are asked of the trader once for the whole notification: one arrival date, one port of entry, one means of transport, one transport identification, one transport document reference and one list of transit countries, however many commodity lines or animals the notification holds.
requirements.why: The data dictionary puts each of these fields at notification level and gives the user as its source for all but the port of entry's list of values, so the questions are asked once and not repeated per line or per animal. It marks each of them as impacting the germinals journey as well as the animals one, so the same holds in both animals sets.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-006 and p11-037 show one set of five answers collected on one page, p11-080 the one transit list, and p11-039 each bound to the notification's own obligation.

requirements.statement: The germinal-products set asks the same arrival questions as the live-animals set: its arrival details page asks the same five questions in the same wording and order with the same rules, and its transit countries page asks the same question, appearing only when the means of transport is rail or road.
requirements.why: Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences, the data page's germinal section names only the county parish holding number and the permanent address as not required for germinal products and says nothing about the arrival, transport or transited-countries fields, and the prototype decides which questions are asked of which goods. Design Release 2.1's germinal journey moves goods through Great Britain under Transit and asks for transit countries, which c-344 settles.

requirements.statement: Each arrival and transit field's hint shows a worked example: 'Port of Hull' for the port of entry, 12/12/2026 for the arrival date, 'Road Vehicle' for the means of transport, FR-892-LK for the transport identification, CMR-2026-884721 for the transport document reference, and France with Belgium for the transit countries.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the goal is look and feel. The data dictionary gives these as illustrations of each field's format in the specification, not as service copy; Design Release 2.1 and the real service show a worked example only in the arrival date hint, and there it has to be a date the arrival window accepts. The remaining examples are already the tests repo's data.

requirements.statement: In the plants frontend the journey asks which plant health authority a notification goes to and derives the region from the place-of-destination address.
requirements.why: Out of scope: plants parked competent-authority routing because the routing, access parity and region derivation are backend work the plants backend cannot yet do, and this programme's repos do not include it. What the place of destination question says about a spot check is plants' own wording, which no row of this programme changes, and the confirmation page belongs to another area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p8-020 shows every version of the destination question promising only that a plant health inspector may carry out a spot check; no claim in this working set records the journey asking which authority the notification goes to or deriving a region.
